I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: "A man prayed Fajr when the dawn appeared."
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.36 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.274 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.274 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.304 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.208

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «وَقْتُ صَلاَةِ ٱلْغَدَاةِ مَا بَيْنَ طُلُوعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ إلَى طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ».
english_text:
Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far {a.s} said: "The time of the morning prayer is between the rising of the dawn
and the rising of the sun."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.36 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.38 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.275 • Al- Wafi, Vol.7 p.305 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.208

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدِ عَنِ الْحُصَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْحُصَيْنِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ اِخْتَلَفَ مَوَالِيكَ فِي صَلَاَةِ الْفَجْرِ قَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُصَلِّي إِذَا طَلَعَ ٱلْفَجْرُ الْأَوَلُ الْمُسْتَطِيلُ فِي
السَّمَاءِ وَ مِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُصَلِّي إِذَا اِعْتَرَضَ فِي أَسْفَلِ الْأَرْضِ وَ اِسْتَبَانَ وَ لَسْتُ أَعْرِفُ أَفْضَلَ الْوَقْتَيْنِ فَأْصَلِّيَ فِيهِ فَإِنْ
رَأَيْتَ يَا مَوْلَايَ جَعَلَنِي اللَّهُ فِدَاكَ أَنْ تُعَلَّمَنِي أَفْضَلَ الْوَقْتَيْنِ وَ تَحُدَّ لِي كَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ مَعَ الْقَمَرِ وَ الْفَجْرُ لا يَتَبَيَّنْ
حَتَّى يَحْمَرَّ وَ يُصْبِحَ وَ كَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ مَعَ الْقَمَرِ وَ مَا حَدْ ذَلِكَ فِي السَّفَرِ وَ الْحَضَرِ فَعَلْتُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ فَكَتَبَ بِخَطَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «الْفَجْرُ يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ وَ لَيْسَ هُوَ الْأَبْيَضَ صُعَداً وَ لاَ تُصَلِّ فِي سَفَرٍ وَ لاَ فِي حَضَرٍ
حَتَى تَتَبَيَّنَهُ رَجِمَكَ اللهُ فَإِنّ اللّهَ لَمْ يَجْعَلْ خَلْقَهُ فِي شُبْهَةٍ مِنْ هَذَا - فَقَالَ تَعَالَى «كُلُوا وَ اِشرَبُوا حَتّى يَتَبَيَّنَ
لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ» فَالْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ هُوَ الْفَجْرُ الْذِي يَحْرُمُ بِهِ الْأَكْلُ وَ الشُّرْبُ فِي
الصِّيَامٍ وَ كَذَلِكَ هُوَ الّذِي يُوجِبُ الصَّلاَةَ».
english_text:
Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Husayn,
who said:
I wrote to Abu Ja’far {a.s}; “May I be your ransom, your followers have differed regarding
the time of the Fajr prayer. Some of them pray when the first, vertical dawn appears in
the sky, and some of them pray when it spreads horizontally at the lower part of the
horizon and becomes clear. I do not know which of the two times is better, so I may
pray at that time. If you would, O my master, may Allah {SWT} make me your ransom,
teach me which of the two times is better, and set for me a standard regarding what I
should do when the moon is present and the Fajr is not clearly visible until it reddens
and brightens. And how should I act concerning the moon? And what is the limit of that
in both travel and residence? May you do so, if Allah {SWT} wills.”
So He {a.s} wrote back in his own handwriting (peace be upon him):
"The Fajr, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on you, is the white thread, and it is not the
whiteness that rises upward. Do not pray, in travel or in residence, until it becomes
clearly distinguishable. May Allah {SWT} have mercy on you.
Indeed, Allah {SWT} has not placed His {SWT} creation in confusion regarding this matter.
He {SWT}, the Exalted, said: ‘'Eat and drink until the white thread becomes clear to you
from the black thread of the dawn'‘ (Surah Baqarah 2:187), the white thread is the Fajr
which makes eating and drinking prohibited in fasting, and likewise it is the one that
makes prayer obligatory."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Jawad {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.36 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.274 • Awalim Al-Uloom, Vol.2 3 p.381

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَرَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرِّحْمَنِ بْنِ سَالِمِ عَنْ إسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ
لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ أَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ أَفْضَلِ الْمَوَاقِيتِ فِي صَلاَةِ الْفَجْرِ قَالَ «مَعَ طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى
يَقُولُ «إِنَّ قُرْآنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشُهُوداً » يَعْنِي صَلاَةَ الْفَجْرِ يَشهَدُهُ مَلاَئِكَةُ ٱللَّيْلِ وَ مَلائِكَةُ النَّهَارِ فَإِذَا صَلَّى الْعَبْدُ
صَلاةَ الصُّبْحِ مَعَ طُلُوعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ أَثْبِتَ لَهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ تُثُبِتُهُ مَلاَئِكَةُ ٱللَّيْلِ وَ مَلاَئِكَةُ النَّهَارِ».
english_text:
Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abd al-Rahman ibn
Salim from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: "Inform me about the best time for the Fajr prayer."
Imam {a.s} said: "At the time of the rising of the dawn. Indeed, Allah {SWT}, the Exalted,
says: ‘'Indeed, the recitation of Fajr is witnessed'‘ (Surah Isra 17:78), meaning the Fajr
prayer is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day. So when the
servant performs the morning prayer at the time of the rising of the dawn, it is recorded
for him twice, the angels of the night record it and the angels of the day record it."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.282 • Thawab Al-A’mal wa ‘Iqab Al-A’mal, Vol.1 p.36 • ‘Ilal Al-Shara’i’, Vol.2 p.336 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.37 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.275 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.304 • Tafsir Al-Safi, Vol.3 p.210 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.212 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.3 p.567 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.5 p.321

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ ٱلْهُذَيْلِ
عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْمَاضِي عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ وَقْتٍ صَلاةِ ٱلْفَجْرِ فَقَالَ «جِينَ يَعْتَرِضُ ٱلْفَجْرُ فَتَرَاهُ مِثلَ
نَهَرِ سُورَاءَ».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn from
Fadalah from Hisham ibn al-Hudhayl from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the time of the Fajr prayer, and Imam {a.s} said:
"When the dawn spreads horizontally, and you see it like a stream of light across the
horizon."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.37 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.275 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.303 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.212

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
عَلِيْ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: «الصُبْحُ هُوَ
الَّذِي إِذَا رَأْيْتَهُ مُعْتَرِضاً كَأَنَّهُ بَيَاضُ سُورَاءَ».
فأما الحديث المقدم ذكره وهو حديث زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال : وقت صلاة الغداة ما بين طلوع الفجر الى
طلوع الشمس, وما رواه:
english_text:
Narrated by Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Ali ibn ‘Atiyyah:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "The Subh (morning) is that which, when you see it spreading
horizontally, it is as if it were the whiteness of a stream."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
As for the previously mentioned narration, which is the hadith of Zurarah from Abu
Ja’far {a.s}, who said: "The time of the morning prayer is between the rising of the dawn
and the rising of the sun", and what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.37

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَ مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أُبِي الْخَطَّابِ وَ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ
عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ الْمُفَضَّلِ بْنِ صَالِحِ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ طَرِيفِ عَنِ ٱلْأَصْبَعِ بْنِ نُبَاتَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ : «مَنْ أَذرَكَ مِنَ الْغَدَاةِ رَكْعَةً قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ فَقَدْ أَدْرَكَ الْغَدَاةَ تَامَّةً».
فالمراد بهذه الاخبار صاحب الاعذار والحوائج حسب ما ذكرناه في غيره من الصلوات, والذي يدل على ذلك ما رواه:
english_text:
And what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and Abdullah
ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Amr ibn Uthman from Abu Jamilah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Sa’d ibn Tarif
from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said:
Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s}) said:
"Whoever catches a rak’ah of the morning prayer before the rising of the sun has
caught the full morning prayer."
source: Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib al-Murtadha {a.s}
commentary:
So the intended meaning of these narrations is (concerning) the one who has excuses
and pressing needs, just as we have mentioned regarding other prayers. What
indicates this is what has been narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.38 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.275 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.308 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.217 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.69

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقٍ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ
عَمَّارٍ بْنِ مُوسَى السَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «فِي الرَجُلِ إِذَا غَلَبَثْهُ عَيْنُهُ أَوْ عَاقَهُ أَمْرٌ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ
الْمَكْثُوبَةَ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ مَا بَيْنَ أَنْ يَطْلُعَ الْفَجْرُ إِلَى أَنْ تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ وَ ذَلِكَ فِي الْمَكْثُوبَةِ خَاصَّةً فَإِنْ صَلَّى رَكْعَةَ مِنَ
اَلْغَدَاةِ ثُمَّ طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَلْيُتِمَّ وَ قَدْ جَازَتْ صَلاَتُهُ».
english_text:
Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq
ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "Regarding a man who is overcome by sleep or hindered by
something from performing the obligatory Fajr prayer, (he may pray it) between the
rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun, and that is specific to the obligatory prayer.
So if he performs one rak’ah of the morning prayer and then the sun rises, he should
complete (the prayer), and his prayer is valid."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.38 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.276 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.305

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَرَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَادٍ عَنِ ٱلْحَلَبِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ آَللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «وَقْتُ ٱلْفَجْرِ جِينَ يَنْشَقُ ٱلْفَجْرُ إِلَى أَنْ يَتَجَلَّلَ الصُّبْحُ ٱلسَّمَاءَ وَ لاَ يَنْبَغِي تَأْخِيرُ ذَلِكَ عَمْداً لَكِنَّهُ
وَقْتُ لِمَنْ شُغْلَ أَوْ نَسِيَ أَوْ نَامَ».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad
from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "The time of Fajr is from when the dawn splits until the morning
light covers the sky. It is not appropriate to delay it deliberately, but it is a valid time for
one who is preoccupied, forgets, or sleeps."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.283 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.38 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.276 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.304 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.207

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَ رَوَى الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ النَّضْرِ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرِ ٱلْمَكْفُوفِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلامُ - عَنِ الصَّائِمِ مَتَى يَحْرُمُ عَلَيْهِ الطَّعَامُ فَقَالَ «إِذَا كَانَ الْفَجْرُ كَالْقُبْطِيَّةِ الْبَيْضَاءِ » قُلْتُ فَمَتَى تَجِلُّ الصَّلاَةُ
فَقَالَ «إِذَا كَانَ كَذَلِكَ» فَقُلْتُ أَلَسْتُ فِي وَقْتٍ مِنْ تِلْكَ السَاعَةِ إِلَى أَنْ تَطْلعَ الشَّمْسُ فَقَالَ «لا إِنَّمَا نَعْدُهَا صَلاَةَ
الصِّبْيَانِ» ثُمَّ قَالَ «إِنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ يُحْمَدُ الرَّجُلُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ ثُمَّ يَرْجِعَ فَيُنَبَّهَ أَهْلَهُ وَ صِبْيَانَهُ».
english_text:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr from ‘Asim ibn Humayd from Abu Basir al-Makfuf, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about the fasting person; when does food become forbidden
for him?
Imam {a.s} said: "When the dawn is like the white Coptic garment."
I asked: "Then when does the prayer become permissible?"
Imam {a.s} said: "When it is like that."
I asked: "Am I not within the time (of prayer) from that moment until the sun rises?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No, we only count that as the prayer of children."
Then Imam {a.s} said: "Indeed, it was not commendable for a man to pray in the mosque
and then return to wake up his family and children"
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.39 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.276 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.306 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.213

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَرَوَى ٱلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ ٱلنَّضْرِ وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لِكُلَ صَلاةٍ وَقْتَانٍ
وَ أَوْلُ آلْوَقْتَيْنِ أَفْضَلُهُمَا وَقْتُ صَلاَةِ ٱلْفَجْرِ جِينَ يَنْشَقُ ٱلْفَجْرُ إِلَى أَنْ يَتَجَلَّلَ الصُّبْحُ السِّمَاءَ وَ لا يَنْبَغِي تَأْجِيرُ
ذَلِكَ عَمْداً لَكِنَّهُ وَقْتُ مَنْ شُغِلَ أَوْ نَسِيَ أَوْ سَهَا أَوْ نَامَ وَ وَقْتُ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ جِينَ تَجِبُ الشَّمْسُ إِلَى أَنْ تَشْتَبِكَ النُجُومُ
وَلَيْسَ لِأَحَدٍ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ آخِرَ ٱلْوَقْتَيْنِ وَقْتاً إلاَّ مِنْ عُذْرٍ أَوْ عِلَّةِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : (ولكل صلاة من الفرائض الخمس وقتان أول وآخر فالاول لمن لا عذر له والثاني لاصحاب الاعذار,
ولا ينبغي لاحد أن يؤخر الصلاة عن أول وقتها وهو ذاكر لها غير ممنوع منها فان أخرها ثم اخترم في الوقت قبل أن
يؤديها كان مضيعا لها, وان بقي حتى يؤديها في آخر الوقت أو فيما بين الاول والآخر عفي عن ذنبه في تأخيرها). قد بينا
فيما تقدم ان آخر الوقت وقت لصاحب العذر والحاجة, وان من لا عذر له فوقته أول الوقت, ويؤكد ذلك أيضا ما رواه:
english_text:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr and Fadalah from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "For every prayer there are two times, and the first of the two is
the better. The time of the Fajr prayer is from the moment the dawn splits until the
morning light covers the sky, and it is not appropriate to delay that deliberately, but it
is the time for one who is preoccupied, forgets, is heedless, or sleeps. And the time of
Maghrib is from the setting of the sun until the stars become interwoven. And no one
should make the latter of the two times their time (of prayer), except due to an excuse
or a valid reason."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said:
"And every one of the five obligatory prayers has two times: an initial time and a final
time. The first is for one who has no excuse, and the second is for those with excuses.
And it is not appropriate for anyone to delay the prayer beyond its initial time while
being mindful of it and not prevented from performing it. If he delays it and then dies
during the time before performing it, he has neglected it. But if he remains until he
performs it at the end of the time or between the first and the last time, he is excused
for the delay."
We have already clarified previously that the end of the time is for one who has an
excuse or a pressing need, and that one who has no excuse, his time is the beginning
of the time. What further confirms this is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.39 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.276 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.209 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.208

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ
قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «لِكُلَ صَلاةٍ وَقْتَانِ وَ أَوَّلُ ٱلْوَقْتِ أَفْضَلُهُ وَ لَيْسَ لِأَحَدٍ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ آخِرَ
الْوَقْتَيْنِ وَقْتاً إِلاَّ فِي عُذْرٍ مِنْ غَيْرٍ عِلَّةٍ».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-
Rahman from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s} say: "For every prayer there are two times, and the beginning
of the time is the best of it. And it is not for anyone to make the latter of the two times
his (designated) time except in a case of excuse without (blameworthy) reason."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.274 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.39 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.244 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.68 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.205 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.122

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَرَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ
عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ أَو اِبْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : «لِكُلِّ صَلاةٍ وَقْتَانٍ وَ أَوّلُ الْوَقْتِ أَفْضَلُهُمَا».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-
Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar or Ibn Wahb, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "For every prayer there are two times, and the beginning of the
time is the better of the two."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.274 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.40 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.244 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.205 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.1 p.373 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.121 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.68

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبِ عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ : «لَفَضْلُ
الْوَقْتِ الْأَوَّلِ عَلَى ٱلْأَخِيرِ خَيْرٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ مِنْ وَلَدِهِ وَ مَالِهِ».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Bakr ibn Muhammad, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "The superiority of the first time (of prayer) over the last is better
for the believer than his children and his wealth."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Qurb Al-Isnad, Vol.1 p.43 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.217 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.40 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, Vol.1 p.301 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.207 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.80 p.12

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَ رَوَى الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَدَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلَاَمْ
أَصْلَحَكَ اللَّهُ وَقْتُ كُلِّ صَلَاَةٍ أَوَّلُ الْوَقْتِ أَفْضَلُ أَوْ وَسَطُهُ أَوْ آخِرُهُ فَقَالَ «أَوَّلُهُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ
آلِه «إِنَّ اَللهَ يُحِبُّ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ مَا يُعَجَّلُ» ».
english_text:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far {a.s}: "May Allah {SWT} set you right, is the beginning of the time for each
prayer better, or the middle, or the end?"
Imam {a.s} said: "The beginning."
He {a.s} then said: “The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family,
said: ‘Indeed, Allah {SWT} loves from goodness that which is done promptly.’"
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.274 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.40 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.206 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.122

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَرَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبِ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ أَبِي خَلَفٍ عَنْ أَبِي
الْحَسَن مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «الصَّلَوَاتُ ٱلْمَفْرُوضَاتُ فِي أَوَّلِ وَقْتِهَا إِذَا أَقِيمَ حُدُودُهَا أَظيَبُ رِيحاً مِنْ قَضِيبِ
اَلْآسِ جِينَ يُوْخَذُ مِنْ شَجَرِهِ فِي طِيبِهِ وَ رِيحِهِ وَ طَرَاوَتِهِ فَعَلَيْكُمْ بِالْوَقْتِ الْأَوَّلِ».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub
from Sa’d ibn Abi Khalaf:
(Imam) Abu al-Hasan Musa {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
"The obligatory prayers, when performed at their initial time while fulfilling their proper
conditions, are more fragrant than the myrtle branch when it is freshly taken from its
tree in its fragrance, scent, and freshness. So adhere to the first time (of prayer)."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
references: Thawab Al-A’mal wa ‘Iqab Al-A’mal, Vol.1 p.36 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.40 • Mishkat Al- Anwar, Vol.1 p.73 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.207 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.118 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.80 p.18

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ سَلَمَةَ بْنِ الْخَطَابِ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ
قُتَيْبَةَ الْأَعْشَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: «إِنَّ فَضْلَ ٱلْوَقْتِ ٱلْأَوَّلِ عَلَى ٱلْأَخِيرِ كَفَضْلِ الآخِرَةِ عَلَى ٱلدُّنْيَا».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn
Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from his father from Qutaybah al-A’sha:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "Indeed, the superiority of the first time (of prayer) over the last
is like the superiority of the Hereafter over this world."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.274 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.40 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, Vol.1 p.301 • Falah Al-Sa’il, Vol.1 p.155 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.206 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.123 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.7 9 p.359 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.80 p.12 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.3 p.102 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.3 p.102

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلام : «إغْلَمْ أَنَّ أَوْلَ الْوَقْتِ أَبَداً أَفْضَلُ فَتَعَجَلِ الْخَيْرَ مَا اِسْتَطَعْتَ وَ أَحَبَّ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مَا دَامَ
اَلْعَبْدُ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ قَلَّ».
english_text:
Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ziyad
from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja’far {a.s} said: "Know that the beginning of the time is always better, so hasten
toward good as much as you are able. And the most beloved of deeds to Allah {SWT},
Mighty and Majestic, is that which the servant remains consistent upon, even if it is
little."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.274 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.41 • Al-Sarair, Vol.3 p.586 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.206 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.121 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.68 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.6 8 p.216 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.7 9 p.355 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.80 p.6

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُوبَ الْخَزَّازِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «إِذَا دَخَلَ وَقْتُ صَلاةٍ فُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُ السَّمَاءِ لِصُعُودِ ٱلْأَعْمَالِ فَمَا أُحِبُ أَنْ يَصْعَدَ عَمَلٌ أَوَّلُ
مِنْ عَمَلِي وَ لا يُكْتَبَ فِي الصِّجِيفَةِ أَحَدٌ أَوَّلُ مِنَّي».
english_text:
Narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from
Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s} say: "When the time of a prayer enters, the gates of the
heavens are opened for the ascent of deeds. So I do not wish that any deed ascends
before mine, nor that anyone's name is recorded in the scroll (of deeds) before mine."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.41 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.208 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.119

Chapter Title: TIMES OF PRAYER AND SIGN OF EACH OF ITS TIMES
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَهْلٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ رِبْعِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ قَالَ: «إِنَّا لَنُقَدَّمُ وَ نُؤَخِّرُ وَ لَيْسَ كَمَا يُقَالُ
مَنْ أَخْطَاً وَقْتَ الصَّلاَةِ فَقَدْ هَلَكَ وَ إِنَّمَا الرُّخْصَةُ لِلنَّاسِي وَ ٱلْمَرِيضِ وَ الْمُدْنِفِ وَ ٱلْمُسَافِرِ وَ النَّائِمِ فِي تَأْخِيرِهَا».
وليس لاحد أن يقول إن هذه الاخبار إنما تدل على ان اول الاوقات أفضل ولا تدل على انه يجب في أول الوقت لانه إذا
ثبت انها في أول الوقت أفضل ولم يكن هناك منع ولا عذر فانه يجب أن يفعل, ومتى لم يفعل والحال على ما وصفناه
ستحق اللوم والتعنيف, ولم يرد بالوجوب هاهنا ما يستحق بتركه العقاب لان الوجوب على ضروب عندنا, منها ما يستحق
بتركه العقاب, ومنها ما يكون الاولى فعله ولا يستحق الاخلال به العقاب وإن كان يستحق به ضرب من اللوم والعتب, ثم
ذكر الشيخ رحمه اللّه تفضيل الوقتين لكل صلاة الى آخر الباب وقد مضى شرح ذلك مستوفى.
٥ - باب القبلة
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : (والقبلة هي الكعبة) الى قوله : (ومن أراد معرفتها في باقي الليل فليجعل الجدي على منكبه الايمن
فانه يكون متوجها إليها). قال اللّٰه تعالى : (قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء فلنولينك قبلة ترضيها فول وجهك شطر
المسجد الحرام وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره) وقال : (ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وانه
للحق من ربك وما اللّٰه بغافل عما تعملون) وقال : (ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام وحيث ما كنتم
فولوا وجوهكم شطره) فأوجب اللّٰه تعالى بظاهر اللفظ التوجه نحو المسجد الحرام لمن نأى عن المسجد الحرام ، والمراد
بالشطر هاهنا النحو، قال هذيل: اقول لام زنباع أقري ، صدور العيس شطر بني تميم
وقال لفيط الايادي :فقد أظلكم من شطر ثغركم، هول له ظلم تغشا كم قطعا
english_text:
And from him, from Isma‘il ibn Sahl from Hammad from Rib‘i:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “Indeed, we advance and delay (the prayer), and it is not as
people say: ‘Whoever misses the time of prayer has perished.’ Rather, there is a
concession for the one who forgets, the sick person, the severely ill, the traveller, and
the one asleep, in delaying it.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
And no one has the right to say that these narrations merely indicate that the beginning
of the time is better, but do not indicate that it is obligatory (to pray) at the beginning
of the time, because when it has been established that the beginning of the time is
superior, and there is no barrier or excuse, then it becomes obligatory to act
accordingly. And whenever one does not act in such a case as we have described, he
deserves blame and reproach.
However, what is meant by "obligation" (wujub) here is not the type whose
abandonment incurs punishment, because obligation, according to us, is of various
kinds: among them is that whose abandonment brings about punishment, and among
them is that which is preferable to do but whose abandonment does not incur
punishment, even if it deserves a type of blame and reprimand.
Then the Shaykh, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, mentioned the preference of the
two time intervals for each prayer until the end of the chapter, and the explanation of
that has already been covered in full.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said:
"The qiblah is the Ka’bah," up to his statement: "And whoever wishes to determine its
direction during the rest of the night, let him place the constellation of al-Jady (Polaris)
on his right shoulder, for he will be facing it."
Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, said: ‘"Indeed We see the turning of your face toward the
heaven, so We shall surely turn you to a qiblah that pleases you. So turn your face
toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it."‘ (Surah
Baqarah 2:144)
And He {SWT} said: ‘"And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-
Haram, and indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And Allah {SWT} is not unaware of what
you do."‘ (Surah Baqarah 2:149)
And He {SWT} said: ‘"And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-
Haram. And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it."‘ (Surah Baqarah 2:150)
So Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, has obligated by the apparent meaning of these words the
facing of al-Masjid al-Haram for those who are far from it. The meaning of ‘shatr’ here
is "direction" or "toward."
Hudhail said: "I say to Umm Zunba’: Lead the breasts of the camels toward (shatr)
Banu Tamim."
And Lafit al-Ayadi said: "So a terror has overshadowed you from the direction (shatr)
of your frontier, A darkness that covers you with layers."
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.41 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.262 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.208 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.139

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
عَلِي بْنُ الْحَسَنِ الطَّاطَرِيّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ
قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَ «فَأُقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفا» قَالَ «أَمَرَهُ أَنْ يُقِيمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلْقِبْلَةِ لَيْسَ فِيهِ شَيْءَ
مِنْ عِبَادَةِ اَلْأَوْثَانِ خَالِصاً مُخْلِصاً».
english_text:
Narrated by Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir
from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the saying of Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic: ‘"So set your face
toward the religion, upright (hanifan)."‘ (Surah Rum 30:30)
Imam {a.s} said: "He {SWT} commanded him to direct his face toward the qiblah, with
nothing of idol worship in it, purely and sincerely (for Allah {SWT})."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.42 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.540 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.295 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.4 p.345 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 1 p.75 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.10 p.196

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
وَ عَنَهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اللَّهِ
عَزَّ وَ جَلّ «وَ أَقِيمُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ» قَالَ «هَذِهِ الْقِبْلَةُ أَيْضاً».
english_text:
Narrated from him from Ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the saying of Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic: ‘"And direct your
faces at every place of worship."‘ (Surah A'raf 7:29)
Imam {a.s} said: "This also refers to the qiblah."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tafsir Al-’Ayyashi, Vol.2 p.12 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.43 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.540 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.296 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.2 p.527 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.2 p.528 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 1 p.66 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 1 p.75 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.2 p.17 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.3 p.168

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
وَعَنْهُ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ ٱللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَتَى صُرِفَ رَسُولُ ٱللّهِ
صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ إِلَى ٱلْكَعْبَةِ فَقَالَ «بَعْدَ رُجُوعِهِ مِنْ بَدْرٍ».
english_text:
Narrated from him from Ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: "When was the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and
his family, turned toward the Ka’bah?"
Imam {a.s} said: "After his return from Badr."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.43 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.538 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.297 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.1 9 p.199

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ ٱلْحَلَبِيّ
عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ : فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى «وَ أَقِيمُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلَّ مَسْجِدٍ» قَالَ «مَسَاجِدُ مُحْدَثَةٌ فَأُمِرُوا
أَنْ يُقِيمُوا وُجُوهَهُمْ «شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ» ».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Abu Jamilah
from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} (was asked) regarding the saying of the Exalted: ‘"And direct your faces
at every place of worship,"‘ (Surah A'raf 7:29)
Imam {a.s} said: "Newly built mosques, so they were commanded to direct their faces
‘toward al-Masjid al-Haram’."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tafsir Al-’Ayyashi, Vol.2 p.12 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.43 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.540 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.296 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.2 p.528 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.2 p.528 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 1 p.66 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.2 p.18 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.3 p.168

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
الطَّاطَرِيّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: سَألْتُهُ عَنْ
قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى «وَ مَا جَعَلْنَا ٱلْقِبْلَةَ الَّتِي كُنْتَ عَلَيْهَا إِلا لِنَعْلَمَ مَنْ يَتَّبِعُ الرَسُولَ مِمَّنْ يَنْقَلِبُ عَلىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ» أَمَرَهُ بِهِ قَالَ
«نَعَمْ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ كَانَ يُقَلَّبُ وَجْهَهُ فِي السَّمَاءِ فَعَلِمَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَ مَا فِي نَفْسِهِ فَقَالَ «قَدْ
نَرىٰ تَقَلْبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي السَّمَاءِ فَلَنُوَلَّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضاها» ».
english_text:
Narrated by al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah
{a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the saying of the Exalted: ‘"And We did not make the qiblah which
you were upon except that We might know who follows the Messenger from those who
turn back on their heels"’ (Surah Baqarah 2:143). Was He {saws} commanded with it?”
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and
his family, used to turn His {saws} face toward the sky, and Allah {SWT}, Mighty and
Majestic, knew what was in His {saws} soul, so He {SWT} said: ‘'Indeed, We see the turning
of your face toward the sky, so We shall surely turn you to a qiblah that pleases you.'’"
(Surah Baqarah 2:144)
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.43 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.536 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.296 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.1 p.345 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.1 9 p.199 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.136 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.2 p.181

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ وُهَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى «سَيَقُولُ السُّفَهَاءُ مِنَ النَّاسِ مَا وَلاهُمْ
عَنْ قِبْلَتِهِمُ الَّتِي كَانُوا عَلَيْهَا قُلْ لِلهِ الْمَشرِقُ وَ الْمَغْرِبُ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ إِلى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمِ» فَقُلْتُ لَهُ اللّهُ أَمَرَهُ
أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ إِلَى ٱلْبَيْتِ الْمُقَدَّسِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ أَلاَ تَرَى أَنَّ اللّهَ تَعَالَى يَقُولُ «وَ مَا جَعَلْنَا ٱلْقِبْلَةَ آلَّتِي كُثْتَ عَلَيْها إِلا لِنَعْلَمَ
مَنْ يَتَّبِعُ الرَّسُولَ مِمَّنْ يَتْقَلِبُ عَلى عَقِبَيْهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةَ إِلا عَلَى آلَّذِينَ هَدَى اللهُ وَ مَا كَانَ اللَهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَانَكُمْ
إنَّ اللهَ بِالنّاسِ لَرَوُفٌ رَجيمٌ» » قَالَ «إِنّ بَنِي عَبْدِ الْأَشهَلِ أَتَوْهُمْ وَ هُمْ فِي الصَّلَاةِ وَ قَدْ صَلَّوْا رَكْعَتَيْنِ إلَى بَيْتِ
الْمَقْدِسِ فَقِيلَ لَهُمْ إِنَّ نَبِيَّكُمْ قَدْ صُرِفَ إِلَى الْكَعْبَةِ فَتَحَوَّلَ ٱلنَّسَاءُ مَكَانَ ٱلرِّجَالِ وَ الرِّجَالُ مَكَانَ النَّسَاءِ وَ جَعَلُوا
الرَّكْفَتَيْنِ الْبَاقِيَتَيْنِ إِلَى الْكَفْبَةِ فَصَلَّوْا صَلاَةً وَاحِدَةً إِلَى قِبْلَتَيْنِ فَلِذَلِكَ سُمِّيَ مَسْجِدُهُمْ مَسْجِدَ الْقِبْلَتَيْنِ».
english_text:
Narrated from him from Wuhayb from Abu Basir from one of the two (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon them:
(Imam {a.s} was asked) regarding the saying of the Exalted: ‘"The foolish among the
people will say: What has turned them away from their qiblah, which they were upon?
Say: To Allah {SWT} belong the East and the West. He guides whom He wills to a straight
path."’ (Surah Baqarah 2:142)
I (Abu Basir) said to Him {a.s}: "Did Allah {SWT} command Him {saws} to pray toward Bayt al-
Maqdis (Jerusalem)?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes. Do you not see that Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, says: ‘'And We did not
make the qiblah which you were upon except that We might know who follows the
Messenger from those who turn back on their heels. And indeed, it was difficult except
for those whom Allah {SWT} has guided. And Allah {SWT} would never let your faith go to
waste. Indeed, Allah {SWT} is Kind and Merciful to the people.'‘" (Surah Baqarah 2:143)
Imam {a.s} said: "The tribe of Banu Abd al-Ashhal came to them while they were in prayer
and had already prayed two rak’ahs facing Bayt al-Maqdis. It was said to them,
'Indeed, your Prophet has now been directed toward the Ka’bah.' So the women
switched places with the men, and the men switched places with the women, and they
made the remaining two rak’ahs facing the Ka’bah. Thus, they prayed one prayer
toward two qiblahs. For that reason, their mosque was named 'Masjid al-Qiblatayn'
(the Mosque of the Two Qiblahs)."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.43 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.537 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.297 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.1 p.339 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.1 9 p.200 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.136 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.2 p.183

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ الْحَجَّالِ عَنْ بَعْضِ رِجَالِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ
اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ : «أَنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى جَعَلَ الْكَعْبَةَ قِبْلَةً لِأَهْلِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَجَعَلَ الْمَسْجِدَ قِبْلَةً لِأَهْلِ الْحَرَمِ وَجَعَلَ الْحَرَمَ
قِبْلَةً لِأهْلِ الدُّنْيَا».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn from ‘Ubaydullah ibn
Muhammad al-Hajjal from some of his men:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "Indeed, Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, made the Ka’bah the qiblah for
the people of the Masjid, and made the Masjid the qiblah for the people of the Haram,
and made the Haram the qiblah for the people of the world."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.272 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.2 p.195 • ‘Ilal Al-Shara’i’, Vol.2 p.415 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.44 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.71 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.541 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.303 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.304 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 1 p.50

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
أَبُو الْعَبَّاسٍ اِبْنُ عُقْدَةَ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَازِمِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا تَغْلِبُ بْنُ الضَّحَاكِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا بِشِرُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ
الْجُعْفِي أَبُو الْوَلِيدِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ جَعْفَرَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ يَقُولُ: « البَيْتُ قِبْلَةً لِأَهْلِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَ الْمَسْجِدُ قِبْلَةً
لِأَهْلِ اَلْحَرَمِ وَ الْحَرَمُ قِبْلَةٌ لِلنَّاسِ جَمِيعاً».
english_text:
Narrated by Abu al-Abbas Ibn ‘Uqdah from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Hazim, who said: Taghlib ibn al-
Dahhak narrated to us, who said: Bishr ibn Ja’far al-Ju’fi Abu al-Walid narrated to us, who said:
I (Bishr ibn Ja’far) heard (Imam) Ja’far ibn Muhammad {a.s}, peace be upon him, say:
"The House (Ka’bah) is the qiblah for the people of the Mosque, and the Mosque is the
qiblah for the people of the Haram, and the Haram is the qiblah for all people."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.44 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.542 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.304

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ رَفَعَهُ قَالَ: قِيلَ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ لِمَ صَارَ الرَّجُلُ يَنْحَرِفُ فِي
الصَّلاةٍ إِلَى الْيَسَارِ فَقَالَ «لِأَنَّ لِلْكَفْبَةِ سِتَّةَ حُدُودٍ أَرْبَعَةٌ مِنْهَا عَلَى يَسَارِكَ وَ إِثنَانٍ مِنْهَا عَلَى يَمِينِكَ فَمِنْ أَجْلِ ذَلِكَ
وَقَعَ التَّحْرِيفُ عَلَى الْيَسَارِ».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Ali ibn Muhammad, who raised it, said:
It was said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: "Why does a person turn slightly to the left during
prayer?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Because the Ka’bah has six sides, four of them are on your left and two
of them are on your right. Therefore, the slight turning is toward the left."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.487 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.44 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.542 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.305

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
وَ سَأَلَ الْمُفَضَّلُ بْنُ عُمَرَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ : عَنِ التَّحْرِيفِ لِأَصْحَابِنَا ذَاتَ الْيَسَارِ عَنِ الْقِبْلَةِ وَ عَنِ السِّبَبِ فِيهِ فَقَالَ
«إِنَّ الْحَجَرَ الْأَسْوَدَ لَمَا أَنْزِلَ بِهِ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ وَ وُضِعَ فِي مَوْضِعِهِ جُعِلَ أَنْصَابُ الْحَرَمِ مِنْ حَيْثُ يَلْحَقُهُ النُورُ نُورُ
اَلْحَجَرِ فَهِيَ عَنْ يَمِينِ الْكَفْبَةِ أَرْبَعَةُ أَمْيَالٍ وَ عَنْ يَسَارِهَا ثَمَانِيَةُ أَمْيَالٍ كُلُهُ اِثنَا عَشَرَ مِيلاً فَإِذَا اِنْحَرَفَ الْإِنْسَانُ
ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ خَرَجَ عَنْ حَدِّ الْقِبْلَةِ لِقِلَّةِ أَنْصَابِ الْحَرَمِ وَ إِذَا اِنْحَرَفَ ذَاتَ ٱلْيَسَارِ لَمْ يَكُنْ خَارِجاً عَنْ حَدَّ الْقِبْلَةِ».
english_text:
Al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about the slight turning to the left from
the qiblah by our companions and about the reason for it.
Imam {a.s} said: "Indeed, when the Black Stone was brought down from Paradise and
placed in its position, the boundaries (ansab) of the Haram were set according to the
extent reached by the light, the light of the Stone. So the boundary on the right side of
the Ka’bah is four miles, and on its left side is eight miles, altogether twelve miles.
Therefore, if a person turns to the right, he exits the boundary of the qiblah due to the
shorter extent of the Haram markers on that side. But if he turns to the left, he is not
outside the boundary of the qiblah."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.272 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.44

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
الطّاطَرِيٌ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةً عَنْ عَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا ٱلسَلامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ
الْقِبْلَةً قَالَ «ضَعِ الْجَدْيَ فِي قَفَاكَ وَ صَلَّ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (وإذا اطبقت السماء بالغيم فلم يجد الانسان دليلا عليها بالشمس والنجوم فليصل الى أربع جهات،
مان له يقد عل ذلك لسسسمن الاساب المانعة من الصلاة ألعمدات فليصا الأ، حمة شاء وذلك محذمه الاضطا,)
english_text:
Narrated by al-Tatari from Ja’far ibn Sama’ah from al-’Alaʾ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one
of the two (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the qiblah.
Imam {a.s} said: "Place al-Jady (the Pole Star) behind you and pray."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "And if the sky is completely
covered with clouds and a person cannot determine the qiblah by means of the sun or
stars, then he should pray facing all four directions. And if he is unable to do so due to
any reason that prevents him from praying four times, then he should pray facing
whichever direction he chooses, and that is sufficient in a state of necessity."
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.45 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.547 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.306

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عَبَّادٍ عَنْ جِرَاشٍ عَنْ بَعْضٍ
أَضْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّ هَوُلاءِ الْمُخَالِفِينَ عَلَيْنَا يَقُولُونَ إِذَا أُظْبِقَتْ
عَلَيْنَا أَوْ أَظْلَمَتْ فَلَمْ نَعْرِفِ السِّمَاءَ كُنَّا وَ أَنْتُمْ سَوَاءً فِي الاِجْتِهَادِ فَقَالَ «لَيْسَ كَمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ فَلْيُصَلَ
الأزبَع وُجُوهٍ».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Isma’il ibn
Abbad from Khirash from one of our companions from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: "May I be your ransom, these opponents of ours say that when the
sky is covered or darkened so we cannot recognize the direction of the sky, we and you
are the same in exercising ijtihad (independent judgment)."
Imam {a.s} said: "It is not as they say. When that happens, then one must pray in four
directions."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.45 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.295 • Al-Aman, Vol.1 p.94 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.550 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.311

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
وَ رَوَى الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عَبَادٍ عَنْ خِرَاشٍ عَنْ بَعْضٍ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ : مِثلَهُ.
فأما ما يدل على ان التحري يجزي عند الضرورة ما رواه:
english_text:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Isma’il ibn ‘Abbad from Khirash from one of our
companions from Abu Abdillah {a.s}: the same (report).
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
As for what indicates that estimation (taharri) is sufficient in cases of necessity, it is
what has been narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.45 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.295 • Al-Aman, Vol.1 p.94 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.550 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.311

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَخيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ حَمَادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «يُجْزِي التَّحَرِّي أُبَداً إذَا لَمْ يُعلَمْ أَيْنَ وَجْهُ ٱلْقِبْلَةِ».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from
Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:
Abu Ja’far {a.s} said: "Estimation (taharri) is always sufficient when the direction of the
qiblah is not known."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.285 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.45 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.295 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.548 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.307 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.73

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عُثَمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ بِاللَّيْلِ
وَ اَلنَّهَارِ إِذَا لَمْ تُرَ الشَمْسُ وَ لا الْقَمَرُ وَ لاَ النُجُومُ قَالَ «اِجْتَهِذْ رَأْيَكَ وَ تَعَمَّدِ الْقِبْلَةَ جُهْدَكَ».
english_text:
Narrated Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama’ah, said:
I asked Him {a.s} about praying during the night and the day when neither the sun, nor
the moon, nor the stars can be seen.
Imam {a.s} said: "Exert your reasoning and aim toward the qiblah as best you can."
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.284 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.222 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.46 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.46 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.255 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.295 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.295 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.255 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.548 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.308

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
الحسين بن سعيد عن الحسن عن زرعة عن سماعة قال : سألته عن الصلاة بالليل والنهار إذا لم تر الشمس ولا
القمر ولا النجوم قال : تجتهد رأيك وتعمد القبلة جهدك.
وليس لاحد أن يقول لم حملتم هذه الاخبار على حال الاضطرار دون حال الاختيار؟ وهلا جاز التحرى في كل وقت التبس
فيه القبلة؟ لانا متى لم نحمل هذه الاخبار على حال الاضطرار لم يكن لما قدمناه من الخبرين بأنه يصلي الى أربع جهات
معنى ، لان على مقتضى ظاهر هذه الاحاديث يجزي التحري ولا يحتاج في حال أن يصلي الى أربع جهات فيسقط
متضمنهما جملة ، وإذا حملنا هذه الاخبار على حال الضرورة وذينك الحديثين على حال الاختيار نكون قد جمعنا بينها على
وجه لا تنافي بينها، والذي يدل على ما قلناه من أن المراد بهذه الاخبار حال الاضطرار دون حال الاختيار.
english_text:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Hasan from Zur’ah from Sama’ah, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about prayer during the night and day when neither the sun, nor the
moon, nor the stars are visible.
Imam {a.s} said: "Exert your reasoning and aim toward the qiblah as best you can."
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
commentary:
And no one has the right to say: ‘Why have you interpreted these narrations as applying
only to a state of necessity and not also to a state of choice? Why should estimation
(taharri) not be permissible at any time when the direction of the qiblah is uncertain?’
Because, if we do not interpret these narrations as referring to a state of necessity,
then the two previously mentioned reports, that one should pray toward four
directions, would have no meaning. According to the apparent sense of these hadiths,
taharri would be sufficient, and there would be no need to pray in four directions, thus
their content would be entirely negated.
However, if we interpret these narrations as applying to a case of necessity, and those
two reports as referring to the state of choice, then we will have reconciled them in a
way that avoids contradiction. And what supports what we have said, that the meaning
of these narrations is in cases of necessity, not choice, is the following:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
مَا رَوَاهُ الطّاطَرِيٌّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ حَمَادٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ يَحْيَى قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجْلِ
صَلَّى عَلَى غَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ ثُمَّ تَبَيَّنَتْ لَهُ الْقِبْلَةُ وَ قَدْ دَخَلَ فِي وَقْتِ صَلاةٍ أُخْرَى قَالَ «يُعيدُهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ هَذِهِ الَّتِي
قَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُهَا».
english_text:
Narrated by al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hammad from ‘Amr ibn Yahya, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who prayed not facing the qiblah, and then the
correct direction of the qiblah became clear to him after he had entered the time of
another prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must repeat that prayer before performing the one whose time has
now entered."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.46 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.297 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.553 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.313

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مَعْمَرِ بْنِ يَحْيَى قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلِ
صَلَّى عَلَى غَيْرِ ٱلْقِبْلَةِ ثُمَّ تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ ٱلْقِبْلَةُ وَ قَدْ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ صَلاَةٍ أُخْرَى قَالَ «يُصَلِّيهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ هَذِهِ الَّتِي دَخَلَ
وَقْتُهَا إِلاَّ أَنْ يَخَافَ فَوْتَ الْتِي دَخَلَ وَقْتُهَا».
فلو لم يكن المراد بتلك الاحاديث حال الاضطرار لم يكن لايجاب الاعادة بعد خروج الوقت معنى حسب ما تضمنه هذان
الخبران لان ظاهرهما يقضي انه متى تحرى القبلة وصلى ثم خرج الوقت فانه اجزات صلاته. قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه :ومن
اخطأ القبلة أوسها عنها ثم عرف ذلك والوقت باق أعاد ، فان عرفه بعد خروج الوقت لم يكن عليه اعادة فيما مضى اللهم
إلا أن يكون قد صلى مستدبر القبلة فيجب عليه حينئذ اعادة الصلاة كان الوقت باقيا أو منقضيا.
english_text:
Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ma’mar ibn Yahya, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who prayed not facing the qiblah, and then the
correct direction of the qiblah became clear to him after the time of another prayer
had entered.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should repeat the former prayer before performing the one whose
time has entered, unless he fears missing the one whose time has now entered."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So if the meaning of those hadiths were not referring to a state of necessity, then the
requirement to repeat the prayer after the time has passed, as these two narrations
indicate, would have no meaning. Because their apparent meaning implies that
whenever a person estimates the direction of the qiblah (taharra al-qiblah) and
performs the prayer, and then the time exits, his prayer is valid.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "And whoever errs in the
direction of the qiblah or forgets it, then realizes it while the time remains, he must
repeat (the prayer). But if he realizes it after the time has passed, there is no obligation
upon him to repeat what has passed, except if he had prayed with his back to the
qiblah, in which case he must repeat the prayer, whether the time remains or has
ended."
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.46 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.297

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
عَلِي بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا
صَلَّيْتَ وَ أَنتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ وَ اِسْتَبَانَ لَكَ أَنَّكَ صَلَّيْتَ وَ أَنْتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ وَ أَنتَ فِي وَقْتٍ فَأَعِدْ وَ إِنْ فَانَكَ
اَلْوَقْتُ فَلا تُعِد».
english_text:
Narrated by Ali ibn Mahzyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "If you pray while not facing the qiblah, and it becomes clear to
you that you prayed not facing the qiblah while still within the time (of that prayer), then
repeat it. But if the time has passed, then do not repeat it."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.284 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.47 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.47 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.142 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.296 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.552 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.315 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.317 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.74

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
وَ عَنَهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمِ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدِ قَالَ:
قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَ الرَّجُلُ يَكُونُ فِي قَفْرٍ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ فِي يَوْمٍ غَيْمٍ فَيُصَلِّي لِغَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ ثُمّ يُضْحِي فَيَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ
صَلَّى لِغَيْرٍ الْقِبْلَةِ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ فِي وَقْتٍ فَلْيُعِذْ صَلاَتَهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ مَضَى الْوَقْتُ فَحَسْبُهُ اِجْتِهَادُهُ».
english_text:
Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from
Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: "A man is in a remote land on a cloudy day and prays not
facing the qiblah, then the sky clears and he realizes that he prayed in the wrong
direction, what should he do?"
Imam {a.s} said: "If he is still within the time (of that prayer), then he should repeat his
prayer. But if the time has passed, then his effort (ijtihad) suffices him."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.285 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.47 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.142 • Al- Istibsar, Vol.1 p.296 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.551 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.317

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text: الطَاطَرِيّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ : مِثلَهُ.
english_text:
Narrated by al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Abdullah ibn Muskan
from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah {a.s}: the same (report).
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.285 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.47 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.142 • Al- Istibsar, Vol.1 p.296 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.551 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.317

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
وعنه عن محمد بن زياد عن أبان بن عثمان عن عبد الرحمن ابن أبي عبد اللّٰه عن أبي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام قال
قال أبو عبد اللّه عليه السلام : إذا صليت وأنت على غير القبلة واستبان لك انك على غير القبلة وأنت في وقت
فأعد وان فاتك فلا تعد.
english_text:
Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah
from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "If you pray while not facing the qiblah, and it becomes clear to
you that you were not facing the qiblah while you are still within the time (of that
prayer), then repeat it. But if the time has passed, then do not repeat it."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ عَبْداَ صَالِحاً عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى
فِي يَوْمٍ سَحَابٍ عَلَى غَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ ثُمَّ طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ وَ هُوَ فِي وَقْتِ أَ يُعِيدُ الصَّلاَةَ إِذَا كَانَ قَدْ صَلَى عَلَى غَيْرٍ
الْقِبْلَةً وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَدْ تَحَرَّى الْقِبْلَةَ بِجُهْدِهِ أتُجْزِيهِ صَلَاَتُهُ فَقَالَ «يُعِيدُ مَا كَانَ فِي وَقْتٍ فَإِذَا ذَهَبَ ٱلْوَقْتُ فَلاَ إِعَادَةَ
عَلَيْهِ».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ya’qub ibn Yaqtin, who
said:
I asked the Righteous Servant (Abd Salih {a.s}) about a man who prayed on a cloudy day
not facing the qiblah, and then the sun rose while he was still within the prayer time.
Should he repeat the prayer if he had prayed not facing the qiblah, even if he had made
his best effort to determine its direction? Does his prayer suffice him?
Imam {a.s} said: "He must repeat what was within the time. But once the time has
passed, there is no repetition upon him."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.48 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.141 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.552 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.316

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى غَيْرٍ
الْقِبْلَةٍ فَاسْتَبَانَ لَكَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُصْبِحَ أَنَّكَ صَلِّيْتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ ٱلْقِبْلَةِ فَأَعِدْ صَلاَتَكَ».
english_text:
Narrated from him from Ahmad from al-Husayn from Fadalah from Aban from Zurarah:
Abu Ja’far {a.s} said: "If you prayed not facing the qiblah, and it becomes clear to you
before morning that you had prayed not facing the qiblah, then repeat your prayer."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.48 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.297 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.553 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.316

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ الْحَجَالِ عَنْ تَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسّلَاَمُ
قَالَ: قُلْتُ الرَّجُلُ يَقُومُ فِي الصَّلاَةِ ثُمَّ يَنْظُرُ بَعْدَ مَا فَرَغَ فَيَرَى أُنَّهُ قَدِ إِنْحَرَفَ عَنِ ٱلْقِبْلَةِ يَمِينا وَ شِمَالاً قَالَ «قَدْ
مَضَتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ مَا بَيْنَ ٱلْمَشرِقِ وَ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ قِبْلَةٌ».
english_text:
Narrated from him from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hajjal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from
Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I said (to Imam {a.s}): "A man stands in prayer, and then after finishing he notices that he
had deviated from the qiblah to the right or to the left."
Imam {a.s} said: "His prayer is valid. What lies between the East and the West is qiblah."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.276 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.48 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.297 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.554 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.314

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ الْوَلِيدِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ وَ هُوَ فِي
الصَّلاةٍ أَنَّهُ عَلَى غَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ قَالَ «يَسْتَقْبِلُهَا إِذَا أُثُبِتَ ذَلِكَ وَ إن كَانَ قَدْ فَرَغَ مِنْهَا فَلا يُعيدُهَا».
english_text:
Narrated from him from Ahmad from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid,
who said:
I asked him about a man who realizes during his prayer that he is not facing the qiblah.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should turn toward it if that is confirmed. But if he has already
finished the prayer, then he does not need to repeat it."
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.48 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.297 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.554 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.314

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ
سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقٍ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى السَّابَاطِيَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ : فِي رَجُلٍ صَلَّى عَلَى
غَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ فَيَعْلَمُ وَ هُوَ فِي الصَّلاَةِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَفْرُغَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ قَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ مُتَوَجَّها فِيمَا بَيْنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَ ٱلْمَعْرِبِ
فَلْيُحَوِّلْ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ جِينَ يَعْلَمُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ مُتَوَجِّها إِلَى دُبُرِ الْقِبْلَةِ فَلْيَقْطَعْ ثُمَّ يُحَوِّلُ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ ثُمَّ
يَفْتَتِحُ الصَّلاَةَ».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn
Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa’id from Musaddiq
ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} (was asked) regarding a man who prayed not facing the qiblah, and he
realizes this while still in his prayer, before completing it.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he is facing a direction between the East and the West, then he
should turn his face toward the qiblah when he becomes aware. But if he is facing the
opposite of the qiblah (his back toward it), then he should stop the prayer, then turn
his face toward the qiblah, and then begin the prayer anew."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.285 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.48 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.142 • Al- Istibsar, Vol.1 p.298 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.73 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.554 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.315

Chapter Title: THE QIBLAH (DIRECTION OF PRAYER)
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُصَيْنِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى عَبْدِ صَالِحِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ الرَّجُلُ يُصَلِّي فِي يَوْمٍ غَيْمِ
فِي فَلاَةٍ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَ لا يَعْرِفُ الْقِبْلَةَ فَيُصَلِّي حَتَّى إِذَا فَرَغَ مِنْ صَلَاَتِهِ بَدَثْ لَهُ الشَّمْسُ فَإِذَا هُوَ قَدْ صَلِّى لِغَيْرٍ
الْقِبْلَةِ أَيَعْتَدُّ بِصَلاتِهِ أَمْ يُعِيدُهَا فَكَتَبَ «يُعِيدُهَا مَا لَمْ يَفُثْهُ الْوَقْتُ أَوَ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَقُولُ وَ قَوْلُهُ الْحَقُّ «فَأَيْنَمَا
ثُوَلُوا فَتَمَّ وَجَهُ اللَّهِ» ».
٦ - باب الاذان والاقامة
english_text:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, who said:
I (Muhammad ibn al-Husayn) wrote to the Righteous Servant (Abd Salih {a.s}), peace be
upon him, asking; “A man prays on a cloudy day in an open desert and does not know
the direction of the qiblah, so he prays, and then after finishing his prayer, the sun
appears and he realizes that he had prayed in the wrong direction. Should he count his
prayer as valid, or must he repeat it?”
He {a.s}, peace be upon him, wrote in reply: "He should repeat it, as long as the time has
not passed. Do you not know that Allah {SWT} says, and His {SWT} word is the truth, ‘So
wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah {SWT}’?" (Surah Baqarah 2:115)
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is proper that the adhan be
given for every obligatory prayer, and the iqamah as well."
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.49 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.297 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.555 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.316 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.1 p.313 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 1 p.31

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
رَوَى الْحُسَيْنُ بنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ أَو اِبْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنِ ٱلصَّبَّاحِ بْنِ سَيَابَةَ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَنْدِ
اللَّهِ عَ : «لا تَدَعِ الْأَذَانَ فِي الصَّلَوَاتِ كُلَّهَا فَإِنْ تَرَكْتَهُ فَلاَ تَتْرُكْهُ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ وَ الْفَجْرِ فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ فِيهِمَا تَقْصِيرٌ».
english_text:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Mu’awiyah ibn Wahb or Ibn ‘Ammar from al-Sabbah ibn
Sayyabah, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said to me (al-Sabbah): "Do not abandon the adhan in any of the
prayers. But if you do leave it, then do not leave it for Maghrib and Fajr, for there is no
shortening in them."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.49 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.299 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.386

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدَّقٍ بْنِ صَدَفَةَ عَنْ
عَمَّارٍ السَّابَاطِيَّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا قُمْتَ إِلَى صَلاَةٍ فَرِيضَةٍ فَأَذِّنْ وَ أَقِمْ وَ اِفْصِلْ بَيْنَ ٱلْأَذَانِ
وَ الإقَامَةٍ بِقُعُودٍ أَوْ بِكَلاَمٍ أَوْ بِتَسْبِيحِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (فان كانت صلاة جماعة كان الاذان والاقامة لها واجبين لا يجوز تركهما في تلك الحال).
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Amr ibn
Sa’id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "When you stand for an obligatory prayer, then give the adhan
and the iqamah, and separate between the adhan and the iqamah by sitting, or by
speaking, or by glorifying (tasbih)."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "If the prayer is being
performed in congregation, then the adhan and the iqamah are both obligatory for it,
and it is not permissible to omit them in that case."
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.49 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.397

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدِ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ
بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السِّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلتُهُ أَ يُجْزِي أَذَانْ وَاحِدٌ قَالَ «إِنْ صَلِّيْتَ جَمَاعَةً
لَمْ يُجْزِ إِلّا أَذَانُ وَ إِقَامَةُ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ وَحْدَكَ تُبَادِرُ أَمْراً تَخَافُ أَنْ يَفْوتَكَ يُجْزِيكَ إِقَامَةٌ إِلا الْفَجْرَ وَ ٱلْمَغْرِبَ فَإِنَّهُ
يَتْبَغِي أَنْ تُوَذِّنَ فِيهِمَا وَ تُقِيمَ مِنْ أَجْلٍ أَنَّهُ لا تَقْصُرُ فِيهِمَا كَمَا تَقْصُرُ فِي سَائِرِ الصَّلَوَاتِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ولا بأس أن يقتصر الانسان إذا صلى وحده بغير إمام على الاقامة ويترك الاذان في ثلاث صلوات
الظهر والعصر والعشاء الآخرة ولا يترك الاذان والاقامة في المغرب والفجر لانهما صلاتان لا يقصران في السفر) قد مضى
ذكر ذلك في الحديثين المتقدمين ويزيد تأكيدا ما رواه:
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya’qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-
Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from one of the two
(Imams {a.s}), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him {a.s}: "Is one adhan sufficient?"
Imam {a.s} said: "If you are praying in congregation, then one adhan and one iqamah are
required. But if you are alone and hastening due to a matter you fear may pass you by,
then the iqamah suffices, except for Fajr and Maghrib, for it is proper that you give the
adhan and the iqamah for them, because they are not shortened like the other
prayers."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "There is no harm if a person,
when praying alone without an imam, suffices with the iqamah and leaves out the
adhan in three prayers: Dhuhr, ‘Asr, and ‘Ishaʾ al-Akhirah. But he should not leave out
the adhan and the iqamah in Maghrib and Fajr, for these are two prayers that are not
shortened during travel."
This has already been mentioned in the two previously cited hadiths, and it is further
affirmed by what has been narrated:
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.303 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.50 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.299 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.603

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ
بْنِ زِيَادٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: «إِذَا كَانَ الْقَوْمُ لا يَنْتَظِرُونَ أَحَداً اِكْتَفَوْا بِإِقَامَةٍ وَاحِدَةِ».
english_text:
Narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from
Abdullah ibn Bukayr from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "If the people are not waiting for anyone, then one iqamah alone
suffices."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.50 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.603 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.385

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
وَ عَنَهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَادٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ ٱلْحَلَبِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ : «أَنَّهُ كَانَ إِذَا صَلَّى وَحْدَهُ فِي الْبَيْتِ أَقَامَ إِقَامَةً وَ لَمْ يُؤَذِّنْ».
english_text:
Narrated from him from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad from ‘Ubaydullah ibn
Ali al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} (narrates) from his father {a.s}: "That He (Imam al-Baqir {a.s}), when He
{a.s} prayed alone in the house, would give the iqamah and would not give the adhan."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al- Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.50 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.604 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.385

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
وَ رَوَى الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «يُجْزِيكَ
إِذَا خَلَوْتَ فِي بَيْتِكَ إِقَامَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ بِغَيْرِ أَذَانِ».
وهذه الاخبار كلها دالة على تأكيد الاذان في صلاة الجماعة لانها تتضمن إباحة تركها مقيدا بحال الوحدة والخلوة، وهذا
الا يكون إلا للمنفرد فأما اختصاص الغداة والمغرب فقد مضى ما يدل عليه ويزيده بيانا ما رواه :
english_text:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "It suffices you, when you are alone in your house, to give one
iqamah without an adhan."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
And all these narrations indicate the emphasis on the adhan in congregational prayer,
because they include the permissibility of omitting it only when alone and in seclusion,
and this applies only to the individual praying alone. As for the particular emphasis on
Fajr and Maghrib, what has been mentioned already supports that, and it is further
clarified by what has been narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.50 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.604 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.384

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بَنْ سَعِيدِ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ أَخِيهِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ : « لا تُصَلِّ اَلْغَدَاةَ وَ
اَلْمَغْرِبَ إلاَّ بِأْذَانٍ وَ إِقَامَةٍ وَ رُخَّصَ فِي سَائِرِ الصَّلَوَاتِ بِالْإِقَامَةِ وَ الْأَذَانُ أَفْضَلُ».
english_text:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from his brother al-Hasan from Zur’ah from Sama’ah, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "Do not pray the morning (ghadah) and Maghrib prayers except
with adhan and iqamah, and it is permitted in the rest of the prayers to suffice with the
iqamah, but the adhan is better."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.51 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.299 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.604 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.384 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.387

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ النَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «يُجْزِيكَ فِي الصَّلاَةِ إِقَامَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ
إلاًّ الْغَدَاةَ وَ ٱلْمَغْرِبَ».
english_text:
Narrated from him from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "One iqamah suffices you for the prayer, except for the morning
(ghadah) and Maghrib."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.51 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.300 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.604 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.387

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ
اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الْإِقَامَةِ بِغَيْرِ أَذَانٍ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ فَقَالَ «لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسِّ وَ مَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ يُعْتَادَ».
فليس بمناف لما ذكرناه لانه إنما جوز له الاقتصار على الاقامة في هذه الصلاة عند عارض ومانع ثم نبهه بقوله وما أحب
أن يعتاد ذلك على أن الاولى فعله ، والذي يكشف عما ذكرناه من أنه إنما جوز له الاقتصار على الاقامة في سائر الصلوات
لعارض ومانع ما رواه:
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from
‘Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about giving the iqamah without the adhan for Maghrib.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in it, but I do not like that it becomes a habit."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So this is not in contradiction with what we have mentioned, for he only permitted
limiting oneself to the iqamah in this prayer (Maghrib) due to a temporary
circumstance or hindrance. Then he alerted him to what is preferable by saying, ‘"but
I do not like that it becomes a habit,"‘ indicating that it is better to perform both the
adhan and the iqamah.
And what further clarifies what we have mentioned, that the permission to suffice with
the iqamah in the rest of the prayers is due to a temporary situation or hindrance, is
what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.51 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.300 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.604 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.387

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ السِّنْدِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ
اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ: «يُقْصَرُ الْأَذَانُ فِي السَّفَرِ كَمَا تُقْصَرُ الصَّلاَةُ تُجْزِي إِقَامَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ».
english_text:
Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn
Udhaynah from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I heard Him {a.s} say: "The adhan is shortened during travel just as the prayer is
shortened. One iqamah suffices."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.51 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.605 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.385

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ الْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ
اللَّه عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ - عَنِ الرَّجُلِ هَلْ يُجْزِيهِ فِي السَّفَرِ وَ الْحَضَرِ إِقَامَةً لَيْسَ مَعَهَا أَذَانَ قَالَ «نَعَمْ لا بَأْسّ بِهِ».
english_text:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from
‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man, does it suffice him in travel and at home to give
only the iqamah without the adhan?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, there is no harm in it."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.51 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.605 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.384

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
سَعدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ وَ
الْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ قَالَ: «تُجْزِيكَ إِقَامَةٌ فِي السَّفَرِ».
فدلت هذه الاخبار على أن الاولى في الحضر فعل الاذان لانها تضمنت الرخصة في حال السفر ، ولو لم يكن الامر على ما
ذكرناه لم يكن لاختصاصه بحال السفر فائدة. قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (وفي الاذان والاقامة فضل كثير) إلى قوله : (ولا
english_text:
Narrated by Sa’d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban
ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from one of the two (Imams {a.s}):
(Imam {a.s}), peace be upon them, said: "One iqamah suffices you in travel."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
These narrations indicate that the preferable (awla) practice in a state of residence
(hadar) is to perform the adhan, because they include a concession specifically for the
state of travel. And if the matter were not as we have stated, then specifying the
concession for the case of travel would hold no benefit.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "There is great merit in the
adhan and the iqamah," up to his statement: "And it is not permissible to give the
adhan for any of the prayers before their time has entered, except for Fajr."
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.52 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.606 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.385

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى الْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا أَذَّنْتَ فِي أَرْضِ فَلاةٍ وَ أَقَمْتَ صَلَّى
خَلْفَكَ صَفَّانٍ مِنَ ٱلْمَلائِكَةِ وَ إِنْ أَقَمْتَ وَ لَمْ تُؤَذِّنْ صَلَّى خَلْفَكَ صَفّ وَاحِدٌ».
english_text:
Narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Yahya al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "If you give the adhan and the iqamah in an open, deserted land,
two rows of angels will pray behind you. But if you give only the iqamah without the
adhan, then one row of angels will pray behind you."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.52 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.1 p.330 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.559 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.381

Chapter Title: THE ADHAN (CALL TO PRAYER) AND THE IQAMAH
arabic_text:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ
: «إِنَّكَ إِذَا أَذَّنْتَ وَ أَقَمْتَ صَلَّى خَلْفَكَ صَفَّانِ مِنَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةِ وَ إِنْ أَقَمْتَ إِقَامَةً بِغَيْرِ أَذَانِ صَلَّى خَلْفَكَ صَفّ وَاجِدٌ».
english_text:
Narrated from him from Fadalah from Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan from Muhammad ibn Muslim,
who said:
