فِي التَّوَجُّهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَنْ تَقُولَ - «وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي قَطَرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَ الْأَرْضَ» عَلَى مِلَّةٍ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفاً مُسْلِما
«وَ مَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُشِرِكِينَ» «إِنَّ صَلاتِي وَ نُسُكِي وَ مَحْيَايَ وَ مَمَاتِي لِلهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ "لا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ بِذَلِكَ أُمِرْتُ»
وَ أَنَا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ يُجْزِيكَ تَكْبِيرَةً وَاحِدَةٌ».
english_text:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and
al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “It suffices you in prayer, in the words of
directing yourself toward Allah {SWT} (‘tawajjuh’), to say:
‘I turn my face toward the One {AZJ} who created the heavens and the earth, upon the
creed of Abraham, upright and submitting, and I am not among the polytheists. Indeed
my prayer, my sacrifice, my life, and my death are for Allah {SWT}, the Lord {AZJ} of the
worlds. No partner has He {AZJ}, and with this I have been commanded, and I am among
the Muslims.’
And one ‘takbirah’ (saying of ‘Allahu Akbar’) is sufficient for you.”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.67 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.4 p.17 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.639 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.25

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ صَفَوَانَ قَالَ: صَلِّيْتُ خَلْفَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَيَّاماً
كَانَ يَقْرَأَ فِي فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ «بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمْنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ -» فَإِذَا كَانَ صَلاَةً لاَ يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ جَهَرَ بِ «بِسْمِ اللَّهِ
الرّحْمْنِ الرّجِيمِ -» وَ أَخْفَى مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ.
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Safwan who said:
I prayed behind Abu Abdillah {a.s} for several days. He {a.s} used to recite in Surah al-
Fatiha: ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’, and when it was a prayer in which the
recitation is not to be recited aloud, He {a.s} would recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir
Rahim’ aloud and would conceal the rest (of the surahs).”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.68 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.310 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.650 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.57 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.134 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.35

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ
بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ إِمَاماً
فَيَسْتَفْتِحُ بِالْحَمْدِ وَ لا يَقْرَأُ «بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمْنِ الرَّجِيمِ -» فَقَالَ «لا يَضْرُهُ وَ لا بَأْسَ بِهِ».
فمحمول على حال التقية لان عند التقية يجوز الاخفات بها ويحتمل أن يكون أراد عليه السلام من لا يقرأ بسم اللّٰه الرحمن
الرحيم ناسيا لان من نسي ذلك لا يضر ولا يجب عليه اعادة الصلاة ، ونحن نبينه فيما بعد، والذي يدل على أن في حال
التقية يجوز أن لا يجهر بها ما رواه:
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abd
al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz
ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who is an imam and begins with (Surah) al-Hamd
but does not recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’.
Imam {a.s} said: “It does not harm him, and there is no problem with it.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So it is to be interpreted as referring to a situation of ‘taqiyyah’ (dissimulation),
because in a state of ‘taqiyyah’ it is permissible to recite it silently. It is also possible
that the Imam {a.s}, peace be upon him, intended someone who did not recite ‘Bismillah
Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ out of forgetfulness, for the one who forgets that does not incur
harm and is not required to repeat the prayer, and we will clarify this later. What
indicates that during ‘taqiyyah’ it is permissible not to recite it aloud is what has been
narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.68

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي جَرِيرٍ زَكَرِيَّا بْنِ
إِذْرِيسَ الْقُمِّيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي بِقَوْمٍ يَكْرَهُونَ أَنْ يَجْهَرَ هِ «بِسْمِ اللَّهِ
الرَّحْمْنِ الرَّحِيمِ -» فَقَالَ «لا يَجْهَزْ».
english_text:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu
Jarir Zakariyya ibn Idris al-Qummi who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who leads a
people in prayer who dislike that he recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ aloud.
Imam {a.s} said: “Then he should not recite it aloud.”
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.68 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.312 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.650 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.60

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ
عَلِيَّ الْحَلَبِيِّ وَ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ وَ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ
عَلِيَّ الْحَلَبِيَّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : أَنَّهُمَا سَأَلاهُ عَمَّنْ يَقْرَأْ «بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمْنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ -» جينَ يُرِيدُ يَقْرَأْ
فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ إِنْ شَاءَ سِرَاً وَ إن شَاءَ جَهرا» فَقَالاَ أَ فَيَقْرَوُهَا مَعَ السُّورَةِ ٱلْأُخْرَى فَقَالَ «لا».
فمحمول على من كان في صلاة النافلة وقد قرأ من السورة الاخرى بعضها ويريد أن يقرأ باقيها فحينئذ لا يقرأ بسم اللّٰه
الرحمن الرحيم، والذي يبين ذلك ما رواه،
english_text:
Narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad
ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man and
Muhammad ibn Sinan and Abdullah ibn Muskan from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah {a.s}:
Both of them (Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi) asked Him {a.s} about one who recites
‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ when he wishes to recite Surah al-Fatiha.
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, if he wishes, silently, and if he wishes, aloud.”
So they asked: “Does he recite it with another Surah as well?”
Imam {a.s} said: “No.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So this is to be interpreted as referring to someone who is in a ‘nafila’ (supererogatory)
prayer and has already recited part of another Surah and intends to continue the rest
of it, in that case, he does not recite ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’. What clarifies
this is what has been narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.68 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.312 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.650 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.61

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ
بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسِّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَفْتَتِحُ ٱلْقِرَاءَةَ فِي الصَّلاةِ أَيَقْرَأْ «بِسْمِ اللّهِ الرَّحْمْنِ
الرَّجيمِ -) قَالَ «نَعَمْ إِذَا اِفْتَتَحَ الصَّلاةَ فَلْيَقُلْهَا فِي أَوَّلِ مَا يَفْتَتِحُ ثُمَّ يَكْفِيهِ مَا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ».
english_text:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala ibn Ayyub from Aban
ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, he said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who begins the recitation in prayer, should he recite
‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’?
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, when he begins the prayer, let him say it at the beginning of what
he opens with, and thereafter it suffices him.”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.69 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.313 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.651 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.61

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ
اللّه عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ إِذَا أَقَمْتُ للصَّلاةِ أَقْرَأ «بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمْنِ الرَّحِيمِ -» فِي فَاتِحَةِ الْقُرْآنِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ فَإِذَا
قَرَأْتُ فَاتِحَةَ الْقُرْآنِ أَقْرَأْ «بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمْنِ الرَّحِيمِ -» مَعَ السُّورَةِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Mu‘awiyah ibn
‘Ammar who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “When I stand for prayer, should I recite ‘Bismillah Hir
Rahman Nir Rahim’ in Surah al-Fatiha?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes.”
I asked: “Then when I have recited Surah al-Fatiha, should I recite ‘Bismillah Hir
Rahman Nir Rahim’ with the next Surah?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.312 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.69 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.311 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.647 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.58 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.9 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.1 p.12

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ عِمْرَانَ ٱلْهَمْدَانِيَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ
إِلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا تَقُولُ فِي رَجُلِ اِبْتَدَأَ بٍ «بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمْنِ الرَّحِيمِ» فِي صَلاتِهِ وَحْدَهُ
فِي أُمِّ الْكِتَابِ فَلَمَّا صَارَ إِلَى غَيْرِ أُمِّ الْكِتَابِ مِنَ السُّورَةِ تَرَكَهَا فَقَالَ الْعَبَّاسِيُ لَيْسَ بِذَلِكَ بَأْسٍّ فَكَتَّبَ بِحَطَّهِ
«يُعِيدُهَا مَرَّتَيْنِ عَلَى رَغَمِ أَنْفِهِ» يَعْنِي الْعَبَّاسِيَّ.
english_text:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Yahya
ibn ‘Imran al-Hamdani who said:
I wrote to Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him; “May I be your ransom, what do you say
about a man who begins with ‘Bismillah Hir Rahman Nir Rahim’ in his prayer, alone, in
Surah al-Fatiha, but when he reaches a different Surah after al-Fatiha, he omits it? The
‘Abbasid (official) said: ‘There is no harm in that.’”
So He {a.s}, peace be upon him, wrote in His {a.s} own handwriting:
“He must repeat it twice, despite his nose.”
This was meaning the ‘Abbasid (so the nose of that ‘Abbasid, who claimed there was
no harm, be rubbed in the dust).
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Jawad {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.313 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.69 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.58 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.87 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.9 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.1 p.13 • Awalim Al- Uloom, Vol.2 3 p.162 • Awalim Al-Uloom, Vol.2 3 p.391

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إذرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ
مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلامُ: «لا تَقْرَأ فِي الْمَكْتُوبَةِ بِأَقَلَ مِنْ سُورَةٍ وَ لاَ بِأَكْثَرَ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-
Hamid from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “Do not recite in the obligatory prayer less than one Surah, nor
more.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.314 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.69 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.314 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.679 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.43

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ الْعَلَاءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ
يَقْرَأُ السُّورَتَيْنِ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ فَقَالَ «لا لِكُلِّ سُورَةٍ رَكْعَةٌ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams {a.s}),
peace be upon them:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who recites two Surahs in one rak‘ah.
Imam {a.s} said: “No, for each Surah there is a rak‘ah.”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.70 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.314 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.679 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.44 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.50

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ الصَّيْقَلِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ
أَيُجَزِي عَنِّي أَنْ أَقُولَ فِي الْفَرِيضَةِ فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ وَحْدَهَا إِذَا كُنُتُ مُسْتَعْجِلاً أَوْ أَعْجَلَنِي شَيْءٌ فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from al-Hasan al-Sayqal who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “Is it sufficient for me to recite only Surah al-Fatiha in an
obligatory prayer if I am in a hurry or something hastens me?”
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.314 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.70 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.314 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.653 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.40

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ
اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «يَجُوزُ لِلْمَرِيضِ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ فِي الْفَرِيضَةِ فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ وَحْدَهَا وَ يَجُوزُ لِلصَّجِيحِ فِي قَضَاءٍ
صَلاةِ اَلتَّطَوْعِ بِاللّيْلِ وَ اَلنَّهَارِ».
وهذان الخبران يدلان على ان مع الاختيار لا يجوز الاقتصار على سورة واحدة
english_text:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abdullah
ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “It is permissible for a sick person to recite only Surah al-Fatiha
in the obligatory prayer, and it is also permissible for a healthy person when making up
voluntary prayers, whether at night or during the day.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
And these two reports indicate that in a state of choice, it is not permissible to suffice
with only one Surah.
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.314 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.70 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.315 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.654 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.40 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.130

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَرَوَى الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ الْقَرَوِيَّ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَقْرَأَ سُورَتَيْنِ
فِي رَكْعَةٍ قَالَ «نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ أَ لَيْسَ يُقَالُ أَغْطِ كُلَ سُورَةِ حَقَّهَا مِنَ الرُكُوعِ وَ السُّجُودِ فَقَالَ «ذَاكَ فِي ٱلْفَرِيضَةِ فَأَمًا
فِي اَلنَّافِلَةِ فَلَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسِّ».
english_text:
And al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from al-Qarawi from Aban from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “May I recite two Surahs in one rak‘ah?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes.”
I asked: “Is it not said that each Surah should be given its due in bowing and
prostration?”
Imam {a.s} said: “That applies in the obligatory prayer, but as for the supererogatory
prayer, there is no harm in it.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.70 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.316 • Al-Sarair, Vol.3 p.614 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.680 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.51 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.53 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.4 p.162

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ زُرَارَةُ قَالَ أَبْو
جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «إِنَّمَا يُكْرَهُ أَنْ يُجْمَعَ بَيْنَ السُّورَتَيْنِ فِي الْفَرِيضَةِ فَأَمَا النَّافِلَةُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from
Zurarah who said: Zurarah said:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “It is only disliked to combine two Surahs in
the obligatory prayer, but as for the supererogatory prayer, there is no harm in it.”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.314 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.70 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.72 • Al- Istibsar, Vol.1 p.317 • Al-Sarair, Vol.3 p.614 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.679 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.50 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.51 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.93 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.53

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ: «إِنَّ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ تَجُوزُ وَحْدَهَا فِي الْفَرِيضَةِ».
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from
Ali ibn Ri’ab from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, he said:
I heard Him {a.s} say: “Indeed, Surah al-Fatiha alone is valid in the obligatory prayer.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.71

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَرَوَى اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبِ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِنَّ فَاتِحَةَ ٱلْكِتَابِ
وَحَدَهَا تُجْزِي فِي الْفَرِيضَةِ».
فمحمول على حال الضرورة بدلالة ما ذكرناه أولا من انه لا يجوز الاقتصار على سورة الحمد مع الاختيار، ويزيده بيانا ما
رواه :
english_text:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri’ab from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “Indeed, Surah al-Fatiha alone suffices in the obligatory prayer.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So this is to be interpreted as referring to a situation of necessity, based on what we
mentioned earlier, that it is not permissible to suffice with Surah al-Hamd alone when
one has the choice. What further clarifies this is what has been narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.71 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.654 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.40

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ ٱلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلامُ قَالَ: «لا بَأْسَ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ الرَّجُلُ فِي الْفَرِيضَةِ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ إِذَا مَا أَعْجَلَتْ بِهِ حَاجَةٌ
أَوْ تَخَوَّفَ شَيْئاً».
english_text:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “There is no harm if a man recites only Surah al-Fatiha in the first
two rak‘ahs of an obligatory prayer if a need hastens him or he fears something.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.71 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.654 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.40

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ ٱلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ
عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ السَّرِيِّ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَيَقْرَأُ الرَّجُلُ السُّورَةَ الْوَاحِدَةَ فِي
الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْفَرِيضَةِ فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ إِذَا كَانَتْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ثَلاثٍ آيَاتٍ».
فمحمول على أنه يجوز له أن يكررها في الركعة الثانية دون أن يفرقها في الركعتين وهذا إذا لم يحسن غيرها ، فأما مع
التمكن من غيرها فانه يكره ذلك يبين ما ذكرناه :
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Safwan ibn
Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muskan from al-Hasan ibn al-Sarri from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “May a man recite the same Surah in both rak‘ahs of the
obligatory prayer?”
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm if it is more than three verses.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So this is to be interpreted as permitting him to repeat the same Surah in the second
rak‘ah, without splitting it between the two rak‘ahs, and this applies if he does not
know any other Surah. But if he is capable of reciting another one, then it is disliked
(‘makruh’) to do so. What clarifies what we have mentioned is:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.71 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.315 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.675 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.47

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى
بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَقْرَأُ سُورَةً وَاحِدَةً فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْفَرِيضَةِ وَ هُوَ يُحْسِنُ غَيْرَهَا
فَإِنْ فَعَلَ فَمَا عَلَيْهِ قَالَ «إِذَا أَحْسَنَ غَيْرَهَا فَلاَ يَفْعَلْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُحْسِنْ غَيْرَهَا فَلاَ بَأْسَ».
english_text:
What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim
from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother (Imam) Musa ibn Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon them, said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who recites the same Surah in both rak‘ahs of the
obligatory prayer while he is able to recite others, if he does so, is there anything upon
him?
Imam {a.s} said: “If he can recite other than it, then he should not do it. But if he cannot
recite other than it, then there is no harm.”
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
references: Qurb Al-Isnad, Vol.1 p.206 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.71 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.315 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.675 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.47

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ
عَنْ زَيْدِ الشَّحَامِ قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ فَقَرَأَ بِنَا بِالضُّحَى وَ أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ.
فليس في هذا الخبر انه قرأهما في ركعة أو ركعتين، وعندنا انه لا يجوز قراءة هاتين السورتين إلا في ركعة وإذا لم يجز
ذلك حملناه على انه قرأهما في ركعة.
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn
from Fadhala from Husayn from Ibn Muskan from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} led us in prayer and recited for us ‘Surah al- Duha’ and ‘Surah al-
Sharh’.
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
This report does not state whether he recited them in one rak‘ah or in two. According
to our view, it is not permissible to recite these two Surahs (‘al- Duha’ and ‘al-Sharh’)
except in a single rak‘ah. And since it is not permissible to separate them, we interpret
the narration to mean that He {a.s} recited them together in one rak‘ah.
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.72 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.317 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.681 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.54 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.46

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَرَوَى هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضٍ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ زَيْدِ الشَحَامِ قَالَ: صَلَّى أَبُو عَبْدِ
اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ فَقَرَأَ فِي الْأُولَى «وَ الضُّحى» وَ فِي الثَّانِيَةِ «أَ لَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ».
فهذه الرواية تضمنت انه قرأهما في الركعتين إلا انه ليس في الخبر أنه قرأهما في النافلة أو الفريضة وإذا احتمل ذلك
حملناه على النافلة، والذي يكشف عما تأولنا عليه الرواية الاولى رواية :
english_text:
This hadith was also narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from one of our companions
from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} prayed and recited in the first rak‘ah ‘By the morning brightness”
(Surah al-Duha)’ and in the second ‘Did We not expand for you your chest?” (Surah al-
Sharh)’.
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
This narration indicates that he recited them in two rak‘ahs; however, the report does
not specify whether he recited them in a ‘nafila’ (supererogatory) prayer or an
‘obligatory’ one. And since that possibility exists, we interpret it as referring to a
‘nafila’. What clarifies and supports the interpretation we gave for the first narration is
the following narration:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.72 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.682 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.54 • Bihar Al- Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.46

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ الْعَلاءِ عَنْ زَيْدِ الشَّحَامِ قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ الْفَجْرَ فَقَرَأَ » وَ
الضُّحن» وَ «أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ» فِي رَكْعَةٍ.
وأما النوافل فلا بأس أن يجمع الانسان فيها بين سورتين وأكثر من ذلك وأن يفرق السورة الواحدة أيضا ، وقد قدمنا طرفا
مما يدل عليه ، ويزيده بيانا ما رواه :
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala from al-‘Ala’ from Zayd al-Shahham who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} led us in the Fajr prayer, and He {a.s} recited ‘By the morning brightness”
(Surah al-Duha)’ and ‘Did We not expand for you your chest?” (Surah al-Sharh)’ in one
rak‘ah.
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
As for the ‘nawafil’ (supererogatory prayers), there is no harm if a person combines
two Surahs or more within them, or even splits a single Surah. We have already
mentioned some evidence indicating this, and what further clarifies it is what has been
narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.72 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.317 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.88 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.681 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.54 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.46 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.5 p.593 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.1 4 p.316

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
الحسين بن سعيد عن صفوان عن ابن بكير عن زرارة قال قال أبو جعفر عليه السلام : إنما يكره أن يجمع بين
السورتين في الفريضة فاما النافلة فلا بأس.
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “It is only disliked to combine two Surahs in
the obligatory prayer, but as for the ‘nafila’ (supererogatory prayer), there is no harm.”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَقْرُنُ بَيْنَ السُّورَتَيْنِ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ
فَقَالَ «إنَّ لِكُلَّ سُورَةٍ حَقَاً فَأَعْطِهَا حَقَّهَا مِنَ الرُكُوعِ وَ السُّجُودِ» قُلْتُ فَيَقْطَعُ السُورَةَ فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِهِ».
english_text:
And from him, from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who joins two Surahs in one rak‘ah.
Imam {a.s} said: “Every Surah has a right, so give it its due in bowing and prostration.”
I asked: “What if he cuts the Surah (splits it)?”
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm in that.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.73 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.680 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.50

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ ٱلْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ عَبْدا صَالِحاً عَ هَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُقْرَأَ فِي صَلاةِ اللَّيْلِ بِالسُورَتَيْنِ وَ الثَّلاَثِ
فَقَالَ «مَا كَانَ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اللَّيْلِ فَاقْرَأْ بِالسُّورَتَيْنِ وَ الثَّلاَثِ وَ مَا كَانَ مِنْ صَلاَةِ النَّهَارِ فَلاَ تَقْرَأ إلاَّ بِسُورَةٍ سُورَةِ».
english_text:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim who said:
I asked the Righteous servant (Abd Salih {a.s}), peace be upon him: “Is it permissible to
recite two or three Surahs in the night prayer?”
Imam {a.s} said: “As for the night prayer, recite two or three Surahs. But as for the
daytime prayer, do not recite except one Surah (in each rak‘ah).”
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.73 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.680 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.50

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عُثُمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ
الله عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لا بَأْسَ أَنْ تَجْمَعَ فِي النَّافِلَةِ مِنَ السُّوَرِ مَا شِئُتَ».
english_text:
Sa‘d from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Abdullah ibn Abi
Ya‘fur:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “There is no harm in combining as many Surahs as you wish in
the ‘nafila’ (supererogatory prayer).”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.73 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.681 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.51 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.93

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَعَنَهُ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَمَّنْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَلاَمُ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ هَلْ تُقْسَمُ السُّورَةُ فِي رَكْعَنَيْنِ فَقَالَ «نَعَمِ اِقْسِمْهَا كَيْفَ شِئْتَ».
english_text:
And from him, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadhala ibn Ayyub from Aban ibn Uthman from someone who
informed him from one of the two (Imams), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him {a.s}: “May a Surah be divided between two rak‘ahs?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, divide it however you wish.”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.73 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.676 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.44

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ الطَّوِيلِ عَنْ أَبِي دَاوُدَ الْمُنْشِدِ عَنْ مُحَسِّنِ الْمِيثَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي
عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «تَقْرَأَ فِي صَلاَةِ ٱلزَّوَالِ فِي الرَكْعَةِ الْأُولَى الْحَمْدَ وَ «قُلْ هُوَ اللهُ أُحَدٌ» وَ فِي الرَكْعَةِ
الثَّانِيَةِ الْحَمْدَ وَ «قُلْ يَا أَيْهَا الْكَافِرُونَ» وَ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الثَالِثَةِ الْحَمْدَ وَ «قُلْ هُوَ اللهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ وَ فِي
الرَّكْعَةِ الرَّابِعَةِ الْحَمْدَ وَ «قُلْ هُوَ اللهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ آخِرَ الْبَقَرَةِ «آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ » إِلَى آخِرِهَا وَ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الْخَامِسَةِ الْحَمْدَ
وَ «قُلْ هُوَ اللهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ الْخَمْسَ آيَاتٍ مِنْ آلِ عِمْرَانَ «إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السِّمَاوَاتِ وَ ٱلْأَرْضِ» إلَى قَوْلِهِ «إِنَّكَ لا تُخْلِفُ
الْمِيعَادَ» وَ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ السَّادِسَةِ الْحَمْدَ وَ «قُلْ هُوَ اللهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ ثَلاَثَ آيَاتِ السِّخْرَةِ «إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللهُ اَلَّذِي خَلَقَ
السِّمَاوَاتِ وَ الأَرْضَ» إِلَى قَوْلِهِ «إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ اللهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ» وَ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ الْحَمْدَ وَ «قُلْ هُوَ
اللهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ الايَاتِ مِنْ سُورَةِ الْأَنْعَامِ «وَ جَعَلُوا لِلهِ شُرَكَاءَ الْجِنَّ» إلَى قَوْلِهِ «وَ هُوَ اللَّطِيفُ الْخَبِيرُ» وَ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ
الثَامِنَةِ الْحَمْدَ وَ «قُلْ هُوَ اللهُ» وَ آخِرَ سُورَةِ اَلْحَشْرِ مِنْ قَوْلِهِ «لَوْ أَنْزَلْنَا هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ عَلى جَبَلٍ» إِلَى آخِرِهَا فَإِذَا
فَرَغْتَ قُلْتَ اللَّهُمَّ مُقَلَّبَ الْقُلُوبِ وَ الْأَبْصَارِ ثَبِّثْ قَلْبِي عَلَى دِينِكَ وَ لا تُزِغْ قَلْبِي بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنِي وَ هَبْ لِي «مِنْ
لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَابُ» سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ ثُمَّ تَقُولُ أَسْتَجِيرُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ النَّارِ سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ».
english_text:
IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn al-Tawil from Abu Dawud al-Munshid from
Muhassin al-Mithami:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “In ‘Zawal’ prayer (midday supererogatory), you recite in:
- The first rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas),
- The second rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun),
- The third rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and Ayat al-Kursi,
- The fourth rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and the end of Surah al-
Baqarah ‘Amana al-rasulu...’ to its end,
- The fifth rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and five verses from Aal ‘Imran
starting from ‘Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...’ to ‘Indeed, You
do not break the promise,’
- The sixth rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and three verses of Surah al-
A‘raf starting from ‘Indeed, your Lord is Allah {SWT} who created the heavens and the
earth...’ to ‘Indeed, the mercy of Allah {SWT} is near to the doers of good,’
- The seventh rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and the verses from Surah
al-An‘am ‘And they assigned to Allah {SWT} partners of the jinn...’ to ‘And He is the
Subtle, the All-Aware,’
- The eighth rak‘ah: al-Hamd and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’, and the end of Surah al-
Hashr from ‘If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain...’ to its end.
Then when you finish, you say:
‘O Allah {SWT}, Turner of hearts and sights, make my heart firm upon Your {SWT} religion,
and do not let my heart deviate after You {SWT} have guided me, and grant me from
Yourself {SWT} mercy, indeed, You {SWT} are the Bestower’, seven times.
Then you say: ‘I seek refuge with Allah {SWT} from the Fire’, seven times.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.73 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.666 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.63

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ حَدْثَنِي مُعَاذُ بْنُ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ
اَللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لا تَدَعْ أَنْ تَقْرَأْ بٍ «قُلْ هُوَ اللهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ «قُلْ يَا أَيْهَا الْكَافِرُونَ» فِي سَبْعِ مَوَاطِنَ فِي
اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ وَ رَكْعَتَي الزَّوَالِ وَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ بَعْدَ الْمَغْرِبِ وَ رَكْعَتَيْنٍ فِي أَوْلِ صَلَاَةِ اللَّيْلِ وَ رَكْعَتَي الْإِحْرَامِ وَ
الْفَجْرِ إِذَا أَصْبَحْتَ بِهِمَا وَ رَكْعَتَي الطَّوَافِ».
english_text:
IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah who said: Mu‘adh
ibn Muslim narrated to me:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “Do not leave off reciting ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-
Ikhlas) and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun) in seven places:
- In the two rak‘ahs before Fajr,
- The two rak‘ahs of Zawal (midday supererogatory prayer),
- The two rak‘ahs after Maghrib,
- The first two rak‘ahs of the Night Prayer (‘Salat al-Layl’),
- The two rak‘ahs of ‘Ihram’ (entering prayer),
- The two rak‘ahs of Fajr if you begin your day with them,
- The two rak‘ahs of ‘Tawaf’ (circumambulation).”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Khisal, Vol.2 p.347 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.74 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.665 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.65 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.31 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.5 p.687 • Tafsir Kanz Al- Daqaiq, Vol.1 4 p.471 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.4 p.173

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَ فِي رِوَايَةِ أُخْرَى : «يُقْرَأُ فِي هَذَا كُلَّهِ بِ «قُلْ هُوَ آللَهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ فِي الثَانِيَةِ بِ «قُلْ يَا أَيُهَا الكَافِرُونَ» إلاّ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ
قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ فَإِنَّهُ يُبْدَأَ بٍ «قُلْ يا أَيْهَا الْكَافِرُونَ» ثُمَّ يُقْرَأَ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الثَانِيَةِ «قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ» ».
english_text:
And in another narration: “In all of these (prayers), ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ is recited
in the first rak‘ah and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ in the second, except in the two rak‘ahs
before Fajr, in which ‘Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun’ is recited first, and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu
Ahad’ is recited in the second rak‘ah.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.74 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.1 4 p.471

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ آللّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ
قَالَ: «إِذَا كُنْتَ خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ فَقَرَأَ الْحَمْدَ وَ فَرَغَ مِنْ قِرَاءَتِهَا فَقُلْ أَنْتَ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبَّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ وَ لا تَقُلْ آمِينَ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Jamil:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “If you are behind an imam and he recites al-Hamd (Surah al-
Fatiha) and finishes its recitation, then you say: ‘Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin’ (All
praise is due to Allah {SWT}, Lord of the worlds), and do not say ‘Amin’.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.313 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.74 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.318 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.657 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.67 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.25 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.1 p.87

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ الْحَلَبِيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ
أَقُولُ إِذَا قَرَغْتُ مِنْ فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ آمِينَ قَالَ «لا».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “Should I say ‘Amin’ when I finish reciting Surah al-Fatiha?”
Imam {a.s} said: “No.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.74 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.318 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.657 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.67 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.1 p.87

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنْ قَوْلٍ
النَّاسِ فِي الصَّلاةِ جَمَاعَةً جِينَ تُقْرَأُ فَاتِحَةُ الْكِتَابِ آمِينَ قَالَ «مَا أَحْسَنَهَا وَ اِخْفِضِ الصَّوْتَ بِهَا».
فاول ما فيه ان جميلا قد روى ضد ذلك وهو ما قدمناه من قوله ولا تقل آمين بل قل الحمد اللّٰه رب العالمين وإذا كان قد
اروى ضد ذلك وما ينقض هذه الرواية ويوافق رواية غيره فيجب الحكم على فساد هذه الرواية التي انفرد بها دون ما
شاركه فيها غيره ولو صح هذا الخبر لكان محمولا على التقية ، والذي يدل على ذلك ما رواه:
english_text:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about the people saying ‘Amin’ together in prayer when Surah
al-Fatiha is recited.
He said: “How beautiful it is, but lower your voice with it.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The first issue with this is that Jamil has himself narrated the opposite, as we have
mentioned earlier, his statement: ‘Do not say Amin, rather say: al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-
‘alamin.”’ And since he has narrated the contrary of this and what contradicts the
current narration and agrees with the narrations of others, it is necessary to judge this
solitary narration as invalid, especially since no one else has reported it alongside him.
And even if this report were to be authentic, it would be interpreted as having been
said under ‘taqiyyah’ (dissimulation). What indicates this is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.75 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.318 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.657 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.68

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ أَقُولُ آمِينَ إِذَا
قَالَ الْإِمَامُ «غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَ لا الضَّالِّينَ» قَالَ «هُمُ ٱلْيَهُودُ وَ النَّصَارَى وَ لَمْ يُجِبُ فِي هَذَا».
فعدوله عليه السلام عن جواب ما سأله السائل عنه دليل على كراهية هذه اللفظة ولم يتمكن من التصريح بكراهيته للتقية
والاضطرار فعدل عن جوابه جملة.
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “Should I say ‘Amin’ when the imam (of prayer) says: ‘ghayril-
maghdubi ‘alayhim wa lad-dallin’?”
Imam {a.s} said: “They are the Jews and the Christians.”
And He {a.s} did not respond regarding this (He {a.s} gave no ruling about saying ‘Amin’).
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
His (peace be upon him) avoidance of answering what the questioner directly asked is
an indication of the dislike (‘karahah’) of this phrase (‘Amin’), and He {a.s} was not able
to explicitly declare its dislike due to ‘taqiyyah’ (precautionary dissimulation) and
necessity, so He {a.s} entirely refrained from answering the question.
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.75 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.319 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.657 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.67 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.25 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.1 p.83

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ يَرْفَعُ يَدَيْهِ إِذَا
رَكَعَ وَ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ وَ إِذَا سَجَدَ وَ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ السُّجُودِ وَ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ الثَّانِيَةَ.
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah {a.s} raising his hands when He {a.s} bowed (for ‘ruku’), and when He
{a.s} raised his head from bowing, and when He {a.s} prostrated (‘sujud’), and when He {a.s}
raised his head from prostration, and when He {a.s} intended to go into the second
prostration.
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.75 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.704 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.296 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.114

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّد بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: فِي الرَّجْلِ
يَرْفَعُ يَدَهُ كُلَّمَا أَهْوَى لِلرُكُوعِ وَ السُّجُودِ وَ كُلّمَا رَفَعَ رَاْسَهُ مِنْ رُكُوعِ أَوْ سُجُودٍ قَالَ «هِيَ الْعُبُودِيَّةُ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Ibn Muskan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said regarding a man who raises his hands whenever he goes down
for bowing (‘ruku’) and prostration (‘sujud’), and whenever he raises his head from
bowing or prostration.
Imam {a.s} said: “It is servitude (‘al-‘ubudiyyah’).”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.75 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.704 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.297 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.114

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَعَنْهُ عَنِ ٱلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مُوسَى الْوَرْاقِ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ : رَفْعْكَ يَدَيْكَ فِي الصَّلاَةِ زِينَتُهَا.
english_text:
And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Musa al-Warraq from Yunus from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Hariz from Zurarah
who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “Your raising of your hands in prayer is its adornment.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.76 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.704 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.297

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ وَ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ خَالِدِ ٱلْبَرْقِيّ وَ ٱلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ
مَغْرُوفٍ عَنِ ٱلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ التَّسْبِيحِ فِي الرُّكُوعِ وَ
السُّجُود فَقَالَ يَقُولُ فِي الرُّكُوعِ « سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ اَلْعَظِيمِ وَ فِي السُّجُودِ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى الْفَرِيضَةُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ
تَسْبِيحَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ وَ السِّنَّةُ ثَلاَثُ وَ الْفَضْلُ فِي سَبْعٍ».
english_text:
Sa‘d ibn Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, and Muhammad ibn Khalid
al-Barqi, and al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from Hisham ibn Salim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about the ‘tasbih’ in ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’.
Imam {a.s} said: “In ‘ruku’, say: ‘Subhana Rabbiyal-‘Azim (Glory be to my Lord {AZJ}, the
Great)’, and in ‘sujud’, say: ‘Subhana Rabbiyal-A‘la (Glory be to my Lord {AZJ}, the Most
High)’. The obligation in that is one ‘tasbih’, the Sunnah is three, and the excellence is
in saying it seven times.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.76 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.81 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.322 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.92 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.704 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.299

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَعَنَهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ الرِّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ
عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَا يُجْزِي مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ فِي الرُكُوعِ
وَ السُّجُودِ فَقَالَ «ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ فِي تَرَسُلٍ وَ وَاحِدَةُ تَامَّةً تُجْزِي».
english_text:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-
Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdullah from Zurarah from Abu Ja‘far {a.s} (peace be
upon him), he said:
I said to Him {a.s}: “What suffices in terms of what is to be said in ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Three ‘tasbihat’ with calm recitation (‘tarassul’), and one complete
(tasbihah) suffices.”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.76 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.323 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.705 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.299

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَعَثَهُ عَنْ أَيُوبَ بَنِ نُوحِ النَّخَعِيّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَبِي ٱلْحَسَنِ ٱلْأَوَّلِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ
قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ الرُكُوعِ وَ السَّجُودِ كَمْ يُجْزِي فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلتَّسْبِيحِ فَقَالَ «ثَلاَثَةٌ وَ تُجْزِيكَ وَاحِدَةً إِذَا أَمْكَنْتَ جَبْهَتَكَ
مِنَ الْأَرْضِ».
english_text:
And from him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh al-Nakha‘i from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu
al-Hasan al-Awwal {a.s} (peace be upon him), he said:
I asked Him {a.s} about ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’, how much ‘tasbih’ suffices in them?
Imam {a.s} said: “Three, and one suffices you if you have firmly placed your forehead on
the ground.”
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.76 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.705 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.300

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَجِيهِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيَ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَسْجُدُ كَمْ يُجْزِيهِ مِنَ التَّسْبِيحِ فِي رُكُوعِهِ وَ سُجُودِهِ فَقَالَ «ثَلاثُ وَ تُجْزِيهِ
وَاحِدَةٌ».
english_text:
And from him, from Abu Ja‘far from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin
from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), he said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man in ‘sujud’, how much ‘tasbih’ suffices him in his ‘ruku’ and
‘sujud’?
Imam {a.s} said: “Three, and one suffices him.”
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.76 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.323 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.706 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.300

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ أَبِي الصُهْبَانِ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ مِسْمَعٍ أَبِي سَيَّارٍ عَنْ
أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «يُجْزِيكَ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ فِي الرُّكُوعِ وَ السُّجُودِ ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ أَوْ قَدْرُهُنَّ مُتَرَسِّلاً وَ
لَيْسَ لَهُ وَ لا كَرَامَةَ أَنْ يَقُولَ سُبْحَ سُبْحَ سُبْحَ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran
from Misma‘ Abi Sayyar:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “It suffices you in ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’ to say three ‘tasbihat’, or
their equivalent with calm and clear recitation (‘tarassul’). But it is of no value, nor
does it hold any merit, for one to say: ‘Subh... Subh... Subh’ (in a hurried manner).”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.77 • Al-Sarair, Vol.3 p.602 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.706 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.302 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.115

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ الرُّكُوعِ وَ السُّجُودِ هَلْ
نَزَلَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ قَوْلُ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ «يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اِرْكَعُوا وَ أُسْجُدُوا» » فَقُلْتُ كَيْفَ حَدْ ٱلرُّكُوعِ
وَ السَّجُودِ فَقَالَ «أَمّا مَا يُجْزِيكَ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ فَثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ تَقُولُ سُبْحَانَ اللّهِ سُبْحَانَ اللّهِ ثَلاَثاً وَ مَنْ كَانَ
يَقْوَى عَلَى أَنْ يُطَوِّلَ الرُّكُوعَ وَ السُّجَودَ فَلْيُطَوَّلْ مَا اِسْتَطَاعَ يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ فِي تَسْبِيحِ اللّهِ وَ تَحْمِيدِهِ وَ تَمْجِيدِهِ وَ
الدُّعَاءٍ وَ التَّضَرُّع فَإِنَّ أَقْرَبَ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ إِلَى رَبِّهِ وَ هُوَ سَاجِدٌ فَأَمّا ٱلْإِمَامُ فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا قَامَ بِالنَّاسِ فَلاَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ
يُطَوِّلَ بِهِمْ فَإِنَّ فِي النَّاسِ الضَّعِيفَ وَ مَنْ لَهُ الْحَاجَةُ فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللّهِ صَلِّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ كَانَ إِذَا صَلِّى بِالنَّاسِ
خَفَّ بِهِمْ».
english_text:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from al-Husayn from al-Hasan from Zur‘ah from Sama‘ah who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’, whether they were mentioned in the Qur’an.
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, in the words of Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic: ‘O you who believe,
bow and prostrate’.” (Surah Hajj 22:77)
I asked: “What is the minimum required for ‘ruku’ and ‘sujud’?”
Imam {a.s} said: “As for what suffices you in ‘ruku’, it is to say three ‘tasbihat’, ‘Subhan
Allah, Subhan Allah’ three times. And whoever is able to lengthen the ‘ruku’ and
‘sujud’, let him lengthen them as much as he is able. That should be in glorifying Allah
{SWT}, praising Him {SWT}, magnifying Him {SWT}, supplicating, and showing humility, for the
closest a servant is to his Lord {AZJ} is when he is in ‘sujud’.
As for the imam (of prayer), when he leads the people in prayer, he should not prolong
it for them, for among them are the weak and those who have needs. Indeed, the
Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, used to lighten the prayer
when leading the people.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.77 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.706 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.3 p.910

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَعَنَهُ عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَ أَخَفٌ مَا يَكُونُ
مِنَ التَّسْبِيحِ فِي الصَّلاَةِ قَالَ «ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ مُتَرَسَّلاً تَقُولُ سُبْحَانَ اللّهِ سُبْحَانَ اللّهِ سُبْحَانَ اللهِ ».
english_text:
And from him, from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “What is the lightest (minimum) amount of ‘tasbih’ in
prayer?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Three ‘tasbihat’ with calm and clear recitation (‘tarassul’), saying:
‘Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah, Subhan Allah’.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.77 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.324 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.707 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.303

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلامُ قَالَ: «إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَرْكَعَ فَقُلْ وَ أَنْتَ مُنتَصِبٌ - اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ ثُمَّ اِرْكَغْ وَ قُلْ رَبِّ لَكَ رَكَفْتُ وَ لَكَ أَسْلَمْتُ وَ بِكَ
آَمَنْتُ وَ عَلَيْكَ تَوَكِّلْتُ وَ أَنْتَ رَبِّي خَشَعَ لَكَ سَمْعِي وَ بَصَرِي وَ شَعْرِي وَ بَشَرِي وَ لَحْمِي وَ دَمِي وَ مُخَي وَ عَصَبِي
وَ عِظَامِي وَ مَا أَقَلَّثهُ قَدَمَايَ غَيْرَ مُسْتَنْكِفٍ وَ لا مُسْتَكْبِرٍ وَ لاَ مُسْتَحْسِرٍ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ وَ بِحَمْدِهِ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ
فِي تَرَسُلٍ وَ تَصُفُّ فِي رُكُوعِكَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْكَ تَجْعَلُ بَيْنَهُمَا قَدْرَ شِبْرٍ وَ تُمَكِّنُ رَاحَتَيْكَ مِنْ رُكْبَنَيْكَ وَ تَضَّعُ يَدَكَ
الْيُمْنَى عَلَى رُكْبَتِكَ الْيُمْنَى قَبْلَ الْيُسْرَى وَ تَلْقُمُ بِأَطْرَافِ أَصَابِعِكَ عَيْنَ الرُّكْبَةِ وَ فَرِّجْ أَصَابِعَكَ إِذَا وَضَعْتَهَا عَلَى
رُكْبَتَيْكَ وَ أَقِمْ صُلْبَكَ وَ مُدَّ عُنُقَكَ وَ لَيَكُنْ نَظَرُكَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْكَ ثُمَّ قُلْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ وَ أَنْتَ مُنْتَصِبٌ قَائِمٌ
«الْحَمْدُ لِلهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ» أَهلَ ٱلْجَبَرُوتِ وَ ٱلْكِبْرِيَاءِ وَ ٱلْعَظَمَةِ «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ» تَجْهَرُ بِهَا صَوْتَكَ ثُمَّ تَرْفَعُ
يَدَيْكَ بالتَّكْبِيرٍ وَ تَخِرُ سَاجِداً».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Hariz from
Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “When you intend to go into bowing (ruku‘),
say while you are standing upright: ‘Allahu Akbar’, then bow and say:
‘My Lord {AZJ}, for You {AZJ} have I bowed, to You {AZJ} have I submitted, in You {AZJ} have I
believed, upon You {AZJ} have I relied, and You {AZJ} are my Lord {AZJ}. My hearing, my sight,
my hair, my skin, my flesh, my blood, my brain, my nerves, my bones, and everything
my feet carry have humbled themselves to You {AZJ}, not arrogantly, nor proudly, nor
with weariness. Glory be to my Lord {AZJ}, the Mighty, and praise be to Him {AZJ}’, three
times, in a calm and deliberate manner (tarassul).
And in your bowing, align your feet, placing between them the distance of one span.
Place your palms firmly on your knees. Put your right hand on your right knee before
the left, press the tips of your fingers on the center of the kneecap, and spread your
fingers when placing them on your knees. Keep your back straight and extend your
neck, and let your gaze be between your feet.
IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
Then say: ‘Sami‘a Allahu liman hamidah’ (Allah {SWT} hears the one who praises Him
{AZJ}), while you are upright standing, and say: ‘Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin’ (Praise
be to Allah {SWT}, the Lord of the worlds), the One worthy of majesty, sovereignty, and
greatness. ‘Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil-‘alamin’, say it aloud.
Then raise your hands with the takbir and go down into prostration (sujud).”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.319 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.77 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.701 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.295

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا رَفَعْتَ
رَأْسَكَ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ فَأْقِمْ صُلْبَكَ فَإِنَّهُ لا صَلاَةَ لِمَنْ لاَ يُقِيمُ صُلْبَهُ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from a man from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “When you raise your head from bowing (ruku‘), straighten your
back, for there is no prayer for the one who does not straighten his back.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.320 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.78 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.703 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.321

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ الْعَلَاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَضَّعُ يَدَيْهِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ
إِذَا سَجَدَ وَ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَقُومَ رَفَعَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ قَبْلَ يَدَيْهِ.
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah {a.s} placing his hands before his knees when He {a.s} went into
prostration (sujud), and when He {a.s} wanted to rise, He {a.s} would raise his knees before
his hands.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.78 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.713 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.337

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَ عَنَهُ عَنِ ٱلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ ٱلْجَوْهَرِيّ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْعَلاءِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنِ ٱلرَّجُلِ
يَضَعُ يَدَيْهِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ فِي الصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ».
english_text:
And from him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-‘Ala’, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who places his hands before his knees during
prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes (it is permissible).”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.78 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.325 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.713 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.338

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَضَعُ يَدَيْهِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ قَبْلَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ قَالَ
«نَعَمْ» يَعْنِي فِي الصَّلاَةِ.
english_text:
And from him, from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
He {a.s} was asked about a man who places his hands on the ground before his knees.
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes,” meaning in prayer.
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.78 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.326 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.713 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.337

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ
قَالَ: «لا بَأْسَ إِذَا صَلَّى الرَّجُلُ أَنْ يَضَعَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ قَبْلَ يَدَيْهِ».
فانه محمول على حال الضرورة ومن لا يتمكن من تلقي الارض باليدين أولا لعلة أو مرض.
english_text:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Husayn from Sama‘ah from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “There is no harm if a man, when praying, places his knees on
the ground before his hands.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
For it is to be understood as applying to a case of necessity, and to one who is unable
to touch the ground with his hands first due to an ailment or illness.
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.78

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثُمَانَ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ
اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: «إِذَا سَجَدْتَ فَكَبِّرْ وَ قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ سَجَدْتُ وَ بِكَ آمَنْتُ وَ لَكَ أَسْلَمْتُ وَ عَلَيْكَ تَوَكِّلْتُ وَ أَنْتَ
رَبِّي سَجَدَ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي خَلَقَهُ وَ شَقَّ سَمْعَهُ وَ بَصَرَهُ «وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ» تَبَارَكَ «اللهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ» ثُمَّ
قُلْ سُبْحَانَ رَبَّيَ الْأَعْلَى وَ بِحَمْدِهِ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ فَإِذَا رَفَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ فَقُلْ بَيْنَ السَّجْدَتَيْنِ اللَّهُمَّ اِغْفِرْ لِي وَ اِرْحَمْنِي وَ
أُجْبُرْنِي وَ اِدْفَعْ عَنِّي وَ عَافِنِي «إِنِّي لِمَا أَنْزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ» «تَبْارَكَ اللَهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ» ».
english_text:
IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman
from al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “When you go into prostration (sujud), say the takbir (Allahu
Akbar), and say: ‘O Allah {SWT}, to You {AZJ} I have prostrated, in You {AZJ} I have believed, to
You {AZJ} I have submitted, upon You {AZJ} I have relied. You {AZJ} are my Lord {AZJ}. My face
has prostrated to the One {AZJ} who created it, and who split open its hearing and sight.’
‘All praise belongs to Allah {SWT}, Lord {AZJ} of the worlds.’ ‘Blessed is Allah {SWT}, the best
of creators.’
Then say: ‘Glory be to my Lord {AZJ}, the Most High, and with His {AZJ} praise,’ three times.
Then when you raise your head, say between the two prostrations: ‘O Allah {SWT}, forgive
me, have mercy on me, mend me, repel from me (what harms me), and grant me well-
being. Indeed, I am in need of whatever good You {AZJ} may send down to me.’ ‘Blessed
is Allah {SWT}, Lord {AZJ} of the worlds.’”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.321 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.79 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.711 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.339

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ جَمَاعَةٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ
سِئَانٍ عَنْ حَفْص الْأَعْوَرِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلَامُ قَالَ: «كَانَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ إِذَا سَجَدَ يَتَخَوْى كَمَا يَتَخَوَّى
اَلْبَعِيرُ الضَامِرُ يَغِنِي بُرُوكَهُ».
فان قيل قد ذكرتم من الروايات ما يتضمن جواز الاقتصار على تسبيحة واحدة في الركوع والسجود، وقد روى الحسين
بن سعيد وغيره ما يدفعكم عن ذلك.
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from a group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Fadalah
ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Hafs al-A‘war:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “When (Imam) Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, performed
prostration, He {a.s} would collapse as the emaciated camel collapses, meaning the
way it kneels down.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib al-Murtadha {a.s}
commentary:
If it is said: You have mentioned narrations that include the permissibility of limiting
oneself to a single tasbihah (saying "Subhan Allah") in bowing and prostration, while
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id and others have narrated what repels you from that: (see following
narration)
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.321 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.79 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.712 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.341

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
رَوَى الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مِسْمَعِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: «لا يُجْزِي الرَّجُلَ فِي صَلاتِهِ
أَقَلُّ مِنْ ثَلاثِ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ أَوْ قَدْرِهِنَّ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id narrated from Safwan, from Misma‘:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “It does not suffice a man in his prayer with less than three
tasbihat or their equivalent.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.79 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.323 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.707 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.303

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَعَنْهُ عَنِ النَّضْرِ عَنْ يَحْيَى الْحَلَبِيّ عَنْ دَاوُدَ ٱلْأَبْزَارِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱَلسَّلامُ قَالَ: «أَدْنَى التَسْبِيحِ ثَلاَثُ
مَرَّاتٍ وَ أَنْتَ سَاجِدٌ لاَ تَعْجَلْ بِهِنَّ».
english_text:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Dawud al-Abzari:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: “The minimum of tasbih is three times while you are in
prostration, do not hasten through them.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.79 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.323 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.714 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.303

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ أَدْنَى مَا يُجْزِي مِنَ التَّسْبِيحِ فِي الرُّكُوعِ
وَ السُّجُودِ فَقَالَ «ثَلاَثُ تَسْبِيحَاتٍ».
فكيف تجمعون بين هذه الاخبار؟ قيل له : أول ما نقول أنا لا نجوز ان يقتصر الانسان على مرة واحدة من التسبيح مع
الاختيار وإنما جوزنا ذلك عند الضرورة والاعذار فاما مع الاختيار فلا يجوز ذلك ولانا إنما جوزنا الاقتصار على مرة واحدة
إذا ذكر تسبيحا مخصوصا وهو أن يقول: (سبحان ربي العظيم وبحمده) في الركوع أو (سبحان ربي الاعلى وبحمده) في
السحود فاما اذا قال : (سحان الله) فحسب فلا بحون اقا من ثلاث مرات وايضا لس ف شء من هذه الاخيار ان م.
english_text:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the minimum that suffices of tasbih in bowing and prostration.
Imam {a.s} said: “Three tasbihat.”
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
commentary:
So how do you reconcile these reports? It was said to him: The first thing we say is that
we do not permit a person to suffice with only one tasbih when they have the ability to
do more; rather, we only allowed that in cases of necessity and valid excuses. As for
when there is ability and choice, then that is not permitted.
And we only permitted limiting it to one tasbih when a specific phrase is mentioned,
which is to say: ‘Subhana Rabbi al-‘Azim wa bi-hamdih’ in bowing, or ‘Subhana Rabbi
al-A‘la wa bi-hamdih’ in prostration. But if one says only ‘Subhan Allah’, then it is not
permissible to say it less than three times.
Also, none of these reports state that whoever does less than three tasbihat, then his
prayer is invalid. It is possible that what was meant by them was the negation of
perfection and merit, not invalidation. And what clarifies what we have mentioned is:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.80 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.323 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.707 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.303

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ الْحَضْرَمِيَّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ
لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ أَيْ شَيْءٍ حَدُّ الرُكُوعِ وَ السُّجُودِ قَالَ «تَقُولُ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ وَ بِحَمْدِهِ ثَلاثاً فِي
اَلرُكُوعِ وَ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى وَ بِحَمْدِهِ ثَلاَثاً فِي السُّجُودِ فَمَنْ نَقَصَ وَاحِدَةً نَقَصَ ثُلُثَ صَلاَتِهِ وَ مَنْ نَقَصَ اِثْنَتَيْنِ
نَقَصَ ثُلْثَيْ صَلاَتِهِ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يُسَبِّحْ فَلاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ».
فدل هذا الخبر على أنهم إنما نفوا الكمال والفضل ألا ترى انهم قالوا من نقص واحدة نقص ثلث صلاته ومن نقص اثنتين
نقص ثلثي صلاته فلو لا أن الامر على ما ذكرناه كان لا فرق بين الاخلال بواحدة في أن ذلك يبطل الصلاة وبين الاخلال
بالجميع الذي يبطل الصلاة وقد علمنا انهم فرقوا ، مع انا قد بينا فيما تقدم من الاخبار ما يصرح بان الواحدة فريضة وما
زاد عليه مسنون وهو رواية هشام بن سالم حين سأل أبا عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام عن التسبيح فقال له تقول : (سبحان ربي
العظيم) ف الكوع وف السحود (سحان اي الاعل ) ثم قال الفريضة من ذلك تسحة والسنة ثلاث والفضا ف سبع
english_text:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Uthman ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu
Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
I said to (Imam) Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him: “What is the limit of bowing and
prostration?”
Imam {a.s} said: “You say ‘Subhana Rabbi al-‘Azim wa bi-hamdih’ three times in bowing,
and ‘Subhana Rabbi al-A‘la wa bi-hamdih’ three times in prostration. So whoever
omits one has omitted one-third of his prayer, and whoever omits two has omitted
two-thirds of his prayer, and whoever does not perform tasbih, then he has no prayer.”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
commentary:
So this report indicates that they only intended to negate perfection and merit. Do you
not see that they said: whoever omits one has omitted a third of his prayer, and
whoever omits two has omitted two-thirds of his prayer? If the matter were not as we
have mentioned, then there would be no difference between failing to say one tasbih,
which, according to that interpretation, would invalidate the prayer, and failing to say
all of them, which indeed does invalidate the prayer. And yet, we know that they made
a distinction.
Moreover, we have already clarified in previous narrations what explicitly states that
one tasbih is obligatory, and whatever is beyond that is recommended. This is in the
narration of Hisham ibn Salim when he asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about the tasbih, and
Imam {a.s} said to him: You say ‘Subhana Rabbi al-‘Azim’ in bowing and ‘Subhana Rabbi
al-A’la’ in prostration. Then Imam {a.s} said: The obligation of that is one tasbih, the
sunnah is three, and the merit is in seven, and this is explicit in what we have said.
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.80 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.324 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.300

Chapter Title: THE MANNER OF PRAYER, EXPLANATION OF THE FIFTY-ONE RAK‘AHS; THE ORDER, RECITATION, TASBIH IN BOWING AND PROSTRATION, QUNUT, AND WHAT IS OBLIGATORY AND RECOMMENDED THEREIN
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَوْماً
«يَا حَمَّادُ تُحْسِنُ أَنْ تُصَلَّيَ» قَالَ فَقُلْتُ يَا سَيَّدِي أَنَا أَحْفَظُ كِتَابَ حَرِيزٍ فِي الصَّلاةِ فَقَالَ «لاَ عَلَيْكَ يَا حَمَّادُ قُمْ
فَصَلِّ» قَالَ فَقُمْتُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مُتَوَجِّها إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ فَاسْتَفْتَحْتُ الصّلاَةَ فَرَكَعْتُ وَ سَجَدْتُ فَقَالَ «يَا حَمَادُ لاَ تُحْسِنُ
أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ مَا أَقْبَحَ بِالرَّجُلِ مِنْكُمْ يَأْتِي عَلَيْهِ سِتُونَ سَنَةً أَوْ سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً فَلاَ يُقِيمُ صَلاَةً وَاحِدَةً بِحُدُودِهَا تَامَّةً)
قَالَ حَمَّادٌ فَأَصَابَنِي فِي نَفْسِي الذُّلُ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتْ فِدَاكَ فَعَلَّمْنِي الصَّلاةَ فَقَامَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلَامُ مُسْتَقْبِلَ
اَلْقِبْلَةِ مُنْتَصِباً فَأَرْسَلَ يَدَيْهِ جَمِيعاً عَلَى فَخِذَيْهِ قَدْ ضَمَّ أَصَابِعَهُ وَ قَرَّبَ بَيْنَ قَدَمَيْهِ حَتَّى كَانَ بَيْنَهُمَا قَدْرُ ثَلاَثِ
أَصَابِعَ مُنْفَرِجَاتٍ وَ اِسْتَقْبَلَ بِأَصَابِعِ رِجْلَيْهِ جَمِيعاً الْقِبْلَةَ لَمْ يُحَرِّفُهَا عَنِ الْقِبْلَةِ وَ قَالَ بِخَشوعِ « اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ » ثُمَّ قَرَأَ
الْحَمْدَ بِتَرْتِيلٍ وَ «قُل هُوَ اللهُ أَحَدٌ» ثُمَّ صَبَرَ هُنَيْئَةً بِقَدْرِ مَا يَتَنَفَسُ وَ هَوَ قَائِمٌ ثُمَّ رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ جِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ وَ قَالَ
« اللهُ أَكْبَرُ » وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ ثُمَّ رَكَعَ وَ مَلَاً كَفَّيْهِ مِنْ رُكْبَتَيْهِ مُنْفَرِجَاتٍ وَ رَدَّ رُكْبَتَيْهِ إِلَى خَلْفِهِ ثُمَّ اِسْتَوَى ظَهْرُهُ حَتَّى
لَوْصُبَّ عَلَيْهِ قَطْرَةٌ مِنْ مَاءِ أَوْ دُهْنٍ لَمْ تَزُلُ لإِسْتِوَاءِ ظَهْرِهِ وَ مَدَّ عُنْقَهُ وَ غَمَّضَ عَيْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ سَبَّحَ ثَلاَثاً بِتَرْتِيلٍ فَقَالَ
« سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ وَ بِحَمْدِهِ » ثُمَّ اِسْتَوَى قَائِماً فَلَمَّا اِسْتَمْكَنَ مِنَ الْقِيَامِ قَالَ » سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ » ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ
وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ جِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ ثُمّ سَجَدَ وَ بَسَطَ كَفَّيْهِ مَضْمُومَتَي الْأَصَابِعِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رُكْبَتَيْهِ جِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ
فَقَالَ « سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى وَ بِحَمْدِهِ » ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ وَ لَمْ يَضَعْ شَيْئًا مِنْ جَسَدِهِ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ - وَ سَجَدَ عَلَى
ثَمَانِيَةِ أَعْظُمِ الْكَفِّيْنِ وَ الرُكْبَتَيْنِ وَ أَنَامِلِ إِنْهَامَي الرَّجْلَيْنِ وَ الْجَبْهَةِ وَ الْأَتْفِ وَ قَالَ «سَبْعْ مِنْهَا فَرْضَ يُسْجَدُ عَلَيْهَا
وَ هِيَ الَّتِي ذَكَرَهَا اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِي كِتَابِهِ وَ قَالَ «وَ أَنَّ الْمَسْاجِدَ لِلْهِ فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللهِ أَحَداً» وَ هِيَ الْجَبْهَةُ وَ
الْكَفَّانِ وَ الرُّكْبَتَانِ وَ الْإِبْهَامَانِ وَ وَضْعُ الْأَنْفِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ سُنَّةٌ» ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ السُّجُودِ فَلَمَّا اِسْتَوَى جَالِساً
قَالَ « اللهُ أَكْبَرُ » ثُمَّ قَعَدَ عَلَى فَخِذِهِ الْأَيْسَرِ قَدْ وَضَعَ قَدَمَهُ ٱلْأَيْمَنَ عَلَى بَطْنِ قَدَمِهِ الْأَيْسَرِ وَ قَالَ « أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ
رَبِّي وَ أَتُوبُ إلَيْهِ» ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ وَ سَجَدَ سَجْدَةَ الثَّانِيَةِ وَ قَالَ كَمَا قَالَ فِي الْأَولَى وَ لَمْ يَضَعْ شَيْئًا مِنْ
بَدَنِهِ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ فِي رُكُوعِ وَ لا سُجُودٍ وَ كَانَ مُجَنِّحاً وَ لَمْ يَضَعْ ذِرَاعَيْهِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ فَصَلَّى رَكِّعَتَيْنِ عَلَى هَذَا
وَ يَدَاهُ مَضْمُومَةُ الْأَصَابِعِ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ فِي التّشَهُدِ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنَ التّشَهُدِ سَلَّمَ فَقَالَ «يَا حَمَّادُ هَكَذَا صَلِّ».
english_text:
