وعنه عن محمد بن سنان عن ابن مسكان وفضالة عن حسين عن ابن مسكان عن عنبسة بن مصعب قال قال
أبو عبد اللّه عليه السلام : إذا شككت في المغرب فأعد ، وإذا شككت في الفجر فأعد.
english_text:
And from him, from Muhammad bin Sinan, from Ibn Maskan, and Fadalah, from Husayn, from Ibn Maskan,
from Anbasah bin Mus‘ab, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you are doubtful in Maghrib, then repeat
(the prayer), and if you are doubtful in Fajr, then repeat (the prayer)."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ ٱلنَّضْرِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنِ ٱلْفُضَيْلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ السَّهْوِ فَقَالَ «فِي صَلاَةِ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ إِذَا لَمْ تَحْفَظْ مَا
بَيْنَ الثَّلاَثِ إِلَى الْأَرْبَعِ فَأَعِدْ صَلاَتَكَ».
english_text:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from Musa bin Bakr, from al-Fudayl, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about forgetfulness.
Imam {a.s} said: "In the Maghrib prayer, if you do not remember whether it was three or
four (rak‘ahs), then repeat your prayer."
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.179 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.370 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.195 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.167

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحَضْرَمِيَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلسّهْوِ فِي صَلاَةِ الْغَدَاةِ قَالَ
«إِذَا لَمْ تَذْرِ وَاحِدَةً صَلَّيْتَ أَمْ ثِنْتَيْنِ فَأَعِدِ الصَّلاَةَ مِنْ أَوْلِهَا وَ الْجُمُعَةُ أَيْضا إِذَا سَهَا فِيهَا الْإِمَامُ فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعِيدَ
الصَّلاَةَ لِأَنَّهَا رَكْعَتَانِ وَ الْمَغْرِبُ إِذَا سَهَا فِيهَا وَ لَمْ يَدْرِ كَمْ رَكْعَةً صَلَّى فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعِيدَ الصَّلاَةَ».
english_text:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah bin Muhammad, from al-Hadrami, from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about forgetfulness in the Fajr prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "If you do not know whether you prayed one rak‘ah or two, then repeat
the prayer from the beginning. And Jumu‘ah also, if the Imam (of prayer) is forgetful in
it, then he must repeat the prayer, because it is two rak‘ahs.
And Maghrib, if one is forgetful in it and does not know how many rak‘ahs he prayed,
then he must repeat the prayer."
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.179 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.366 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.974 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.195

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَعَنَهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ خَارِجَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ
: «إِذَا سَهَوْتَ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ فَأَعِدِ الصَّلاَةَ».
english_text:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Husayn bin Uthman, from Harun bin Kharijah, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you are forgetful in the Maghrib prayer,
then repeat the prayer."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.180 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.370 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.195

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ ٱلْعَلاءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَشُكْ فِي ٱلْفَجْرِ قَالَ «يُعِيدُ»
قُلْتُ الْمَعْرِبِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ وَ الْوَثْرِ وَ الْجُمُعَةِ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ أَسْأَلَهُ».
english_text:
And from him, from Fadalah, from al-‘Ala’, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who doubts in the Fajr prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should repeat (the prayer)."
I asked: (how about) "Maghrib?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, and Witr, and Jumu‘ah", without me asking Him {a.s} about them.
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.180 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.366 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.975 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.195 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.230 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.165

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وعنه عن ابن أبي عمير عن حماد عن الحلبي عن أبي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام وابن أبي عمير عن حفص بن البختري
وغير واحد عن أبي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام قال : إذا شككت في المغرب فاعد وإذا شككت في الفجر فاعد.
english_text:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon
him, and from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs bin al-Bakhtari and more than one person:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “If you are doubtful in Maghrib, then repeat
(the prayer), and if you are doubtful in Fajr, then repeat (the prayer).”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ
الْحَضْرَمِيّ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ بِأَصْحَابِيَ الْمَغْرِبَ فَلَمَّا أَنْ صَلَّيْتُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ سَلَّمْتُ فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ إِنَّمَا صَلَّيْتَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ
فَأَعَدْتُ فَأَخْبَرْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ فَقَالَ «لَعَلِّكَ أَعَدْتَ» فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ فَضَحِكَ ثُمَّ قَالَ «إِنَّمَا كَانَ يُجْزِيكَ أَنْ
تَقُومَ وَ تَرْكَعَ رَكْعَةً إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ سَهَا فَسَلَّمَ فِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ حَدِيثَ ذِي الشِّمَالَيْنِ فَقَالَ
ثُمَّ قَامَ فَأَضَافَ إِلَيْهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ».
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah,
from Sayf bin Umayrah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami:
He (Abu Bakr al-Hadrami) said: “I led my companions in the Maghrib prayer, and when
I had prayed two rak‘ahs, I performed the taslim. Some of them said, ‘You only prayed
two rak‘ahs.’
So I repeated the prayer.
Then I informed Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him.
Imam {a.s} said: "Perhaps you repeated it?"
I said: "Yes."
Imam {a.s} laughed and then said: "It would have sufficed you to stand and perform one
rak‘ah. The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, once forgot and
performed the taslim after two rak‘ahs.”
And then He {a.s} mentioned the narration of Dhu al-Shimalayn, and said: “Then he
stood and added two rak‘ahs to it."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.180 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.370 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.959 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.199

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ رَوَى سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنِ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ النَّصْرِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ إِنَّا صَلِّيْنَا الْمَغْرِبَ فَسَهَا الْإِمَامُ فَسَلَّمَ فِي الرّكْعَتَيْنِ فَأَعَدْنَا الصَّلاةَ فَقَالَ «وَ لِمَ أَعَدْتُمْ أَ لَيْسَ قَدِ
انْصَرَفَ رَسُولُ اللّهِ صَلّى اللّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَأَتَمَّ بِرَكْعَتَيْنِ أَلاَ أَثْمَمْتُمْ».
فليس في هذين الخبرين ما ينافي ما قدمناه لان السهو إنما وقع هاهنا في ان سلم في الركعة الثانية ولم يكن السهو قد
وقع في اعداد الصلاة ومن سها في التسليم لم يجب عليه إعادة الصلاة بل يجب عليه جبرانه بركعة حسب ما تضمنه
الخبران، ولو كان السهو واقعا في العدد لوجب اعادة الصلاة من أولها حسب ما قدمناه، والذي يكشف عما ذكرناه ما رواه:
english_text:
And Sa‘d narrated from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ja‘far bin Bashir, from al-Harith bin al-Mughirah al-
Nasri, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “We prayed Maghrib, and the imam (of
prayer) was forgetful and performed the taslim after two rak‘ahs, so we repeated the
prayer.”
Imam {a.s} said: "And why did you repeat it? Did not the Messenger of Allah {SWT} (peace
be upon him and his family) once leave the prayer after two rak‘ahs and then complete
it with two more (rak’ahs)? Should you not have completed it?"
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
commentary:
There is nothing in these two reports that contradicts what we have previously
presented, because the forgetfulness here occurred in that the taslim was performed
in the second rak‘ah, and not in the counting of the number of rak‘ahs of the prayer.
And whoever is forgetful in the taslim is not obligated to repeat the prayer; rather, it is
obligatory upon him to compensate for it with one rak‘ah, as these two reports
indicate. But if the forgetfulness had occurred in the number (of rak‘ahs), then the
prayer would have to be repeated from the beginning, as we have previously stated.
What clarifies what we have mentioned is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.180 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.370 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.958 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.198 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.1 7 p.100

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَيُوبَ بْنِ نُوحِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ ٱلنُّعْمَانِ الرَّازِيِّ قَالَ: كُنْتُ مَعَ أَصْحَابٍ لِي فِي سَفَرٍ وَ أَنَا إِمَامُهُمْ فَصَلَّيْتُ بِهِمُ
اَلْمَغْرِبَ فَسَلَمْتُ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوْلَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ أَصْحَابِي إِنَّمَا صَلِّيْتَ بِنَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَكَلَّمْتُهُمْ وَ كَلَّمُونِي فَقَالُوا أَمَّا نَحْنُ
فَنُعِيدُ فَقُلْتُ لَكِنِّي لاَ أُعِيدُ وَ أَتِمُ بِرَكْعَةِ فَأْتْمَمْتُ بِرَكْعَةِ ثُمَّ سِرْنَا فَأَتَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ فَذَكَرْتُ لَهُ آلَّذِي
كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا فَقَالَ لِي «أَنْتَ كُنْتَ أَصْوَبَ مِنْهُمْ فِعْلاً إِنَّمَا يُعِيدُ مَنْ لاَ يَدْرِي مَا صَلَّى».
فبين عليه السلام في هذا الخبر أن من لا يدري ما صلى يجب عليه الاعادة حسب ما قدمناه، مع ان في الحديثين الاولين
ما يمنع من التعلق بهما وهو حديث ذي الشمالين وسهو النبي صلى اللّٰه عليه وآله وهذا مما تمنع العقول منه ، فاما ما تضمن
الحديث الآخر الذي جعلناه شاهدا على الحديثين الاولين من قوله فكلمتهم وكلموني ليس يناقض ما نذكره من إن من
تكلم في الصلاة عامدا وجب عليه اعادة الصلاة لشيئين، احدهما : انه ليس في الخبر انه قال كلمتهم وكلموني عامدا أو
ناسيا وإذا لم يكن ذلك فيه حملناه على السهو ، والثاني : انه لو كان فيه تصريح بالعمد لجاز أن يكون المراد به من سلم
في الصلاة ناسيا وظن ان ذلك سبب لاستباحة الكلام كما انه سبب لاستباحته بعد الانصراف من الصلاة فلم يجب عليه
إعادة الصلاة لجهله به ولارتفاع علمه بانه لا يسوغ ذلك، فاما ما رواه:
english_text:
Sa‘d, from Ayyub bin Nuh, from Ali bin al-Nu‘man al-Razi, who said:
I (al-Razi) was with some companions of mine on a journey, and I was their Imam (of
prayer). I led them in the Maghrib prayer and performed the taslim after the first two
rak‘ahs.
My companions said: "You only prayed two rak‘ahs with us."
We spoke to each other, and they said: "As for us, we will repeat (the prayer)."
So I said: "As for me, I will not repeat it; I will complete it with one rak‘ah."
So I completed it with one rak‘ah.
Then we continued our journey, and I came to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him and
mentioned to Him {a.s} what had happened with us.
Imam {a.s} said to me: "You acted more correctly than they did. Only the one who does
not know what he has prayed must repeat (the prayer)."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
He {a.s}, peace be upon him, clarified in this report that whoever does not know what he
has prayed is obligated to repeat the prayer, as we have previously mentioned.
Moreover, in the first two reports, there is what prevents relying upon them, namely,
the hadith of Dhu al-Shimalayn and the forgetfulness of the Prophet (peace be upon
him and his family), and this is something that reason rejects.
As for the other report, which we used as supporting evidence for the first two,
containing the statement: "We spoke to each other, and they spoke to me", this does
not contradict what we have mentioned, namely that whoever speaks deliberately
during prayer must repeat the prayer, for two reasons.
First: the report does not state whether he spoke deliberately or out of forgetfulness,
so we interpret it as being due to forgetfulness.
Second: even if the report had clearly stated that it was deliberate, it would still be
possible that what was meant is that he had performed the taslim out of forgetfulness
and thought that this permitted speaking, just as it is permitted after the completion
of prayer. Therefore, he would not be obligated to repeat the prayer due to his
ignorance of the ruling and his lack of knowledge that such speech was not allowed.
As for what was narrated:
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.347 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.181 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.371 • Nuzhat Al-Nazir, Vol.1 p.38 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.958 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.199 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.198

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ وَ الْحَكَمِ بْنِ مِسْكِينٍ عَنْ عَمَّارِ السَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ رَجُلْ شَكَّ فِي الْمَغْرِبِ فَلَمْ يَدْرٍ رَكْعَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ ثَلاَثَةً قَالَ «يُسَلَّمُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُضِيفُ إِلَيْهَا رَكْعَةً» ثُمَّ
قَالَ «هَذَا وَ اللَّهِ مِمَّا لا يُقْضَى أَبَداً».
english_text:
Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad and al-Hakam bin Miskin, from ‘Ammar al-Sabati,
who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “A man doubts in the Maghrib prayer and
does not know whether he has prayed two rak‘ahs or three.”
Imam {a.s} said: "He performs the taslim, then stands and adds to it one rak‘ah."
Then Imam {a.s} said: "By Allah {SWT}, this is something that is never made up (qadha)."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.182 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.371 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.976 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.196 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.232

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَادِ النَّابِ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ
السَّابَاطِيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ لَمْ يَدْرٍ صَلَّى الْفَجْرَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَوْ رَكْعَةً قَالَ «يَتَشَهَدُ وَ
يَنْصَرِفُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَةً فَإِنْ كَانَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ كَانَتْ هَذِهِ تَطَوُعاً وَ إِنْ كَانَ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً كَانَتْ هَذِهِ تَمَامَ
الصَّلَةِ قُلْتُ فَصَلَّى الْمَغْرِبَ فَلَمْ يَدْرِ إِثْنَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ ثَلاَثَةً» قَالَ «يَتَشَهَدُ وَ يَنْصَرِفُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَةً فَإِنْ
كَانَ صَلَّى ثَلاَثاً كَانَتْ هَذِهِ تَطَوْعاً وَ إِنْ كَانَ صَلَّى اِثْنَتَيْنِ كَانَتْ هَذِهِ تَمَامَ الصَلاَةِ وَ هَذَا وَ اللَّهِ مِمَّا لا يُقْضَى أَبَدا».
english_text:
And what was narrated by Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Mu‘awiyah bin Hakim, from Muhammad bin
Abi Umayr, from Hammad al-Nabb, from ‘Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who does not know whether
he prayed two rak‘ahs or one in the Fajr prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should recite the tashahhud and conclude (the prayer), then stand
and pray one rak‘ah. If he had prayed two rak‘ahs, then this (extra) rak‘ah is a
recommended prayer (nafilah), and if he had prayed only one rak‘ah, then this is the
completion of the prayer."
I asked: "And what if he prayed Maghrib and does not know whether he prayed two
rak‘ahs or three?"
Imam {a.s} said: "He should recite the tashahhud and conclude (the prayer), then stand
and pray one rak‘ah. If he had prayed three, then this (extra) rak‘ah is a recommended
prayer (nafilah), and if he had prayed two, then this is the completion of the prayer.
And by Allah {SWT}, this is something that is never made up (qadah’)."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.182 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.976 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.196 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.233

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَجَّالِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ: فِي رَجُلٍ صَلَّى ٱلْفَجْرَ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ
ذَهَبَ وَ جَاءَ بَعْدَ مَا أَصْبَحَ وَ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً قَالَ «يُضِيفُ إِلَيْهَا رَكْعَةً».
فليس في هذه الاخبار ما يضاد ما ذكرناه لانه ليس في ظاهر هذه الاخبار ان السهو وقع في النافلة أو الفريضة وإنما
تضمنت ذكر صلاة الفجر وصلاة المغرب، ويجوز أن يكون المراد بها النوافل لان النوافل قد تنسب الى الفجر وكذلك نوافل
المغرب تنسب الى المغرب كما ان الفريضة تنسب إليه وإذا احتمل ما قلناه حملناه على ما لا تتناقض فيه الاخبار، ويحتمل
الخبر ان الاولان وجها آخر وهو أن يكون من شك في الفجر والمغرب فغلب على ظنه الاكثر فلاجل ذلك جاز له أن يبني
عليه لان غلبة الظن تقوم مقام العلم وقد بيناه فيما مضى ، وإن كان مع هذا يعترضه أدنى شك إلا أنه لا حكم له ويكون
قوله عليه السلام : يضيف إليها ركعة يكون من جهة الاستظهار والاستحباب دون الفرض والايجاب ، والذي يدل على ذلك
مارواه :
١١- ١٥ ٢ ٢٠٠
english_text:
And from him, from al-Hajjal, from Abdillah {a.s}, from ‘Ubayd:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said regarding a man who prayed one rak‘ah of
Fajr, then went away and came back after morning had begun and remembered that
he had prayed only one rak‘ah.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should add one rak‘ah to it."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
There is nothing in these reports that contradicts what we have mentioned, because
there is nothing apparent in these reports indicating whether the forgetfulness
occurred in a recommended prayer (nafilah) or an obligatory one (fard). They only
mention the Fajr and Maghrib prayers, and it is possible that what is meant by them
are the recommended prayers (nawafil), because the recommended prayers are often
attributed to Fajr, just as the nawafil of Maghrib are attributed to Maghrib, just as the
obligatory prayers are attributed to their times. And if what we said is possible, we
interpret these reports in a way that avoids contradiction between them.
Another possibility in understanding the first two reports is that the person who
doubted in Fajr or Maghrib had a predominant assumption (ghalabat al-zann) toward
the higher number, and for that reason, it was permitted for him to build upon it,
because predominant assumption takes the place of certainty, as we have explained
previously. Even if a minor doubt remains, it holds no legal weight.
Therefore, His {a.s} statement, peace be upon him, "He adds a rak‘ah to it" would be
from the standpoint of precaution and recommendation, not obligation and
requirement. What indicates this is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.182 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.961 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.204

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيِى الْمُعَاذِيُّ عَنِ الطَّيَالِسِيَّ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ إسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «إِذَا ذَهَبَ وَهْمُكَ إِلَى التَّمَامِ أَبَداً فِي كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ فَاسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَيْنِ بِغَيْرِ رُكُوعِ أَ فَهِمْتَ» قُلْتُ نَعَمْ.
وأما الخبر الاخير الذي تضمن ذكر صلاة الفجر فيحتمل ما قدمناه من النوافل ويحتمل ايضا أن يكون هذا الخبر مخصوصا
بمن صلى وظن انه صلى ركعتين ثم تيقن انه صلى ركعة واحدة فانه يضيف إليها ركعة اخرى ولا تجب عليه إعادة الصلاة
، والاعادة إنما تجب على من يشك فيها فلا يدري صلى ركعة أو ركعتين ولم يتبين ذلك فيجب عليه حينئذ إعادة الصلاة،
والذي يكشف عما ذكرناه ما رواه:
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya al-Mu‘adhi, from al-Tayalisi, from Sayf bin Umayrah, from Ishaq bin
‘Ammar, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If your assumption always leans toward
completion (the higher number) in every prayer, then perform two prostrations
(sajdatayn) without a ruku‘. Do you understand?"
I said: "Yes."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
As for the last report which includes mention of the Fajr prayer, it may be interpreted
in accordance with what we previously stated, that it refers to the recommended
prayers (nawafil). It is also possible that this report is specific to someone who prayed
and assumed that he had prayed two rak‘ahs, then became certain that he had only
prayed one; in such a case, he adds another rak‘ah to it, and the repetition of the
prayer is not obligatory upon him.
Repetition is only obligatory upon the one who doubts in the prayer and does not know
whether he prayed one rak‘ah or two, and the matter is not clarified for him, then, in
that case, he must repeat the prayer.
What clarifies what we have mentioned is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.183 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.991 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.211 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.177

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْعَلاَءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ أَجِيءُ إِلَى الْإِمَامِ وَ قَدْ سَبَقَنِي بِرَكْعَةِ فِي الْفَجْرِ فَلَمَّا سَلَّمَ وَقَعَ فِي قَلْبِي أَنَّي قَدْ أَثْمَمْتُ
فَلَمْ أَزَلْ ذَاكِراً لِلّهِ حَتَّى طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَلَمَّا طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ نَهَضْتُ فَذَكَزْتُ أَنْ الْإِمَامَ كَانَ قَدْ سَبَقَنِي بِرَكْعَةٍ قَالَ
«فَإِنْ كُنْتَ فِي مَقَامِكَ فَأْتِمَّ بِرَكْعَةٍ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ قَدِ اِنْصَرَفْتَ فَعَلَيْكَ الإِعَادَةُ».
يعني به إذا كان قد أستدبر القبلة. وقوله عليه السلام : في الخبر الاول ذهب وجاء محمول على خلافه على انه ذهب وجاء
من غير أن يستدبر القبلة ، يدل على ذلك ما رواه :
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ya‘qub bin Yazid, from Ali bin al-Nu‘man, from al-Husayn bin Abi
al-‘Ala’, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I (narrator) said: "I came to the imam (of prayer) while he had preceded me by one
rak‘ah in the Fajr prayer. When he completed the prayer with the taslim, it occurred in
my heart that I had completed (my prayer), so I remained engaged in the remembrance
of Allah {SWT} until the sun rose. When the sun rose, I stood up and remembered that
the Imam had preceded me by one rak‘ah."
Imam {a.s} said: "If you were still in your place, then complete it with one rak‘ah; but if
you had already left, then you must repeat the prayer."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
He means by that: if he had turned his back to the qiblah.
And His statement, peace be upon him, (in the first report) "he went and came back,"
is to be understood differently, that he went and came back without turning his back
to the qiblah. What indicates this is what was narrated:
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.383 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.183 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.271 • Al- Istibsar, Vol.1 p.367 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.959 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.209

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
اَلْعَيَّاشِيُ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عَلِي بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ وَ عَلِيْ بْنُ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنِ الْعُبَيْدِيِّ عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنِ الْعَلاءِ
عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلامُ قَالَ: سُيْلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ دَخَلَ مَعَ ٱلْإِمَامِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَ قَدْ سَبَقَهُ بِرَكْعَةٍ
فَلَمَّا قَرَغَ الْإِمَامُ خَرَجَ مَعَ النَّاسِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ فَاتَتْهُ رَكْعَةٌ قَالَ «يُعِيدُ رَكْعَةً وَاحِدَةً يَجُوزُ لَهُ إِذَا لَمْ يُحَوِّلْ وَجْهَهُ
عَنِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَإِذَا حَوَّلَ وَجْهَهُ بِكُلِّيَّةٍ اِسْتَقْبَلَ الصَّلَاةَ اِسْتِقْبَالا».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ومن سها في الركعتين الاخيرتين من الظهر أو العصر أو العشاء الآخرة فلم يدر أهو في الثالثة أو
english_text:
Al-‘Ayyashi, from Ja‘far bin Ahmad, who said: Ali bin al-Husayn and Ali bin Muhammad narrated to me, from
al-‘Ubaydi, from Yunus, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad bin Muslim, from one of them (Imams {a.s}), peace be
upon them both, who said:
He {a.s} was asked about a man who joined the imam (of prayer) in prayer while the
imam (of prayer) had already completed one rak‘ah before him. When the imam
finished the prayer, the man left with the people, then remembered that he had missed
a rak‘ah.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should repeat one rak‘ah, it is permissible for him to do so as long
as he has not turned his face away from the qiblah. But if he has completely turned his
face away, then he must start the prayer anew from the beginning."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “Whoever is forgetful in the
last two rak‘ahs of the Dhuhr, ‘Asr, or Isha prayer and does not know whether he is in
the third or fourth rak‘ah, then he should refer to his assumption regarding that. If his
assumption inclines more strongly toward either one of them, he should act upon it.
But if his assumption is equal between both possibilities, he should act upon the
greater number (assume it is the fourth rak‘ah), and then make up what he assumes
he has missed.
For example, if he doubts between the third and fourth and his assumption is balanced
between them, he should assume he is in the fourth, perform the tashahhud, give the
taslim, then stand and perform one rak‘ah with tashahhud in it, or perform two rak‘ahs
while sitting, and perform tashahhud in the second of them.”
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.184 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.348 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.368 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.957 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.209 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.198

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ
عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ سَيَابَةَ وَ أَبِي الْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا لَمْ تَدْرِ ثَلاَثاً صَلَّيْتَ أَوْ أَرْبَعاً وَ
وَقَعَ رَأْيُكَ عَلَى الثَّلاَثِ فَابْنٍ عَلَى الثَّلاَثِ وَ إِنْ وَقَعَ رَأْيُكَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْبَعِ فَسَلَّمْ وَ اِنْصَرِفُ وَ إِنِ اِعْتَدَلَ وَهْمُكَ فَانْصَرِفْ
وَاصَلً رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَنْتَ جَالِسْ».
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from al-Husayn bin
Sa‘id, from Fadalah bin Ayyub, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman bin Sayabah and Abu al-‘Abbas:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you have
prayed three rak‘ahs or four, and your inclination falls upon three, then build upon
three. And if your inclination falls upon four, then give the taslim and depart. But if your
doubt is balanced (with no inclination toward either), then depart and pray two rak‘ahs
while sitting."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.353 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.184 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.981 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.211

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيِى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ
اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: فِيمَنْ لا يَدْرِي أَثَلَاثاً صَلّى أَمْ أَرْبَعاً وَ وَهْمُهُ فِي ذَلِكَ سَوَاءً قَالَ فَقَالَ «إِذَا اِعْتَدَلَ الْوَهْمُ
فِي الثَّلَاَثِ وَ الْأَرْبَعِ فَهُوَ بِالْخِيَارِ إِنْ شَاءَ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَرْبَعَ سَجَدَاتٍ».
english_text:
And from him, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ali bin Hadid, from Jamil,
from some of our companions:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said regarding someone who does not know
whether he prayed three rak‘ahs or four, and his doubt between them is equal.
Imam {a.s} said: "When the doubt is equal between three and four, then he has a choice:
if he wishes, he may pray one rak‘ah while standing, and if he wishes, he may pray two
rak‘ahs with four prostrations."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.184 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.216

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثَمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةً عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ
صَلَّى فَلَمْ يَدْرِ أ فِي الثَّالِثَةِ هُوَ أَمْ فِي الرَّابِعَةِ قَالَ «فَمَا ذَهَبَ وَهمُهُ إِلَيْهِ إِنْ رَأْى أَنَّهُ فِي الثَالِثَةِ وَ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِنَ
الرَّابِعَةٍ شَيْءً سَلَّمَ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ نَفْسِهِ ثُمَّ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ يَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn bin ‘Uthman, from Sama‘ah, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Him {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who prayed and did not know
whether he was in the third rak‘ah or the fourth.
Imam {a.s} said: "Whatever his assumption inclines toward, if he thinks he is in the third
and there is still something in his heart about the fourth, then he should conclude (the
prayer) between himself and his Lord {AZJ}, then pray two rak‘ahs in which he recites the
Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in both."
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.351 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.185 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.983 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.218 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.177

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْعَلاَءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِنِ اِسْتَوَى وَهْمُهُ فِي الثَّلَاَثِ وَ
اَلْأَرْبَعِ سَلَّمَ وَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَرْبَعَ سَجَدَاتٍ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ يُقَصِّرُ فِي النَّشَهْدِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : (وكذلك من سها فلم يدر أهو في الثانية أو الرابعة فان كان ظنه من احديهما أقوى من الاخرى عمل
. 01ة
فانا هله قاه
بكوتا ص
باقراح دق اف
english_text:
And from him, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn bin Abi al-‘Ala’:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If his doubt is equal between three and
four, then he should give the taslim and pray two rak‘ahs and four prostrations, reciting
the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in them, while he is seated, shortening the
tashahhud."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “And likewise, if one is
forgetful and does not know whether he is in the second or the fourth rak‘ah, if his
assumption is stronger toward one of them, then he should act according to his
assumption. But if his assumption is equal between them, then he should act as if he
is in the fourth rak‘ah, perform the tashahhud, and when he gives the taslim, he should
stand and pray two rak‘ahs while standing, reciting al-Hamd (Surah al-Fatiha) alone in
each of them, and if he wishes, he may recite tasbih instead.”
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.351 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.185 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.984 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.218

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى
رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَلا يَدْرِي رَكْعَتَانِ هِيَ أَوْ أَرْبَعْ قَالَ «يُسَلَّمُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ وَ يَتَشَهَدُ وَ يَنْصَرِفُ
وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad bin Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who prayed two rak‘ahs and
does not know whether they were two or four.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should give the taslim, then stand and pray two rak‘ahs, reciting
the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) in them, perform the tashahhud, and then
conclude (the prayer), and nothing is required of him."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.185 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.372 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.984 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.221

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَادٍ عَنْ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا لَمْ تَدْرِ أَرْبَعاً صَلِّيْتَ أَمْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ
فَقُمْ وَ اِزْكَعْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ سَلَّمْ وَ اِرْكَعْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ سَلَّمْ وَ اُسْجُدْ سَجَدَتَيْنِ وَ أَنْتَ جَالِسْ ثُمَّ تُسَلَّمُ بَعْدَهُمَا».
english_text:
And from him, from Hammad, from Shu‘ayb, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you prayed four
rak‘ahs or two, then stand and perform two rak‘ahs, then give the taslim. Then perform
two more rak‘ahs, then give the taslim, and then perform two prostrations (sajdatayn)
while sitting, and then give the taslim after them."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.185 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.985 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.221 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.183

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ لا يَدْرِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ أَرْبَعاً قَالَ »يَتَشَهَدُ وَ يُسَلَّمُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي
رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَرْبَعَ سَجَدَاتِ يَقْرَأْ فِيهِمَا بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ ثُمَّ يَتَشَهَدُ وَ يُسَلَّمُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَدْ صَلَّى أَرْبَعاً كَانَتْ هَانَانِ نَافِلَةً
وَ إِنْ كَانَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ كَانَتْ هَاتَانِ إِثْمَامَ الْأَرْبَعَةِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ تَكَلَّمَ فَلْيَسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَي السَّهْوِ».
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Maskan, from
Ibn Abi Ya‘fur, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who does not know whether
he prayed two rak‘ahs or four.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should recite the tashahhud and give the taslim, then stand and
pray two rak‘ahs and four prostrations, reciting the Opening of the Book (Surah al-
Fatiha) in both of them, then recite the tashahhud and give the taslim. If he had already
prayed four, then these two are (counted as) recommended prayers (nafilah), and if he
had only prayed two, then these complete the four. And if he spoke (during this state),
then he must perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw)."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.352 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.186 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.372 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.979 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.219

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ
حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا ٱلسِّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَنْ لَمْ يَدْرٍ فِي أَرْبَعِ هَوَ أَوْ فِي ثِنْتَيْنِ وَ قَدْ أَحْرَزَ الثَّنْتَيْنِ
قَالَ «رَكَعَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ أَرْبَعَ سَجَدَاتٍ وَ هَوَ قَائِمٌ بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ وَ يَتَشَهْدُ وَ لا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِذَا لَمْ يَدْرٍ فِي ثَلاَثِ
هُوَ أَوْ فِي أَرْبَعِ وَ قَدْ أَحْرَزَ الثَّلاَتَ قَامَ فَأَضَافَ إِلَيْهَا أُخْرَى وَ لا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ لا يَنْقُضِ ٱلْيَقِينَ بِالشَّكَّ وَ لا يُدْخِلِ
الشَّكَّ فِي الْيَقِينِ وَ لَا يَخْلِطْ أَحَدَهُمَا بِالْآخَرِ وَ لَكِنَّهُ يَنْقُضُ الشَّكَّ بِالْيَقِينِ وَ يُتِمُّ عَلَى الْيَقِينِ فَيَبْنِي عَلَيْهِ وَ لا
بَعْتَدَّ بِالشَّكٍّ فِي حَالٍ مِنَ الْحَالاَتِ».
english_text:
And from him, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, and from Muhammad bin Isma‘il, from al-Fadl bin
Shadhan, all from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from one of them (Imams {a.s}), peace be upon
them both, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: “A person does not know whether he is in the fourth rak‘ah or the
second, but he is certain that he has completed two rak‘ahs.”
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray two rak‘ahs and four prostrations while standing,
reciting the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha), and perform the tashahhud, and
nothing is upon him. And if he does not know whether he is in the third or the fourth,
and he is certain he has completed three rak‘ahs, then he should stand and add one
more, and nothing is upon him. One does not nullify certainty with doubt, and one
should not insert doubt into certainty, nor mix the two together. Rather, doubt is
nullified by certainty, and he completes the prayer based on what is certain and builds
upon it, and doubt is not to be regarded in any situation."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.351 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.186 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.373 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.979 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.2 p.281 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.180

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ ٱلْعَلاءِ عَنْ مُحَمِّدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلرَّجُلِ لا يَدْرِي صَلّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَمْ
أَرْبَعاً قَالَ «يُعِيدُ الصَّلاَةَ».
فلا ينافي الاخبار الاولة لان هذا الخبر محمول على صلاة المغرب أو الغداة التي لا يجوز فيهما الشك على ما بيناه. قال
الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ولو شك في اثنتين وثلاث واربع واعتدل وهمه بنى على الاربع وتشهد وسلم ثم صلى ركعتين من قيام
وتشهد وسلم وصلى ركعتين من جلوس يتشهد أيضا ويسلم).
english_text:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or four.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should repeat the prayer."
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
commentary:
So this does not contradict the earlier reports, because this narration is to be
understood as referring to the Maghrib or Fajr prayers, in which doubt is not permitted,
as we have already explained.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: “And if one doubts between
two, three, and four rak‘ahs, and his assumption is balanced among them, then he
should build upon four, perform the tashahhud, give the taslim, then pray two rak‘ahs
while standing, perform the tashahhud, give the taslim, and then pray two rak‘ahs
while sitting, also performing the tashahhud and giving the taslim.”
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.186 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.373 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.990 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.221 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.182

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ : فِي رَجْلٍ صَلَّى وَ لَمْ يَدْرِ اِثْنَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ ثَلاثاً أَمْ أَرْبَعاً قَالَ «فَيَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ قِيَامٍ وَ يُسَلَّمُ
ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ جُلُوسِ وَ يُسَلَّمُ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ كَانَتِ الرَّكْعَتَانِ نَافِلَةً وَ إِلَّ تَمَّتِ الْأَرْبَعُ».
ومن شك فلم يعلم صلى واحدة أم ثنتين أو ثلاثا أو أربعا وجب عليه اعادة الصلاة لانه لم تسلم له الركعتان الاولتان، وقد
دللنا على ان من لم تسلم له الركعتان الاولتان وجب عليه أن يستأنف الصلاة، ويدل عليه أيضا ما رواه:
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his
companions:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, (said) regarding a man who prayed and did not
know whether he had prayed two, three, or four rak‘ahs.
Imam {a.s} said: "Then he should stand and pray two rak‘ahs while standing and give the
taslim, then pray two rak‘ahs while sitting and give the taslim. If he had actually prayed
four rak‘ahs, then the two rak‘ahs are counted as recommended (nafilah), and if not,
then the four rak‘ahs are completed."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
And whoever doubts and does not know whether he has prayed one rak‘ah, or two, or
three, or four, it is obligatory upon him to repeat the prayer, because the first two
rak‘ahs are not established for him. And we have already demonstrated that whoever
does not have certainty regarding the first two rak‘ahs must begin the prayer anew.
This is also supported by what was narrated:
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.353 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.187 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.981 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.223 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.184

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِنْ شَكَكْتَ وَ لَمْ تَدْرِ أَ فِي ثَلَاَثٍ أَنْتَ أَمْ فِي اِثنَتَيْنٍ أَمْ فِي وَاحِدَةٍ أَوْ فِي أَرْبَعٍ فَأَعِدْ وَ لا تَمْضٍ عَلَى
الشَّكِّ».
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ali bin Isma‘il, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ibn Abi Ya‘fur:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you are doubtful and do not know
whether you are in the third, or the second, or the first, or the fourth, then repeat (the
prayer), and do not proceed based on doubt."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.358 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.187 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.373 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.989 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.226

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبَّادِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ ٱَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِنْ كُنْتَ لا تَدْرِي
كَمْ صَلّيْتَ وَ لَمْ يَقَعْ وَهَمُكَ عَلَى شَيْءٍ فَأَعِدِ الصَّلاةَ».
english_text:
And from him, from ‘Abbad bin Sulayman, from Sa‘d bin Sa‘d, from Safwan:
Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know how many rak‘ahs you
have prayed, and your assumption does not settle upon anything, then repeat the
prayer."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s} & Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.358 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.187 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.373 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.989 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.225 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.210 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.6 p.412 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.6 p.413

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَأَمًا مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ
قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ ٱلرَّجُلِ لا يَدْرِي كَمْ صَلَّى وَاحِدَةً أَوِ اِثْنَتَيْنِ أَمْ ثَلاثاً قَالَ «يَبْنِي عَلَى ٱلْجَزْمِ
وَ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَي اَلسَّهْوِ وَ يَتَشَهَدُ خَفِيف».
فلا ينافي الخبر الاول لانه قال : يبني على الجزم والذي يقتضيه الجزم استيناف الصلاة على ما بيناه والامر بسجدتي
السهو يكون محمولا على الاستحباب لا لجبران الصلاة.
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Ahmad bin Muhammad, from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Yaqtin,
from his brother al-Husayn bin Ali, from their father Ali bin Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who does not know how
many rak‘ahs he has prayed, one, or two, or three.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should build upon what he is certain of, and perform the two
prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw), and recite a light tashahhud."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
commentary:
So this does not contradict the first report, because he said: "He should build upon
certainty (jazm)," and what certainty necessitates is the restarting of the prayer, as we
have previously explained. As for the instruction to perform the two prostrations of
forgetfulness (sajdatay al-sahw), it is to be understood as a recommendation
(mustahabb), not as a required compensation for the prayer.
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.187 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.986

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ
رَجْلٍ صَالِحِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَشُكْ فَلا يَدْرِي وَاحِدَةً صَلَّى أَوِ اِثْنَتَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلاثاً أَوْ أَرْبَعاً تَلْتَبِسُ
عَلَيْهِ صَلاَثُهُ قَالَ «كُلُّ ذَا» قَالَ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ «فَلْيَمْضٍ فِي صَلَاَتِهِ وَ يَتَعَوَّذُ بِاللهِ مِنَ الشِّيْطَانِ فَإِنَّهُ يُوشِكْ أَنْ
يَذْهَبَ عَنْهُ».
فان هذا الخبر محمول على السهو في النوافل وليس في الخبر انه شك في صلاة فريضة ويحتمل ايضا أن يكون المراد
ابه من يكثر سهوه ولا يمكنه التحفظ فيسوغ له أن يمضي في صلاته لانه إن أوجب عليه الاعادة وهو من شانه السهو فلا
ينفك من الصلاة على حال ، فأما من كان نسيانه حينا فانه يجب عليه اعادة الصلاة حسب ما قدمناه، يدل على ما ذكرناه:
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Mu‘awiyah bin Hakim, from Abdillah
bin al-Mughirah, from Ali bin Abi Hamzah, from a righteous man, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who doubts and does not know whether he has prayed
one, two, three, or four rak‘ahs, his prayer becomes confused for him.
Imam {a.s} said: "All of that?"
I said: "Yes."
Imam {a.s} said: "Then let him continue in his prayer and seek refuge with Allah {SWT} from
Shaytan, for soon it will leave him."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
commentary:
For this report is to be understood as referring to forgetfulness in ‘nawafil’
(recommended prayers), and there is nothing in the report indicating that the doubt
occurred in an obligatory prayer (‘fard’). It is also possible that what is meant is a
person who frequently forgets and is unable to maintain awareness, in which case it
is permitted for him to proceed with his prayer, because if repetition were made
obligatory upon him, and forgetfulness is his consistent state, he would never be able
to complete a prayer.
As for one whose forgetfulness occurs only occasionally, then he is obligated to repeat
the prayer, as we have previously stated.
What supports what we have mentioned is:
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.350 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.188 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.374 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.228 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.273

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ
حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالاَ: قُلْنَا لَهُ الرَّجُلُ يَشُكْ كَثِيراً فِي صَلاَتِهِ حَتَّى لا يَدْرِيَ كَمْ
صَلَّى وَ لا مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ «يُعِيدُ» قُلْنَا فَإِنَّهُ يَكْثُرُ عَلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ كُلَّمَا أَعَادَ شَكٍ قَالَ «يَمْضِي فِي شَكِّهِ» ثُمَّ قَالَ «لا
تُعَوِّدُوا الْخَبِيثَ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ نَقْضَ الصَّلاةِ فَتُظْمِعُوهُ فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ حَبِيثْ مُعْتَادٌ لِمَا عُوِّدَ بِهِ فَلْيَمْضِ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي
الْوَهم وَلَا يُكْثِرَنَّ نَقْضَ الصَّلاَةِ فَإِنَّهُ إِذَا فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ مَرَّاتٍ لَمْ يَعْدْ إِلَيْهِ الشَّكُّ» قَالَ زُرَارَةُ ثُمَّ قَالَ «إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ الْخَبِيثُ
أَنْ يُطَاعَ فَإِذَا عُصِيَ لَمْ يَعْدُ إِلَى أَحَدِكُمْ».
ومن كان في صلاته فلم يدر ما صلى وجب عليه اعادة الصلاة، ويدل على ذلك :
english_text:
What was narrated by Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, and from Muhammad
bin Isma‘il, from al-Fadl bin Shadhan, all from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Abu Basir,
who said:
We said to Him {a.s}: “A man frequently doubts in his prayer to the extent that he no
longer knows how much he has prayed or what remains upon him.”
Imam {a.s} said: "He should repeat (the prayer)."
We asked: “But it happens to him frequently, every time he repeats, he doubts again.”
Imam {a.s} said: "Then he should proceed with his doubt."
Then Imam {a.s} said: "Do not accustom the evil one (‘al-khabith’), meaning the Shaytan,
from yourselves to breaking the prayer, lest you encourage him, for Shaytan is wicked
and becomes accustomed to whatever he is trained with. So let one of you proceed in
his assumption and not frequently invalidate the prayer, for if he does that repeatedly,
the doubt will not return to him."
Zurarah said: “Then Imam {a.s} said: ‘Indeed, the evil one only wants to be obeyed; so
when he is disobeyed, he does not return to any one of you.’"
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
commentary:
And whoever is in his prayer and does not know what he has prayed, it is obligatory
upon him to repeat the prayer. What supports this is:
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.358 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.188 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.374 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.997 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.228 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.270

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ الْعَمْرَكِيَّ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السِّلاَمُ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَقُومُ فِي الصَّلاةِ فَلا يَدْرِي صَلَّى شَيْئاً أَمْ لا قَالَ «يَسْتَقْبِلُ».
ومن سها في ركعتين من صلاة الليل ثم ذكرهما وقد أوتر أعادهما وأعاد الوتر روى ذلك :
english_text:
What was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from al-‘Amraki, from Ali bin Ja‘far, from his brother
(Imam) Musa bin Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who stands in prayer and does not know whether he has
prayed anything or not.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should start over."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
commentary:
And whoever forgets two rak‘ahs from the Night Prayer (‘Salat al-Layl’) and then
remembers them after having prayed the ‘Witr’, he must repeat both the two rak‘ahs
and the ‘Witr’. This was narrated:
references: Masa’il Ali Ibn Ja’far, Vol.1 p.252 • Qurb Al-Isnad, Vol.1 p.197 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.189 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.989 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.227 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.169

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ هِلالٍ عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ
اَللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ : عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى صَلاةَ اللَّيْلِ وَ أَوْتَرَ وَ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ نَسِيَ رَكْعَتَيْنٍ مِنْ صَلَاَتِهِ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ «يَقُومُ
فَيُصَلَّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ الَّتِي نَسِيَ مَكَانَهُ ثُمَّ يُوتِرُ».
ومن سها عن التشهد في النافلة حتى يدخل في الركعة الثالثة ثم ذكر بعد الركوع فليلق الركوع ويقعد ويتشهد ويسلم ،
وليس كذلك في الفريضة لان الفريضة إذا ذكر انه لم يتشهد وقد ركع مضى في صلاته ثم يتشهد بعد التسليم ويسجد
سجدتي السهو ، وقد بيناه فيما مضى والذي يدل على ما قلناه :
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Muhammad bin Abdillah bin Hilal,
from ‘Uqbah bin Khalid:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said regarding a man who prayed the Night Prayer
and performed the ‘Witr’, then remembered that he had forgotten two rak‘ahs from his
prayer, what should he do?
Imam {a.s} said: "He should stand and pray the two rak‘ahs that he forgot at that place,
then perform the ‘Witr’ again."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
And whoever forgets the tashahhud in a recommended prayer (‘nafilah’) and enters
into the third rak‘ah, then remembers after the ‘ruku’, he should leave the ‘ruku’, sit
down, recite the tashahhud, and give the ‘taslim’. This is not the case in obligatory
prayer (‘faridah’), because if one remembers after the ‘ruku’ that he did not recite the
tashahhud, he should continue with his prayer, then recite the tashahhud after the
‘taslim’ and perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’). We
have explained this previously. What supports what we have said is:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.189 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.963 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.230

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ
اللَّهِ الْحَلَبِيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ سَهَا فِي رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ ٱلنَّافِلَةِ فَلَمْ يَجْلِسْ بَيْنَهُمَا حَتَّى قَامَ فَرَكَعَ فِي الثَالِثَةِ قَالَ
«يَدَعُ رَكْعَةً وَ يَجْلِسُ وَ يَتَشَهْدُ وَ يُسَلَّمُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَأْنِفُ الصَّلاةَ» بَعْدُ.
english_text:
What was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from his father, from
Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydallah al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who, in a two-rak‘ah recommended prayer (‘nafilah’),
forgot and did not sit between the two rak‘ahs, and then stood and performed the
‘ruku’ in the third.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should abandon that rak‘ah, sit down, recite the ‘tashahhud’, and
give the ‘taslim’. Then he may begin a new prayer afterward."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.189 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.942 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.231 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 4 p.50

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودِ الْعَيَّاشِيُ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي حَمْدَوَيْهِ بْنُ نُصَيْرٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا أَيُوبُ بْنُ نُوحِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ
أَخْبَرَنَا اِبْنُ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ الصَّيْقَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ : فِي الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْوَثْرِ
يَقُومُ فَيَنْسَى التَّشَهْدَ حَتَّى يَرْكَعَ فَيَذْكُرُ وَ هُوَ رَاكِعْ قَالَ «يَجْلِسُ مِنْ رُكُوعِهِ فَيَتَشَهَدُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُتِمُ» قَالَ قُلْتُ أَ
لَيْسَ قُلْتَ فِي الْفَرِيضَةِ إِذَا ذَكَرَ بَعْدَ مَا يَرْكَعُ مَضَّى ثُمَّ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيْنِ بَعْدَ مَا يَنْصَرِفُ وَ يَتَشَهَدُ فِيهِمَا فَقَالَ
«لَيْسَ النَّافِلَةُ مِثْلَ الْفَرِيضَةِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ومن سها عن القراءة) الى قوله : (ومن قرأ سورة) .فقد مضى شرح جميع ذلك : ثم قال الشيخ
بحمهالله . لمصق اسمدة بمد الحمدثه احبل يقاغها فله ل يقطعمامياسماهاما له بحامنة قامتما نصفها
english_text:
Muhammad bin Mas‘ud al-‘Ayyashi said: Hamdawayh bin Nusair narrated to me, who said: Ayyub bin Nuh
narrated to us, from Abdillah bin al-Mughirah, who said: Ibn Maskan informed us, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who is praying the two
rak‘ahs of ‘Witr’, and he stands up and forgets the ‘tashahhud’ until he performs
‘ruku’, and then remembers while he is in ‘ruku’.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should sit from his ‘ruku’, recite the ‘tashahhud’, then stand and
complete (his prayer)."
He (narrator) said: “I asked (Imam {a.s}) ‘Did you not say concerning the obligatory
prayer, that if one remembers after performing ‘ruku’, he should continue and then
perform two prostrations (of forgetfulness) after completing the prayer, and recite the
‘tashahhud’ in them?’
Imam {a.s} said: "The ‘nafilah’ (recommended prayer) is not like the ‘faridah’ (obligatory
prayer)."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: ‘And whoever errs in the
recitation’ up to his statement: ‘And whoever recites a surah’, the explanation of all of
that has already passed.
Then the Shaykh, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: ‘And whoever recites a surah
after ‘al-Hamd’ and then wishes to recite another one, he may abandon it and recite a
different one, so long as he has not passed the halfway point of the surah. But if he
recites ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ or ‘Qul Ya Ayyuhal-Kafirun’, he is not permitted to turn
back from them.’
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.448 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.189 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.336 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.942 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.404

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنِ
اَلْحُسَيْنٍ بْنِ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ الرَّجُلُ يَقُومُ فِي الصَّلاَةِ فَيُرِيدُ
أَنْ يَقْرَأَ سُورَةً فَيَقْرَأ «قُل هُوَ اللهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ «قُلْ يا أَيْهَا الكَافِرُونَ» فَقَالَ «يَرْجِعُ مِنْ كُلَّ سُورَةٍ إِلاّ مِنْ «قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ
أَحَد» وَ «قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ» ».
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from al-Husayn bin Muhammad, from Abdillah bin ‘Amir, from Ali bin Mahziyar,
from Fadalah bin Ayyub, from al-Husayn bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Amr bin Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “A man stands in prayer and wants to
recite a surah, and he begins with ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ and ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’”.
Imam {a.s} said: "He may return (change to another surah) from any surah except ‘Qul
Huwa Allahu Ahad’ and ‘Qul Ya Ayyuhal-Kafirun’."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.317 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.190 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.290 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.673 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.99 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.95 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.5 p.794 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.5 p.687 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.1 4 p.472

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ قَرَأَ فِي الْغَدَاةِ
سُورَةً «قُلْ هُوَ اللهُ أَحَدٌ» قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ وَ مَنِ اِفْتَتَحَ بِسُورَةٍ ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ فِي سُورَةٍ غَيْرِهَا فَلاَ بَأْسَ إِلاّ «قُلْ
هُوَ اللَهُ أَحَدٌ» فَلاَ يَرْجِعُ مِنْهَا إِلَى غَيْرِهَا وَ كَذَلِكَ «قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ» ».
english_text:
Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Ibn Maskan, from al-Halabi, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “A man recites ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’ in the
Fajr prayer.”
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem. And whoever begins with a surah and then
decides to switch to another surah, there is no problem, except for ‘Surah Al-Ikhlas’,
from which he may not switch to another, and likewise ‘Surah Al-Kafirun’."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.190 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.673 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.99

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ الْحَلَبِيِّ وَ الْحُسَيْنِ
بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ عَنْ أَبِي الصِّبَّاحِ الْكِنَانِيِّ وَ أُحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنِ ٱلْمُثَنِّى الْحَنَّاطِ عَنْ أَبِي
بَصِيرٍ جَمِيعاً عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِي الرَّجُلِ يَقْرَأَ فِي ٱلْمَكْتُوبَةِ بِنِصْفِ السُورَةِ ثُمَّ يَنْسَى فَيَأْخُذُ فِي
أُخْرَى حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ مِنْهَا ثُمَّ يَذْكُرُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ قَالَ «يَرْكَعُ وَ لا يَضُرُّهُ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ومن سهى عن سجدة) الى قوله : (ومن تكلم) فقد مضى شرحه في الباب الذي قبل هذا الباب فلا
محه لاعادته
english_text:
Sa‘d, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Muhammad bin Abi Umayr, from Hammad bin ‘Uthman, from
‘Ubaydallah bin Ali al-Halabi; and al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Ali bin al-Nu‘man, from Abu al-Sabbah al-
Kinani; and Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Nasr, from al-Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Basir, all from Abu
Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} (said) regarding a man who, in an obligatory prayer (‘al-maktubah’),
begins reciting from the middle of a surah, then forgets and begins another surah until
he completes it, and then remembers before going into ‘ruku’.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should go into ‘ruku’, and it does not harm him."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: ‘And whoever forgets a
prostration’ up to his statement: ‘And whoever speaks’, its explanation has already
passed in the previous chapter, so there is no need to repeat it.
Then he, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: ‘Whoever speaks deliberately during
the prayer with something that is not permissible to say during the prayer must repeat
it. But whoever speaks out of forgetfulness should perform the two prostrations of
forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’) and is not required to repeat the prayer.’
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.190 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.923 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.101 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 2 p.43

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ ٱلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ
يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَتَكَلَّمُ نَاسِياً فِي الصَّلاَةِ يَقُولُ
أَقِيمُوا صُفُوفَكُمْ قَالَ «يُتِمُ صَلَاَتَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَيْنٍ» فَقُلْتُ سَجْدَتَي السَّهْوِ قَبْلَ التَّسْلِيمِ هُمَا أَوْ بَعْدَهُ قَالَ
«بَعْدَهُ».
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn and Muhammad bin Isma‘il, from al-Fadl bin
Shadhan, all from Safwan bin Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman bin al-Hajjaj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who speaks forgetfully
during the prayer and says, ‘Straighten your rows.’
Imam {a.s} said: "He should complete his prayer, then perform two prostrations
(sajdatay al-sahw)."
I asked: "Are the two prostrations of forgetfulness before the ‘taslim’ or after it?"
Imam {a.s} said: "After it."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.356 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.191 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.378 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.994 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.249

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ
أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ : فِي الرَّجْلِ يَسْهُو فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يَتَكَلَّمُ قَالَ «يُتِمُ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ
تَكَلَّمَ أَوْ لَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ وَ لا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ».
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Abu Ja‘far, from his father, and al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from
Muhammad bin Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar bin Udhaynah, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, (said) regarding a man who is forgetful in the first
two rak‘ahs and speaks.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should complete what remains of his prayer, whether he spoke or
did not speak, and there is nothing upon him."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.191 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.378 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.962 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.200 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.218

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ بُرَيْدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ : فِي رَجُلٍ
صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْمَكْتُوبَةِ فَسَلَّمَ وَ هُوَ يَرَى أَنْهُ قَدْ أَتَمَّ الصَّلاةَ وَ تَكَلَّمَ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أَنْهُ لَمْ يُصَلَ غَيْرَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ
«يُتِمّ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ».
فليس بمناف لما ذكرناه من وجوب سجدتي السهو عليه لانه ليس في هذين الخبرين انه ليس عليه سجدتا السهو وإنما
قال : وليس عليه شئ، ويجوز أن يكون اشار بذلك الى غير ذلك من الوزر والاثم وما يجري مجراهما.
english_text:
Al-Husayn bin Sa‘id, from Fadalah, from al-Qasim bin Burayd, from Muhammad bin Muslim:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, (said) regarding a man who prayed two rak‘ahs of
an obligatory prayer (‘al-maktubah’), then gave the ‘taslim’ thinking that he had
completed the prayer and spoke, then remembered that he had only prayed two
rak‘ah.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should complete what remains of his prayer, and there is nothing
upon him."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
commentary:
So this does not contradict what we have mentioned regarding the obligation of the
two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’) upon him, because there is
nothing in these two reports stating that he is not required to perform the two
prostrations of forgetfulness. Rather, the statement "there is nothing upon him" (‘wa
la shay’a ‘alayhi’) may be referring to other matters such as sin, blame, or the like, and
not a negation of the prostrations themselves.
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.191 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.379 • Nuzhat Al-Nazir, Vol.1 p.38 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.962 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.200 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.198

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدِ ٱلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ
مُصَدِّقٍ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى السَّابَاطِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ : فِي رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ التَّشَهُدَ فِي
الصَّلاةِ قَالَ «إِنْ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ بِسْمِ اللهِ فَقَطْ فَقَدْ جَازَتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَذْكُرْ شَيْئاً مِنَ التَّشَهُمِ أَعَادَ الصَّلاَةَ » وَ
الرَّجُلِ يَذْكُرُ بَعْدَ مَا قَامَ وَ تَكَلَّمَ وَ مَضَّى فِي حَوَائِجِهِ أَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنٍ فِي الظُهْرِ وَ الْعَصْرِ وَ الْعَتَمَةِ وَ الْمَغْرِبِ
قَالَ «يَبْنِي عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ فَيُتِمُّهَا وَ لَوْ بَلَغَ الصِّينَ وَ لاَ يُعيدُ الصَّلاَةَ».
فليس بمناف لما ذكرنا من ان من تكلم عامدا وجب عليه إعادة الصلاة ، لان من سها فسلم ثم تكلم بعد ذلك فلم يتعمد
الكلام وهو في الصلاة لانه إنما تكلم لظنه أنه قد فرغ من الصلاة فجرى مجرى من هو في الصلاة وتكلم لظنه انه ليس هو
في الصلاة، ولو أنه حين ذكر انه قد فاته شئ من هذه الصلوات ثم تكلم بعد ذلك عامدا لكان يجب عليه إعادة الصلاة
حسب ما قدمناه في المتكلم عامدا، ومن شك فلم يدر اثنتين صلى أم ثلاثا فان ذهب وهمه إلى واحد منهما بنى عليه ولا
شئ عليه، وان اعتدل وهمه بنى على الاكثر وأتم ما فاته إذا سلم ، وقد قدمنا ما يدل على ذلك ، ويزيده بيانا ما رواه :
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin al-Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal,
from ‘Amr bin Sa‘id al-Mada’ini, from Musaddiq bin Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar bin Musa al-Sabati:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} (was asked) regarding a man who forgot the ‘tashahhud’ in prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he remembers that he at least said ‘Bismillah’, then his prayer is
valid. But if he does not remember anything from ‘tashahhud’, he must repeat prayer."
And (Imam {a.s} was asked) regarding a man who remembers after having stood up,
spoken, and gone about his affairs, that he had only prayed two rak‘ahs in Dhuhr, ‘Asr,
Isha, or Maghrib.
Imam {a.s} said: "He builds upon his prayer and completes it, even if he had reached
China, and he does not need to repeat the prayer."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So this does not contradict what we have stated, that whoever speaks deliberately
during the prayer must repeat the prayer, because the one who forgets and gives the
‘taslim’, then speaks afterward, did not intentionally speak while still regarding
himself in a state of prayer. Rather, he spoke thinking he had completed the prayer,
and this is like the case of someone who speaks during prayer believing he is not in
prayer.
However, if he had remembered that something from his prayer was still remaining,
and then deliberately spoke after that, it would have been obligatory upon him to
repeat the prayer, as we have previously clarified regarding the one who deliberately
speaks.
As for the one who doubts and does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or three:
if his assumption leans toward one of them, then he should build upon it and nothing
is required of him. But if his assumption is balanced, he should build upon the greater
number and complete what he has missed after giving the ‘taslim’. We have already
mentioned what supports this, and what further clarifies it is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.192

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلْ لاَ يَدْرِي أَوَاحِدَةً صَلَّى أَمِ اِثْنَتَيْنِ قَالَ «يُعيدُ» قُلْتُ رَجُلٌ لَمْ يَدْرِ اِثْنَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ ثَلاثاً
قَالَ «إِنْ دَخَلَهُ الشَّكْ بَعْدَ دُخُولِهِ فِي الثَّالِثَةِ مَضَى فِي الثَّالِثَةِ ثُمَّ صَلِّى الْأُخْرَى وَ لا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ يُسَلَّمُ».
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from Hariz, from
Zurarah, from one of them (Imam {a.s}), peace be upon them both, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: “A man does not know whether he prayed one rak‘ah or two.”
Imam {a.s} said: "He should repeat (the prayer)."
I asked: “A man does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or three.”
Imam {a.s} said: "If the doubt enters after he has already begun the third rak‘ah, then he
should continue in the third, then pray the next rak‘ah (the fourth), and there is nothing
upon him, and he should give the taslim."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.192 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.375 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.173

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ
عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ لَمْ يَدْرٍ رَكْعَتَيْنِ صَلَّى أَمْ ثَلاَثاً قَالَ «يُعيدُ » قُلْتُ أَلَيْسَ يُقَالُ
لاَ يُعِيدُ الصَّلاةَ فَقِيهٌ فَقَالَ «إِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ فِي الثَّلاَثِ وَ الْأَرْبَعِ».
فمحمول على صلاة المغرب لان صلاة المغرب قد بينا انه متى شك الانسان فيها وجب عليه استيناف الصلاة، فاما ما
رواه:
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ja‘far,
from Hammad bin ‘Isa, from ‘Ubayd bin Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who does not know whether he prayed two rak‘ahs or
three.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must repeat (the prayer)."
I asked: “Is it not said that a jurist does not repeat the prayer?”
Imam {a.s} said: "That is only in the case of doubt between three and four (rak‘ahs)."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So this (narration) is to be understood as referring to the Maghrib prayer, because we
have already explained that whenever a person has doubt in the Maghrib prayer, it is
obligatory upon him to begin the prayer anew. As for what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.193 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.375 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.990 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.215 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.173

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَهْلٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ - عَنِ الرَّجُلِ لا يَدْرِي أَثَلاثاً صَلَّى
أَمِ اِثنَتَيْنِ قَالَ «يَبْنِي عَلَى النُّقْصَانِ وَ يَأْخُذُ بِالْجَزْمِ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ بَعْدَ إِنْصِرَافِهِ تَشَهُداً خَفِيفاً كَذَلِكَ فِي أَوْلِ الصَّلاَةِ
وَ آخِرِهَا».
فالوجه في هذا الخبر انه إنما يبني على النقصان إذا ذهب وهمه إليه ويصلي تمامه احتياطا، فاما مع اعتدال الوهم فالبناء
على لاكثر أحوط إذا تمم بعد الفراغ من الصلاة على ما بيناه، والذي يؤكد ما قلناه ما رواه:
english_text:
Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Muhammad bin Sahl, from his father, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who does not know
whether he prayed three rak‘ahs or two.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should build upon the lesser number and act according to what he
is certain of. After finishing his prayer, he should recite a light tashahhud. This is to be
done both at the beginning of the prayer and at its end."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
commentary:
The interpretation of this report is that he builds upon the lesser number when his
assumption inclines toward it, and he completes the prayer out of precaution. But in
the case where the assumption is balanced (no inclination toward either number),
then building upon the greater number is more cautious, provided he completes what
was possibly missed after finishing the prayer, as we have previously explained.
What reinforces what we have said is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.193 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.375 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.987 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.213

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ مُعَاذِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى السَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ
قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ: «كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْكَ مِنَ الشَّكَّ فِي صَلاَتِكَ فَاعْمَلْ عَلَى الأَكْثَرِ» قَالَ «فَإِذَا اِنْصَرَفْتَ
فَأَتِمَّ مَا ظَنَنْتَ أَنَّكَ نَقَصْتَ».
ومن تيقن انه زاد في الصلاة وجب عليه إعادة الصلاة، يدل على ذلك ما رواه:
english_text:
Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Muhammad bin Khalid, from al-Hasan bin Ali, from Mu‘adh bin Muslim, from
‘Ammar bin Musa al-Sabati, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Whenever doubt enters upon you in your
prayer, then act according to the greater number."
Imam {a.s} said: "Then, after you finish, complete what you think you may have left out."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
And whoever is certain that he has added something to the prayer, it is obligatory upon
him to repeat the prayer. What indicates this is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.193 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.376 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.985 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.213

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ بُكَيْرِ إِبْنَيْ أَعْيَنَ
عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا اِسْتَيْقَنَ الرَّجُلُ أَنَّهُ زَادَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ الْمَكْتُوبَةِ لَمْ يَعْتَدَّ بِهَا وَ اِسْتَقْبَلَ صَلَاَتَهُ
اِسْتِقْبَالاً إِذَا كَانَ قَدِ اِسْتَيْقَنَ يَقِينا».
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from ‘Umar bin Udhaynah,
from Zurarah and Bukayr, the sons of A‘yan:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If a man is certain that he has added
something to his obligatory prayer, then he should not count it (as valid), and he must
start his prayer over from the beginning, if he has attained definite certainty."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.348 • Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.354 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.194 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.376 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.94 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.964 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.319 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.231 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.201

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
عَلِي بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ : «مَنْ
زَادَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ فَعَلَيْهِ الْإِعَادَةُ».
english_text:
Ali bin Mahziyar, from Fadalah bin Ayyub, from Aban bin ‘Uthman, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever adds to his prayer, it is obligatory
upon him to repeat it."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.355 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.194 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.376 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.964 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.231

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ هِلالٍ عَنِ ٱلْعَلاءِ عَنْ
مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلِ اِسْتَيْقَنَ بَعْدَ مَا صَلْى الظُّهْرَ أَنَّهُ صَلّى خَمْساً قَالَ
«وَكَيْفَ اِسْتَيْقَنَ» قُلْتُ عَلِمَ قَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ عَلِمَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ جَلَسَ فِي الرَّابِعَةِ فَصَلَاَةُ ٱلظُهْرِ تَامَةٌ وَ لَيَقُمْ فَلْيُضِفُ إِلَى
اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْخَامِسَةِ رَكْعَةً وَ سَجْدَتَيْنِ فَيَكُونَانٍ رَكْعَتَيْنِ نَافِلَةً وَ لا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ».
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Muhammad bin Abdillah bin Hilal,
from al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad bin Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far {a.s} about a man who, after finishing the Dhuhr prayer, becomes
certain that he had prayed five rak‘ahs.
Imam {a.s} said: "And how did he become certain?"
I said: “He knows it (to be certain).”
Imam {a.s} said: "If he knows that he had sat in the fourth rak‘ah, then his Dhuhr prayer
is complete, and he should stand and add to the fifth rak‘ah another rak‘ah and two
prostrations, so they will become two (extra) rak‘ahs as ‘nafilah’ (recommended
prayer), and nothing is upon him."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.194 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.377 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.964 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.232 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.202

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ
صَلَّى خَمْساً فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ جَلَسَ فِي الرَّابِعَةِ قَدْرَ التَّشَهُمِ فَقَدْ تَمَّثْ صَلاَتُهُ».
فليس بمناف للخبر الاول لان من جلس في الرابعة ثم قام وصلى ركعة لم يخل بركن من اركان الصلاة، وإنما يكون أخل
بالتسليم، والاخلال بالتسليم لا يوجب إعادة الصلاة حسب ما قدمناه، ومتى شك في الرابعة والخامسة بنى على الرابعة
وسلم وسجد سجدتي السهو وهما المرغمتان
english_text:
Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil bin Darraj, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace
be upon him, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who prayed five rak‘ahs.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he sat in the fourth rak‘ah for the duration of the tashahhud, then his
prayer is complete."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
commentary:
