So this does not contradict the first report, because one who sat in the fourth rak‘ah
and then stood and prayed an additional rak‘ah has not invalidated any of the essential
pillars (‘arkan’) of the prayer. Rather, what he omitted was the ‘taslim’, and omitting
the ‘taslim’ does not necessitate repeating the prayer, as we have previously
explained.
And whenever one doubts whether he is in the fourth or the fifth rak‘ah, he should build
upon the fourth, give the ‘taslim’, and then perform the two prostrations of
forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’), which are known as ‘al-marghimatan’ (the two that
humiliate (Shaytan)).
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.194 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.377 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.94 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.964 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.232

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ
سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا كُنْتَ لا تَدْرِي أَرْبَعاً صَلَّيْتَ أَمْ خَمْساً فَاسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَي السَّهْوِ بَعْدَ
تَسْلِيمِكَ ثُمَّ سَلِّمْ بَعْدَهُمَا».
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : (وسجدتا السهو بعد التسليم يقول الانسان في سجوده).
قد بينا فيما تقدم ان سجدتي السهو موضعهما بعد التسليم ، ويؤكد ذلك ايضا ما رواه :
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub narrated from Ali bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Yunus bin Abd al-
Rahman, from Abdillah bin Sinan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you prayed four
or five rak‘ahs, then perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’)
after your ‘taslim’, then give the ‘taslim’ again after them."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: ‘The two prostrations of
forgetfulness are performed after the ‘taslim’, and a person says something during his
prostration.’
We have already explained previously that the proper place for the two prostrations of
forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’) is after the ‘taslim’, and this is further confirmed by
what was narrated:
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.355 • Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.355 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.195 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.106 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.988 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.207 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.224 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.224 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.206

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
سَغدّ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْخَطَابِ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
بْنِ مَيْمُونِ الْقَدَّاحِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ قَالَ: «سَجْدَنَا ٱلسَّهْوِ بَعْدَ التَّسْلِيمِ وَ قَبْلَ
اَلْكَلامِ».
english_text:
Sa‘d, from Musa bin al-Hasan, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn bin Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan bin Ali bin
Faddal, from Abdillah bin Maymun al-Qaddah, from (Imam) Ja‘far bin Muhammad {a.s}, from his father (Imam
al Baqir {a.s}):
(Imam) Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "The two prostrations of forgetfulness
(‘sajdata al-sahw’) are to be performed after the ‘taslim’ and before speaking."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib al-Murtadha {a.s}
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.341 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.195 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.380 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.994 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.208

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَأَمًا مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ الْبَرْقِيَ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدِ الْأَشعَرِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ :
«فِي سَجْدَتَي السَّهْوِ إِذَا نَقَصْتَ قَبْلَ التَّسْلِيمِ وَ إِذَا زِدْتَ فَبَعْدَهُ».
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from al-Barqi, from Sa‘d bin Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari,
who said:
(Imam) Al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "In the two prostrations of forgetfulness
(‘sajdatay al-sahw’), if there was a deficiency (in the prayer), then they are before the
‘taslim’; and if there was an addition, then they are after it."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.195

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ إِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي الْجَارُودِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ
عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلَاَمُ مَتَّى أَسْجُدُ سَجْدَتَي السَّهْوِ قَالَ «قَبْلَ التَّسْلِيمِ فَإِنَّكَ إِذَا سَلَّمْتَ بَعْدُ ذَهَبَثْ حُرْمَةُ صَلاَتِكَ».
فان هذين الخبرين محمولان على ضرب من التقية لانهما موافقان لمذاهب العامة ، وقال أبو جعفر محمد بن علي بن بابويه
رحمه اللّه : انا افتي بهما في حال التقية،
english_text:
And what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan,
from Abu al-Jarud, who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him: “When should I perform the two
prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’)?”
Imam {a.s} said: "Before the ‘taslim’, for if you give the ‘taslim’, the sanctity of your
prayer has ended."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
commentary:
For indeed, these two narrations are to be understood as being related to a form of
‘taqiyyah’ (dissimulation), because they are in agreement with the doctrines of the
common (Sunni) sects.
And Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Babawayh, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him,
said: "I issue legal verdicts (‘fatawa’) based on them in situations of ‘taqiyyah’."
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.195 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.380 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.995 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.208

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدِ ٱلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ مُصَدِّقٍ
بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى السَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَألْتُهُ عَنْ سَجْدَتَي السَّهْوِ هَلْ فِيهِمَا
تَكْبِيرٌ أَوْ تَسْبِيحْ فَقَالَ «لا إِنَّهُمَا سَجْدَنَانِ فَقَطْ فَإِنْ كَانَ الَّذِي سَهَا هُوَ ٱلْإِمَامَ كَبَّرَ إِذَا سَجَدَ وَ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ لِيُعِلِمَ
مَنْ خَلْفَهُ أَنَّهُ قَدْ سَهَا وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُسَبَّحَ فِيهِمَا وَ لا فِيهِمَا تَشَهُدٌ بَعْدَ السَّجْدَتَيْنِ».
فالمراد بهذا الخبر انه ليس فيهما تسبيح وتشهد كالتسبيح والتشهد في الصلوات من التطويل فيهما دون أن يكون المراد
به نفي التسبيح والتشهد على كل حال ، وعندنا ان المسنون أن يخفف الانسان في التشهد الذي بعد سجدتي السهو ويحمد
الله تعالى في السجود ويصلي على نبيه صلى اللّٰه عليه وآله بلا تطويل ، والذي يكشف عما ذكرناه :
english_text:
And as for what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Ahmad bin al-Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from ‘Amr
bin Sa‘id al-Mada’ini, from Musaddiq bin Sadaqah, from ‘Ammar bin Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}
(peace be upon him), who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the two prostrations of forgetfulness (‘sajdatay al-sahw’), is
there in them any ‘takbir’ (saying "Allahu Akbar") or ‘tasbih’ (glorification)?
Imam {a.s} said: "No, they are only two prostrations. But if the one who erred is the imam
(of prayer), then he says ‘takbir’ when he goes into prostration and when he raises his
head, in order to inform those behind him that he has made an error. He is not required
to say ‘tasbih’ in them, and there is no ‘tashahhud’ after the two prostrations."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So the meaning of this report is that there is no ‘tasbih’ and ‘tashahhud’ in them in the
same manner as in the regular prayers, meaning without lengthening them, rather than
the intention being to deny ‘tasbih’ and ‘tashahhud’ in every form or in all cases.
According to us, the recommended practice (‘sunnah’) is that a person performs a
light ‘tashahhud’ after the two prostrations of forgetfulness, and praises Allah {SWT}, the
Exalted, in the prostrations and sends blessings upon His Prophet {saws}, peace and
blessings be upon him and his family, but without elaboration or prolongation.
What clarifies what we have mentioned is:
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.341 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.196 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.381 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.106 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.995 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.235 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.221

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيّ
الْحَلَبِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِذَا لَمْ تَدْرِ أَرْبَعاً صَلَّيْتَ أَمْ خَمْساً أَمْ نَقَصْتَ أَمْ زِدْتَ فَتَشَهَّدْ وَ
سَلَّمْ وَ أُسْجُدْ سَجْدَتَيْنٍ بِغَيْرِ رُكُوعِ وَ لاَ قِرَاءَةٍ تَنَشَهَدُ فِيهِمَا تَشَهُداً خَفِيفاً».
فأما ما يستحب من الاقوال في هاتين السجدتين.
english_text:
What was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Abu Ja‘far, from Muhammad bin Abi Umayr, from Hammad
bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydallah bin Ali al-Halabi:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "If you do not know whether you have
prayed four rak‘ahs or five, or whether you have omitted or added something, then
perform the tashahhud, give the salam, and perform two prostrations (‘sajdatayn’)
without bowing (‘ruku’) or recitation, and in them recite a light tashahhud."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary: As for what is recommended from the sayings in these two prostrations.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.350 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.196 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.380 • Nuzhat Al-Nazir, Vol.1 p.40 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.105 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.988 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.224 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.234 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.206 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.226

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَمَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللّهِ
اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: فِي سَجْدَتَي السَّهوِ « بِسْمِ اللّهِ وَ بِاللهِ وَ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ
وَ عَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ» قَالَ وَ سَمِعْتُهُ مَرَّةً أَخْرَى يَقُولُ فِيهِمَا - « بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَ بِاللَّهِ وَ ٱلسَّلامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ وَ رَحْمَةُ
اللّه وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (من ترك صلاة من الخمس متعمدا أو ناسيا ولم يدر أيها هي صلى أربع ركعات وثلاثا وركعتين).
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d bin Abdillah, from Abi Ja‘far, from his father, from Muhammad bin Abi
Umayr, from Hammad bin ‘Uthman, from ‘Ubaydallah al-Halabi, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, say regarding the two prostrations of
forgetfulness: ‘In the name of Allah {SWT}, and by Allah {SWT}, and may Allah {SWT} send
blessings upon Muhammad {saws} and upon the family of Muhammad {saws}.’
He (narrator) said: “And I heard Him {a.s} on another occasion say in them:
‘In the Name of Allah {SWT}, and by Allah {SWT}, and peace be upon you, O Prophet {saws},
and the mercy of Allah {SWT} and His blessings.’
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: ‘Whoever deliberately or
forgetfully misses one of the five (daily) prayers and does not know which one it is, then
he should perform four rak‘ahs, and three, and two.’
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.342 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.196 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.234 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.8 5 p.220

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ الْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطِ عَنْ غَيْرٍ وَاجِدِ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي
عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: «مَنْ نَسِيَ صَلاةً مِنْ صَلاَةِ يَوْمِهِ وَاحِدَةً وَ لَمْ يَدْرِ أَيْ صَلاةِ هِيَ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ ثَلاَثاً
وَ أَرْبَعاً».
وَ رَوَى هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ :
english_text:
Ahmad bin Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from al-Hasan bin Ali al-Washsha’, from Ali bin Asbat, from more than one
of our companions:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, said: "Whoever forgets one of the prayers of his day and does not
know which prayer it is, he should perform two rak’ahs, three, and four."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary: And this hadith was also narrated by:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.197 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1009 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.275

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْخَطَابِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطِ عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي
عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ : مِثْلَهُ.
source: Implicit (Muzmar) Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn bin Abi al-Khattab, from Ali bin Asbat, from more than one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}:, the
commentary: same (narration).
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
الْعَيَّاشِي عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عَلِي بْنُ الْحَسَنِ وَ عَلِيْ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ
مُعَاوِيَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَامَ فِي الصَّلاةِ ٱلْمَكْثُوبَةِ فَسَهَا فَطَنَ أَنّْهَا نَافِلَةً أَوْ قَامَ فِي
النَّافِلَةِ فَظَنَّ أَنَّهَا مَكْتُوبَةٌ قَالَ «هِيَ عَلَى مَا اِفْتَتَحَ الصَّلاَةَ عَلَيْهِ».
english_text:
Al-‘Ayyashi, from Ja‘far bin Ahmad, said Ali bin al-Hasan and Ali bin Muhammad narrated to me, from
Muhammad bin ‘Isa, from Yunus, from Mu‘awiyah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who stood to pray an obligatory prayer (‘al-
maktubah’), then became confused and thought it was a recommended prayer
(‘nafilah’), or he stood to pray a ‘nafilah’ and thought it was an obligatory prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: “It is according to what he began the prayer with.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.197 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.343 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.911 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.6 p.6

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ نُصَيْرٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ : وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَمَّ قَوْما فِي الْعَصْرِ فَذَكَرَ وَ هُوَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنُ صَلَّى الْأُولَى قَالَ «فَلْيَجْعَلْهَا
الْأُولَى الَّتِي فَاتَثْهُ وَ اِسْتَأْنَفَ الْعَصْرَ وَ قَدْ قَضَى الْقَوْمُ صَلاَتَهُمْ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ومن فاتته صلوات كثيرة لم يحص عددها، ولا عرف أيها هي من الخمس صلوات على التعيين أو
د ف
كل مقت لالتضية لصلاة حاضة ٥كة
english_text:
And from him, from Muhammad bin Nusayr, who said: Muhammad bin Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi
Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}:
And I asked Him {a.s} about a man who led a group in prayer for ‘Asr, then remembered
while he was praying with them that he had not yet prayed Dhuhr.
Imam {a.s} said: “Then he should count it as the Dhuhr which he had missed, and begin
‘Asr anew. As for the people, they have completed their prayer."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: ‘Whoever has missed many
prayers and does not know their number, nor does he know which of the five prayers
they are specifically, or if he has missed all five for a period he cannot calculate, then
he should pray four rak‘ahs, three, and two during every time that is not restricted by
the obligation of a current prayer. And he should increase that until he overcomes the
assumption that he has made up what he missed and added to it.’
We have explained that when it is not specified which prayers he missed, he should
pray four, three, and two rak‘ahs in every time.
As for what indicates that it is obligatory to increase such prayers, it is that the making
up (‘qadahʾ’) of the obligatory prayers is indeed obligatory. And when their making up
is obligatory and he cannot be free of that responsibility except by doing more, then it
becomes obligatory upon him to increase them.
And to make this even clearer: the ‘nafilah’ (recommended) prayers, for which making
up is not obligatory, are still recommended to be made up. So if that is the case with
‘nafilah’, then the obligatory prayers are even more deserving of this.
What has been narrated regarding this is:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.197 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1013

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
محمد بن يعقوب عن علي بن ابراهيم عن أبيه عن عمرو ابن عثمان عن علي بن عبد الله عن عبد اللّٰه بن سنان
قال قلت : لابي عبد الله ومحمد بن أحمد بن يحيى عن أبى اسحاق عن عمرو بن عثمان عن ابراهيم بن عبد
الله ابن سام قال قلت لابي عبد الله رجل عليه من صلاة النوافل ما لا يدري ما هو من كثرته كيف يصنع؟ قال
فيصلي حتى لا يدري كم صلى من كثرته فيكون قد قضى بقدر ما عليه ، قلت فانه ترك ولا يقدر على القضاء
من شغله قال : ان كان شغله في طلب معيشة لا بد منها أو حاجة لاخ مؤمن فلا شئ عليه ، وان كان شغله
للدنيا وتشاغل بها عن الصلاة فعليه القضاء والالقي اللّٰه مستخفا متهاونا مضيعا لسنة رسول اللّٰه ص، قلت :
فانه لا يقدر على القضاء فهل يصلح أن يتصدق فسكت مليا ثم قال : نعم ليتصدق بصدقة ، قلت وما يتصدق؟
قال : بقدر قوته وأدنى ذلك مد فقال مد لكل مسكين مكان كل صلاة قلت : وكم الصلاة التي يجب فيها لكل
مسكين مد؟ فقال لكل ركعتين من صلاة الليل وكل ركعتين من صلاة النهار فقلت لا يقدر فقال : مد لكل أربع
ركعات فقلت لا يقدر فقال : مد لصلاة الليل ومد لصلاة النهار، والصلاة أفضل والصلاة أفضل والصلاة أفضل.
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from ‘Amr bin Uthman, from Ali bin Abdillah,
from Abdillah bin Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, and also from Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya,
from Abu Ishaq, from ‘Amr bin Uthman, from Ibrahim bin Abdillah bin Sam, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}: “A man has upon him such a great number of missed ‘nafilah’
prayers that he does not know what they are due to their amount, what should he do?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Then he should pray until he no longer knows how many he has prayed
because of their abundance, and that way he will have fulfilled what was upon him.”
I asked: “Suppose he left them and is not able to make them up due to being busy?”
Imam {a.s} said: “If he was busy (occupied) in the pursuit of livelihood that is necessary,
or a need of a believing brother, then there is nothing upon him.
But if he was busy (occupied) for worldly affairs and he occupied himself with them
instead of prayer, then he must make them up, otherwise he will meet Allah {SWT} having
shown negligence, disrespect, and disregard for Sunnah of Messenger of Allah {SWT}.”
I asked: “If he is unable to make them up, is it acceptable for him to give charity?”
He {a.s} was silent for a while, then said: “Yes, let him give charity.”
I asked: “And what amount of charity?”
Imam {a.s} said: “According to his ability, and the minimum is a ‘mudd’.”
Then Imam {a.s} said: “A ‘mudd’ for every poor person in place of each prayer.”
I asked: “And how many prayers would require a ‘mudd’ for each?”
Imam {a.s} said: “For every two rak’ahs of night prayer, and every two rak’ahs of daytime
prayer.”
I asked: “Suppose he is unable?”
Imam {a.s} said: “A ‘mudd’ for every four rak’ahs.”
I asked: “Suppose he is still unable?”
Imam {a.s} said: “A ‘mudd’ for the night prayer and a ‘mudd’ for the daytime prayer.
And the prayer is better, the prayer is better, the prayer is better.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
الي بن ابراهيم عن أبيه عن ابن أبي عمير عن مرازم قال سأل إسماعيل بن جابر أبا عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام : فقال
اصلحك الله ان علي نوافل كثيره فكيف اصنع؟ فقال : اقضها فقال له : انها اكثر من ذلك قال : اقضها قال لا
احصيها قال: توخ، قال مرازم وكنت مرضت أربعة اشهر لم اتنفل فيها فقلت أصلحك اللّٰه أو جعلت فداك إني
مرضت أربعة أشهر لم اصل فيها نافلة فقال : ليس عليك قضاء إن المريض ليس كالصحيح كلما غلب اللّٰه عليه
فالله أولى بالعذر فيه،
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : (ومن التفت في صلاة فريضة حتى يرى من خلفه وجب عليه إعادة الصلاة).
english_text:
Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Marazim, who said:
Isma‘il bin Jabir asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, saying:
"May Allah {SWT} set you right, I have many missed ‘nafilah’ prayers, what should I do?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Make them up (as qadha)."
I asked: "They are more than that (too many)."
Imam {a.s} said: "Make them up."
I said: "I cannot count them."
Imam {a.s} said: "Approximate (estimate)."
Marazim said: I was ill for four months and did not perform ‘nafilah’ prayers during that
time, so I asked (Imam {a.s}: "May Allah {SWT} set you right or may I be your ransom, I was
ill for four months and did not perform any ‘nafilah’ prayers during that time."
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no ‘qadha’ upon you. The sick is not like the healthy. Whatever
overcomes one by Allah’s {SWT} will, then Allah {SWT} is more entitled to excuse him in it."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: ‘Whoever turns his head in an
obligatory prayer to the extent that he sees what is behind him, it becomes obligatory
upon him to repeat the prayer.’ This is supported by:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ يَقُولُ:
«اَلالْتِفَاتُ يَقْطَعُ الصَّلاَةَ إِذَا كَانَ بِكُلَّهِ».
english_text:
What was narrated by al-Husayn bin Sa’id, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from ‘Umar bin Udhayna, from Zurarah,
who said:
He (Zurarah) heard Abu Ja’far {a.s} say: ‘"Turning (the head) invalidates the prayer when
it is with the whole (of the body)."‘
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.199

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَعَنْهُ عَنْ صَفَوَانَ عَنِ ٱلْعَلاءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السُلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ هَلْ يَلْتَفِتُ الرَّجُلُ فِي
صَلاتِهِ فَقَالَ «لا وَ لا يَنْقُضُ أَصَابِعَهُ».
english_text:
And from him, from Safwan, from al-’Alaʾ, from Muhammad bin Muslim, from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s}: "May a man turn his head during his prayer?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No, and he should not crack his fingers either."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.366 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.199 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.405 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.876 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.7 p.244 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.7 p.264

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:
«إِذَا اِسْتَقْبَلْتَ الْقِبْلَةَ بِوَجْهِكَ فَلاَ تَقْلِبْ وَجْهَكَ عَنِ الْقِبْلَةِ فَتَفْسُدَ صَلاَتُكَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى قَالَ لِنَبِيَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ
فِي الْفَرِيضَةِ «فَوَلَ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَ حَيْثُ مَا كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ» وَ اِخْشَعْ بَصَرَكَ وَ لا
تَرْفَعَهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَ لَكِنْ جِذَاءَ وَجْهِكَ فِي مَوْضِعِ سُجُودِكَ».
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ya‘qub, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah:
Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “When you face the qiblah with your face, do
not turn your face away from the qiblah, lest your prayer become invalid.
For indeed, Allah {SWT} the Exalted said to His Prophet {saws}, peace be upon him,
regarding the obligatory prayer: ‘So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque, and
wherever you are, turn your faces toward it’ (Surah Baqarah 2:144 & 2:150).
And lower your gaze, and do not raise it to the sky, but rather let it be aligned with your
face at the place of your prostration."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.300 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.199 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.286 • Al- Istibsar, Vol.1 p.405 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.539 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol.1 p.346

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ ٱلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصِيبُهُ الرُّعَافُ وَ هُوَ فِي الصَّلاةِ فَقَالَ «إِنْ قَدَرَ عَلَى مَاءِ عِنْدَهُ يَمِيناً أَوْ شِمَالاً بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَ هُوَ
مُسْتَقْبِلُ الْقِبْلَةِ فَلْيَغْسِلْهُ عَنْهُ ثُمَّ لْيُصَلِّ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى مَاءٍ حَتَّى يَنْصَرِفَ بِوَجْهِهِ أَوْ يَتَكَلَّمَ
فَقَدْ قَطَعَ صَلاَتَهُ».
english_text:
And from him, from Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi,
from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who experiences nosebleed (‘ru’af’) while in prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he is able to find water near him, whether to his right, left, or in front
of him, while still facing the qiblah, then let him wash it off and continue with the
remainder of his prayer. But if he is not able to find water without turning his face away
or speaking, then his prayer is invalidated."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.364 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.200 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.404 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.869 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.7 p.239

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَأَمًا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ
عَنْ عَبْدِ ٱلْمَلِكِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنِ الإِلْتِفَاتِ فِي الصَّلاةِ أَيَقْطَعُ الصَّلاةَ فَقَالَ «لا وَ مَا أُحِبُّ
أن يُفْعَلَ».
فالمراد بهذا الخبر هو انه إذا لم يلتفت الى ورائه وإنما يلتفت يمينا وشمالا فان ذلك لا يقطع الصلاة وإن كان منقصا لها ،
فأما إذا كان الالتفات بالكلية فانه يقطع الصلاة حسب ما قدمناه. قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ومن ظن انه على طهارة فصلى
ثم علم بعد ذلك انه على غن طمارة تطم وأعاد الصلاة، وكذلك من صل. ف ثوب وظ. انه طاهر ثم عرف بعد ذلك انه
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Sa’d bin Abdillah, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ja’far bin Bashir, from
Hammad bin Uthman, from Abd al-Hamid, from Abd al-Malik, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about turning the head in prayer, does it invalidate the prayer?
Imam {a.s} said: "No, but I do not like it to be done."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So the meaning of this narration is that if one does not turn entirely behind but only
turns slightly to the right or to the left, then this does not invalidate the prayer, even
though it detracts from it. As for when the turning is complete, then it does invalidate
the prayer, as we have previously explained.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: ‘Whoever assumes that he is
in a state of purity and prays, then later realizes that he was not in a state of purity, he
must perform purification and repeat the prayer. Likewise, whoever prays in a garment
thinking it is pure, and then finds out afterward that it was impure, and he was
negligent in checking it beforehand, must repeat the prayer.’
We have already explained and clarified this in the chapter on purification, and it is
also confirmed by what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.200 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.405 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.875 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.7 p.245

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي الصَّبَّاحِ الْكِنَانِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ
تَوَضًّا فَنَسِيَ أَنْ يَمْسَحَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ حَتَّى قَامَ فِي الصَّلاةِ قَالَ «فَلْيَنْصَرِف فَلْيَمْسَخْ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَ لَيُعِدِ الصَّلاةَ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn bin Sa’id, from Muhammad bin al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about a man who performed ablution but forgot to wipe over
his head until he had already stood for prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: ‘"Then he should leave (the prayer), wipe over his head, and repeat the
prayer."‘
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.200 • Al-Wafi, Vol.6 p.349 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.1 p.370

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةً عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «مَنْ نَسِيَ مَسْحَ رَأْسِهِ أَوْ قَدَمَيْهِ أَوْ شَيْئاً مِنَ
اَلْوُضُوءِ الَّذِي ذَكَرَهُ اللهُ تَعَالَى فِي الْقُرْآنِ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ إِعَادَةُ ٱلْوُضُوءِ وَ الصَّلاةِ».
english_text:
And from him, from Uthman, from Sama’ah:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: ‘"Whoever forgets to wipe his head or his feet, or forgets any part
of the ablution that Allah {SWT} the Exalted has mentioned in the Qur’an, then it is
obligatory upon him to repeat the ablution and the prayer."‘
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.1 p.102 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.200 • Al-Wafi, Vol.6 p.351 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.1 p.370 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.1 p.451

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ إِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ : فِي رَجُلٍ نَسِيَ أَنْ يَمْسَحَ
عَلَى رَأْسِهِ فَذَكَرَ وَ هُوَ فِي الصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ قَدِ اِسْتَيْقَنَ ذَلِكَ اِنْصَرَفَ وَ مَسَحَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَ عَلَى رِجْلَيْهِ وَ
اِسْتَقْبَلَ الصَّلَةَ وَ إِنْ شَكَّ وَ لَمْ يَذْرِ مَسَحَ أَوْ لَمْ يَمْسَحْ فَلْيَتَنَاوَلْ مِنْ لِحْيَتِهِ إِنْ كَانَتْ مُبْتَلَّةً وَ ليَمْسَحْ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ
وَ إنْ كَانَ أَمَامَهُ مَاءً فَلْيَتَنَاوَلْ مِنْهُ فَلْيَمْسَخ بِهِ رَأْسَهُ».
english_text:
And from him, from Muhammad bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} (was asked) regarding a man who forgot to wipe over his head and
remembered while he was in prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he is certain of that, then he should leave the prayer, wipe over his
head and his feet, and then start the prayer anew. But if he is uncertain and does not
know whether he wiped or not, then let him take from his beard if it is moist and wipe
with it over his head; and if there is water in front of him, let him take from it and wipe
his head with it."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.201 • Al-Wafi, Vol.6 p.350 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.1 p.471

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ إِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ قَالَ: «مَنْ نَسِيَ مَسْحَ رَأْسِهِ
ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَمْسَحْ رَأْسَهُ فَإِنْ كَانَ فِي لِحْيَتِهِ بَلَلْ فَلْيَأْخُذْ مِنْهُ وَ لَيَمْسَخْ رَأْسَهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِي لِحْيَتِهِ بَلَلْ
فَلْيَنْصَرِفْ وَ لَيُعِدِ الْوُضُوءَ».
english_text:
And from him, from Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Malik bin A’yan:
Abu Abdillah {a.s} said: "Whoever forgets to wipe his head, then remembers that he did
not wipe his head, if there is moisture in his beard, then let him take from it and wipe
his head. But if there is no moisture in his beard, then he should leave (his prayer) and
repeat the ablution."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.201 • Al-Wafi, Vol.6 p.350 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.1 p.409

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَخْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ
بْنِ مُوسَى قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ يَقُولُ: «لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلاً نَسِيَ أَنْ يَسْتَنْجِيَ مِنَ الْغَائِطِ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَّ لَمْ
يُعدٍ الصَّلاَةَ».
فمحمول على من لم يستنج بالماء وإن كان قد استنجى بالاحجار أو لم يستنج بالاحجار وان كان قد استنجى بالماء، فاما
متى ذكر انه لم يستنج اصلا وجب عليه اعادة الصلاة، والذي يدل على ذلك ما رواه:
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Ja’far
bin Bashir, from Hammad bin Uthman, from ‘Ammar bin Musa, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s} say: "If a man were to forget to perform istinjaʾ (cleansing) after
defecation until he prayed, he does not have to repeat the prayer."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So this is to be understood as referring to the one who did not perform ‘istinjaʾ’ with
water but had performed it with stones, or did not perform it with stones but had
performed it with water. However, if he remembers that he did not perform ‘istinjaʾ’ at
all, then it becomes obligatory upon him to repeat the prayer.
What indicates this is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.1 p.49 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.201 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.54 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.4 p.46 • Al-Wafi, Vol.6 p.158 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.1 p.318

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ الْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السِّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ
عَنْ رَجُلٍ ذَكَرَ وَ هُوَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَسْتَنْجِ مِنَ ٱلْخَلاَءِ قَالَ «يَنْصَرِفُ وَ لَيَسْتَنْجِ مِنَ ٱلْخَلاَءِ وَ يُعيدُ الصَّلاَةَ».
وقد استوفينا ما يتعلق بهذا الباب في كتاب الطهارة وفيه غنى هناك إن شاء الله.
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya from al-’Amraki from Ali bin Ja’far from his brother (Imam) Musa bin Ja’far
{a.s}, peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who remembered, while he was in his prayer, that he had
not performed ‘istinjaʾ’ after relieving himself.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should leave, perform ‘istinja’ after relieving himself, and repeat
the prayer."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
commentary:
And we have fully covered what pertains to this chapter in the Book of Purification, and
in it there is sufficient detail, Allah {SWT} willing.
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.201 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.1 p.315

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ سَيْفٍ عَنْ
مَيْمُونِ الصَّيْقَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلَ أَصَابَثَهُ جَنَابَةٌ بِاللّيْلِ فَاغْتَسَلَ فَلَمَا أَصْبَحَ نَظَرَ
فَإِذَا فِي ثَوْبِهِ جَنَابَةٌ فَقَالَ » الْحَمْدُ لِلّهِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَدَغْ شَيْئا إِلاَّ وَ لَهُ حَدُّ إنْ كَانَ جِينَ قَامَ إِلَى الصَّلاَةِ نَظَرَ فَلَمْ يَرَ
شَيْئاً فَلاَ إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ حِينَ قَامَ فَلَمْ يَنْظُرْ فَعَلَيْهِ الْإِعَادَةُ».
english_text:
Muhammad bin Ya’qub, from Muhammad bin Yahya, from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abdillah, from Abdillah bin
Jabalah, from Sayf, from Maymun al-Sayqal, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I said to Him {a.s}: “A man experienced janabah (ritual impurity) during the night, so he
performed ghusl, and in the morning he looked and saw janabah (impurity) on his
clothing.”
Imam {a.s} said: "Praise be to Allah {SWT}, who has not left anything without assigning a
rule for it. If, when he stood for prayer, he looked and did not see anything, then there
is no repetition (of prayer) required of him. But if, when he stood, he did not look, then
he must repeat the prayer."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.406 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.202 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.182 • Al-Wafi, Vol.6 p.163 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.3 p.478

Chapter Title: RULINGS ON FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER AND WHAT REQUIRES REPEATING OF PRAYER
arabic_text:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ الصُّفَّارُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ حَفْصِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ
اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى وَ فِي ثَوْبِهِ بَوْلٌ أَوْ جَنَابَةٌ فَقَالَ «عَلِمَ بِهِ أَوْ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ فَعَلَيْهِ إِعَادَةُ
الصَّلاَةٍ إِذَا عَلِمَ».
قوله عليه السلام علم به أو لم يعلم يريد به في حال قيامه الى الصلاة بعد أن يكون قد تقدمه العلم بحصول النجاسة في
الثوب ولم يعلم في حال قيامه الى الصلاة لسهو عرض أو نسيان ، ولو لم يتقدمه علم اصلا بحصول النجاسة قبل ذلك لما
وجب عليه إعادة الصلاة على كل حال بدلالة الخبر الاول وإلا تناقضت الاخبار. قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : (ومن صلى في ثوب
بفصول امف مكا مفصول له تحنه ممحب عليه اعلية الصلاة بنا عل ذلكما لاخلاف فه صنانه منه عن٠ الصلاة
١١ - باب ما يجوز الصلاة فيه من اللباس والمكان وما لا يجوز الصلاة فيه من ذلك
english_text:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad bin al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad bin al-Husayn, from Wahb
bin Hafs, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a man who prayed while there was urine or janabah (impurity)
on his garment.
Imam {a.s} said: "Whether he knew of it or not, if he comes to know of it, then he must
repeat the prayer."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM THAT
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
His statement, peace be upon him, “whether he knew of it or not,” refers to the state
when he stands for prayer after he had previously known of the impurity being present
on the garment but did not remember it at the time of standing for prayer due to an
occurrence of forgetfulness or oversight.
However, if there had been no prior knowledge at all of the impurity before that time,
then repeating the prayer would not be obligatory in any case, based on the indication
of the first narration, otherwise, the narrations would be contradictory.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: ‘Whoever prays in a usurped
garment or in a usurped place, his prayer is not valid and he must repeat the prayer.’
This is supported by what is agreed upon, that one is forbidden from praying in either
of the two (a usurped garment or place), and the prohibition indicates the invalidity of
the prohibited action, as has been explained in other places. Also, there is no
disagreement that prayer requires the intention of nearness (to Allah {SWT}), and this
prayer is considered blameworthy without any dispute, and seeking nearness through
blameworthy acts is not valid in any situation.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible to pray
in the skins of a dead animal, even if it is from that which, had it not died [a natural
death], it would have been valid for slaughter (could have been ritually slaughtered)."
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.202 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.182 • Al-Wafi, Vol.6 p.164 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.3 p.476

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING
arabic_text:
أحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ : فِي الْمَيْتَةِ قَالَ
«لاَ تُصَلًّ فِي شَيْءِ مِنْهُ وَ لاَ شِسْعٍ».
english_text:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from more than one person:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, (said) regarding the carcass (maytah).
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in anything from it, not even a sandal strap."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.203 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.415 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.343 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.377

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ الْجِلْدِ الْمَيَّتِ أَيُلْبَسُ فِي
الصَلاَةٍ إِذَا دُبِغَ فَقَالَ «لا وَ لَوْ دُبِغَ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the skin of a dead animal, can it be worn in prayer if it has been
tanned?
Imam {a.s} said: "No, even if it is tanned seventy times."
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.203 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.415 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.343

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING
arabic_text: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ ٱلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ : مِثْلَهُ.
english_text:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Al-‘Ala’, from Muhammad: the same (narration).
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ إسْحَاقَ ٱلْعَلَوِيّ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ
اَلدَّيْلَمِيّ عَنْ عَيْثَمِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ النَّجَاشِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي الْفِرَاءِ
فَقَالَ «كَانَ عَلِي بْنُ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا ٱلسَلاَمُ رَجْلاً صَرِداً فَلاَ تُذْفِئُهُ فِرَاءُ ٱلْحِجَازِ لِأَنَ دِبَاغَهَا بِالْقَرَظِ فَكَانَ يَبْعَثُ
إِلَى الْعِرَاقِ فَيُوتَى مِمَّا قِبَلَكُمْ بِالْفَرْوِ فَيَلْبَسُهُ فَإِذَا حَضَرَتِ الصِّلاةُ أَلْقَاهُ وَ أَلْقَى الْقَمِيصَ الَّذِي يَلِيهِ فَكَانَ يُسْأَلُ
عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَيَقُولُ «إِنَّ أَهْلَ الْعِرَاقِ يَسْتَجِلُونَ لِبَاسَ الْجُلُودِ الْمَيْتَةِ وَ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّ دِبَاغَهُ ذَكَاتُهُ» ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-‘Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali,
from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from ‘Aytham ibn Aslam al-Najashi, from Abu Basir who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about praying in fur garments.
Imam {a.s} said: "(Imam) Ali ibn al-Husayn {a.s} was a man sensitive to cold, and the furs
of the Hijaz would not keep him warm because their tanning was done with qaraz (a
plant extract). So He {a.s} would send to Iraq and He {a.s} would be brought fur from your
region, and He {a.s} would wear it. But when the time for prayer arrived, He {a.s} would
take it off, and also take off the shirt that was in contact with it.
He {a.s} was asked about that, and He (Imam Husayn {a.s}) said: 'Indeed, the people of
Iraq deem it permissible to wear the skins of dead animals, and they claim that tanning
it is its purification (that tanning makes it lawful).’"
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Imam Ali ibn Husayn Zayn al-Abidin {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.203

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنْ لِبَاسِ
الْفِرَاء وَ الصِّلاةٍ فِيهَا فَقَالَ «لا تُصَلَّ فِيهَا إلاَّ فِيمَا كَانَ مِنْهُ ذَكِيّا» قَالَ قُلْتُ أَوَ لَيْسَ الذَّكِيْ مَا ذُكِّيَ بِالْحَدِيدِ فَقَالَ
«بَلَى إِذَا كَانَ مِمَّا يُوكَلُ لَحْمُهُ» فَقُلْتُ وَ مَا لا يُؤكَلُ لَحْمُهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ ٱلْغَنَمِ قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِالسِّنْجَابِ فَإِنَّهُ دَابَّةٌ لا تَأْكُلُ
اللَّحْمَ وَ لَيْسَ هُوَ مِمَّا نَهَى عَنْهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ إِذْ نَهَى عَنْ كُلِّ ذِي نَابٍ أَوْ مِخْلَبٍ».
english_text:
With this same chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s} about wearing fur garments and praying in them.
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in them except in what has been ritually slaughtered."
I asked: "Isn’t dhakiyy what is slaughtered with iron (a blade)?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, if it is from that which its meat is eaten."
So I asked: "What about what is not eaten from animals other than sheep?"
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem with (wearing) squirrel (al-sinjab), for it is a
creature that does not eat meat, and it is not from those things which the Messenger
of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, prohibited when He {saws} prohibited all
animals with fangs or talons."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
source: Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.397 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.203 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.402 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.348

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ إسْحَاقَ ٱلْعَلَوِيّ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ
عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَجَاجِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ إِنِّي أَدْخَلُ سُوقَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ أَغْنِي هَذَا الْخَلْقَ
آلَّذِي يَدَّعُونَ الْإِسْلَامَ فَأَشتَرِي مِنْهُمُ الْفِرَاءَ لِلتَّجَارَةِ فَأَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهَا أَلَيْسَ هِيَ ذَكِيَّةً فَيَقُولُ بَلَى فَهَلْ يَصْلُحُ لِي
أَنْ أَبِيعَهَا عَلَى أَنَّهَا ذَكِيَّةٌ فَقَالَ «لا وَ لَكِنْ لا بَأْسَ أَنْ تَبِيعَهَا وَ تَقُولَ قَدْ شَرَطَ آلَّذِي اِشتَرَيْتُهَا مِنْهُ أَنَّهَا ذَكِيَّةٌ)» قُلْتْ
وَ مَا أَفْسَدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ «اِسْتِخْلاَلُ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ لِلْمَيْتَةِ وَ زَعَمُوا أَنْ دِبَاغَ جِلْدِ ٱلْمَيْتَةِ ذَكَاتُهُ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْضَوْا أَنْ يَكْذِبُوا
فِي ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ ».
english_text:
And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from
Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: "I enter the market of the Muslims, I
mean this group who ‘claim’ Islam, and I buy fur garments from them for trade.
So I say to the seller: 'Is it not from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah)?'
And he (seller) replies: 'Yes.'
So is it permissible for me to sell it on the basis that it is dhakiyyah?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No. But there is no harm in selling them if you say: ‘The one I bought
them from claimed they were from a slaughtered animal.’”
I asked: “What invalidates that? (makes it impermissible to sell as definitely pure)”
Imam {a.s} said: "The people of Iraq making carrion (maytah) lawful, and they claimed
that the tanning of the skin of carrion renders it ritually pure (as its slaughter). Then
they were not content with lying about that except by attributing it to the Messenger of
Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.398 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.204 • Al-Wafi, Vol.1 7 p.285 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.3 p.503

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ غَيْرِهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ
قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ ٱلْمَيْتَةُ يُنْتَفَعُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْهَا قَالَ «لا» قُلْتُ بَلَغَنَا أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ
صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ مَرَّ بِشَاةٍ مَيْتَةٍ فَقَالَ «مَا كَانَ عَلَى أَهلِ هَذِهِ الشَّاةِ إِذْ لَمْ يَنْتَفِعُوا بِلَحْمِهَا أَنْ يَنْتَفِعُوا بِإِهَابِهَا»
فَقَالَ «تِلْكَ شَاةٌ لِسَوْدَةَ بِنتِ زَمْعَةَ زَوْجِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ كَانَتْ شَاةَ مَهْزُولَةً لاَ يُنْتَفَعُ بِلَحْمِهَا فَتَرَكُوهَا
حَتَّى مَاتَتْ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ «مَا كَانَ عَلَى أَهْلِهَا إِذْ لَمْ يَنْتَفِعُوا بِلَحْمِهَا أَنْ يَنْتَفِعُوا بإِهَابِهَا أَيْ
تُذَكّى» ».
english_text:
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from
Asim ibn Humaid, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: "May I be ransomed for you, can anything
from a dead animal (maytah) be benefitted from?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
I asked: "It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah {SWT} (peace be upon him and his
family) passed by a dead sheep and said: 'What would have been upon the people of
this sheep if they could not benefit from its meat, to at least benefit from its hide?'"
Imam {a.s} said: "That was a sheep belonging to Sawdah bint Zam‘ah, the wife of the
Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and it was an emaciated sheep whose
meat was of no benefit, so they left it until it died.
Then the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, said: 'What would
have been upon its people, if they could not benefit from its meat, to benefit from its
hide, that is, by making it ritually slaughtered (tudhakka)'."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.398 • Al-Kafi, Vol.6 p.259 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.204 • Al-Wafi, Vol.1 9 p.101 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.3 p.502 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.2 4 p.184 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.154 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.2 p.220

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text: سَغدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَغْفَرٍ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثِمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ
english_text:
Sa‘d narrated from Abu Ja‘far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa, from Sama’ah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about wearing a sword in prayer when it
contains fur or ‘kaymukht’ (a type of soft leather).
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no problem with it as long as it is not known to be from a dead
animal."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "It is not permissible to pray
in the skins of other impure animals, such as the dog, the pig, the fox, the rabbit, and
anything similar to that, and (their skins) are not purified by tanning."
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.205

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَعْدِ بْنِ ٱلْأَحْوَصِ
قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ - عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي جُلُودِ السِّبَاعِ فَقَالَ «لا تُصَلَ فِيهَا» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْثُهُ هَلْ
يُصَلِّي الرَّجُلُ فِي ثَوْبِ إِبْرِيسَمِ قَالَ «لا».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn
Khalid, from Isma‘il ibn Sa‘d ibn al-Ahwas, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, about praying in the skins of
wild beasts.
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in them."
He (narrator) said: “And I asked Him {a.s}: ‘Can a man pray in a garment made of silk?’"
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.400 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.205

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةً قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ لُحُومِ السِّبَاعِ وَ جُلُودِهَا فَقَالَ «أَمَّا لُحُومُ
السَّبَاعِ مِنَ الطَّيْرِ وَ الدَّوَابِ فَإِنَّا نَكْرَهُهُ وَ أَمَّا اَلْجُلُودُ فَارْكَبُوا عَلَيْهَا وَ لا تَلْبَسُوا مِنْهَا شَيْئاً تُصَلُونَ فِيهِ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from al-Hasan, from Zur‘ah, from Sama‘ah, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about the meat of wild beasts and their skins.
Imam {a.s} said: "As for the meat of wild beasts, from birds and animals, we dislike it.
And as for the skins, ride upon them, but do not wear anything from them in which you
pray."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.205 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.9 p.79 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, Vol.1 p.118 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.62 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.412 • Al-Wafi, Vol.1 9 p.63 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.353 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.2 4 p.114 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.80 p.229 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.3 p.200

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
وَعَثَهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلَامُ - عَنْ جُلُودِ التَّعَالِبِ
أَيْصَلَّى فِيهَا فَقَالَ «مَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ فِيهَا».
english_text:
And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the skins of foxes, can one pray in
them?
Imam {a.s} said: "I do not like to pray in them."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.205 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.381 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.406 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.355

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي جُلُودِ الْأَرَانِبِ فَكَتَبَ «مَكْرُوهَةٌ».
english_text:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who said:
I wrote to Him {a.s} asking about prayer in the skins of rabbits.
Imam {a.s} wrote in reply: "It is makrooh (disliked)."
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.205 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.381 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.75 • Al- Wafi, Vol.7 p.405 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.356 • Awalim Al-Uloom, Vol.2 3 p.333 • Awalim Al-Uloom, Vol.2 3 p.386

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ بُنَانِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ الْأَبْهَرِيَّ قَالَ:
كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ عِنْدَنَا جَوَارِبُ وَ تِكَكْ تُعْمَلُ مِنْ وَبَرِ الْأَرَانِبِ فَهَلْ تَجُوزُ الصَّلاَةُ فِي وَبَرِ الْأَرَانِبِ مِنْ غَيْرٍ
ضَرُورَةٍ وَ لاَ تَقِيَّةٍ فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «لا تَجُوزُ الصَّلاَةُ فِيهَا».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Bunan ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn
Ishaq al-Abhari, who said:
I wrote to Him {a.s}: "May I be ransomed for you, we have socks and padding that are
made from rabbit fur. Is it permissible to pray in rabbit fur without necessity or
taqiyyah?"
Imam {a.s} wrote in reply, peace be upon him: "Prayer in it is not permissible."
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.399 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.206 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.206 • Al- Istibsar, Vol.1 p.383 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.383 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.405 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.356 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.356 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.377 • Awalim Al-Uloom, Vol.2 3 p.314

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
علي بن مهزيار قال : كتب إليه ابراهيم بن عقبة عندنا جوارب وتكك تعمل من وبر الارانب فهل تجوز الصلاة
في وبر الارانب من غير ضرورة ولا تقية؟ فكتب عليه السلام : لا تجوز الصلاة فيها.
english_text:
Ali ibn Mahziyar said Ibrahim ibn Uqbah wrote to Imam {a.s}: "We have socks and
padding that are made from rabbit fur. Is it permissible to pray in rabbit fur without
necessity or taqiyyah?"
Imam {a.s}, peace be upon him, wrote in reply: "Prayer in it is not permissible."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي زَيْدِ قَالَ: سُئِلَ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - عَنْ جُلُودِ التَّعَالِبِ
الذَّكِيَّة قَالَ «لا تُصَلِّ فِيهَا».
english_text:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Zayd, who said:
(Imam) Al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, was asked about the tanned skins of foxes.
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in them."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.206 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.210 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.381 • Al- Wafi, Vol.7 p.406 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.357

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ : سَأَلَ الرَّضَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ - عَنِ
الصَّلاةٍ فِي جُلُودِ التَّعَالِبِ فَنَهَى عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فِيهَا وَ فِي الَّذِي يَلِيهِ فَلَمْ أَدْرِ أَيّ الثَوْبَيْنِ الْذِي يَلْصَقُ بِالْوَبَرِ أَوِ الَّذِي
يَلْصَقُ بِالْجِلْدٍ فَوَقَعَ عَلَيْهِ السْلاَمُ بِخَطَّهِ «ٱلَّذِي يَلْصَقُ بِالْجِلْدِ» وَ ذَكَرَ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ سُيْلَ عَنْ هَذِهِ
الْمَسْألَةٍ فَقَالَ «لا تُصَلَّ فِي آلَّذِي فَوْقَهُ وَ لاَ فِي الَّذِي تَحْتَهُ)».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from a man:
He asked (Imam) Al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, about prayer in the skins of foxes.
He {a.s} forbade praying in them and in what is next to them.
But I (narrator) did not know which of the two garments He {a.s} meant, was it the one
that is in contact with the fur or the one that is in contact with the skin?
So Imam {a.s}, peace be upon him, wrote in his own handwriting:
"The one that is in contact with the skin."
And Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him, mentioned that He {a.s} was asked about this
matter, and Imam {a.s} said:
"Do not pray in what is above it, nor in what is beneath it."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.206 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.381

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصّلاَةِ فِي
جُلُودِ اَلتَّعَالِبِ فَقَالَ «إِذَا كَانَتْ ذَكِيَّةً فَلاَ بَأْسَ».
فيحتمل أن يكون أراد أنه لا بأس به إذا كان على مثل القلنسوة أو ما اشبهها مما لا يتم الصلاة بها ، والذي يكشف عما
ذكرناه ما رواه :
english_text:
And as for what was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about prayer in the skins of foxes.
Imam {a.s} said: "If they are from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah), then there
is no problem."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
It is possible that what he meant is that there is no problem if it is on something like a
cap or something similar, which one does not complete the prayer with. And what
clarifies what we have mentioned is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.206 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.382 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.74 • Al- Wafi, Vol.7 p.408 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.357

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلْهُ هَلْ يُصَلَّى فِي
قَلَنْسُوَةٍ عَلَيْهَا وَبَرُ مَا لا يُوْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ أَوْ تِكَّةِ حَرِيرٍ أَوْ تِكَّةٍ مِنْ وَبَرِ الْأَرَانِبِ فَكَتَبَ «لاَ تَحِلُّ الصَّلاَةُ فِي الْحَرِيرِ
اَلْمَخْضٍ وَ إِنْ كَانَ الْوَبَرُ ذَكِيّاً حَلَّتِ الصَّلاَةُ فِيهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ».
ويجوز ايضا أن يكون المراد بفي في الخبر على فكأنه عليه السلام قال : لا بأس بالوقوف عليه في حال الصلاة وقد بينا
ما يقتضي تحريم الصلاة فيها من الروايات ما فيها كفاية ان شاء اللّٰه تعالى، ويؤكد ايضا ذلك ما رواه:
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, who said:
I wrote to Abu Muhammad {a.s}, peace be upon him, asking: "Is it permissible to pray in
a cap that has upon it the fur of an animal whose meat is not permissible to eat, or in
a waistband of silk, or in a waistband made from rabbit fur?"
Imam {a.s} wrote: "Prayer is not permissible in pure silk. And if the fur is from a properly
slaughtered animal (dhakiyyah), then prayer in it is permissible, Allah {SWT} willing."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
source: Abu Muhammad Imam Hasan ibn Ali al-Askari {a.s}
commentary:
And it is also possible that what is meant by "fi" in the narration is "on", as if He {a.s},
peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem with standing upon it during prayer."
And we have already explained, from the narrations, what indicates the prohibition of
prayer in it, and that is sufficient, Allah {SWT} willing. This is also further confirmed by
what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.207 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.383 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.75 • Al- Wafi, Vol.7 p.406 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.377

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمّدٍ عَنِ الْوَلِيدِ بْنِ أَبَانِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أُصَلِّي فِي الْفَنَكِ وَ السِّنْجَابِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ» فَقُلْتُ
يُصَلَّى فِي التَّعَالِبِ إِذَا كَانَتْ ذَكِيَّةً قَالَ «لا تُصَلِّ فِيهَا)».
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : (ولا تجوز الصلاة للرجال في الابريسم المحض مع الاختيار ولا لبسه إلا مع الاضطرار).
english_text:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Walid ibn Aban, who said:
I said to (Imam) Al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him: "May I pray in the fur of the fennec
and the squirrel?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."
So I asked: "Is it permissible to pray in fox skins if they are from a properly slaughtered
animal (dhakiyyah)?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in them."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "And it is not permissible for
men to pray in pure silk (ibrisim) when there is choice, nor to wear it except in cases of
necessity."
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.207 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.382 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.406

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلْهُ
هَلْ يُصَلَّى فِي قَلَنْسُوَةِ حَرِيرٍ مَحْضٍ أَوْ قَلَنْسُوَةِ دِيبَاجٍ فَكَتَبَ «لا تَجِلُ الصَّلاَةُ فِي حَرِيرٍ مَحْضٍ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, who said:
I wrote to Abu Muhammad {a.s}, peace be upon him, asking Him {a.s}:
"Is it permissible to pray in a cap made of pure silk or a cap made of brocade (dibaj)?"
Imam {a.s} wrote in reply: "Prayer is not permissible in pure silk."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
source: Abu Muhammad Imam Hasan ibn Ali al-Askari {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.399 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.207 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.385 • Awali Al- La’ali, Vol.3 p.75 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.423 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.368 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.376

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ سَعْدِ الْأَشعَرِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الثَّوْبِ الإبْرِيسَمِ هَلْ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ الرِّجَالُ
قَالَ «لا».
والحديث الذي قدمناه من رواية محمد بن أحمد بن أحمد بن يحيى عن محمد بن عبد الجبار يدل على ما قلناه ايضا.
english_text:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Isma‘il ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ari, who said:
I asked Him {a.s} about a garment made of silk, can men pray in it?
He said: "No."
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
commentary:
And the narration that we presented earlier from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya,
from Muhammad ibn Abdul-Jabbar, also indicates what we have said.
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.207 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.385 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.424

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ أَسْبَاطِ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَارِثِ
قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ هَلْ يُصَلِّي الرَجُلُ فِي ثَوْبِ إِبْرِيسَمِ قَالَ «لا».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid, from a group of our companions, from Ali
ibn Asbat, from Abu al-Harith, who said:
I asked (Imam) Al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him: "Can a man pray in a garment made
of silk?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.208 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.386 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.369

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلَاَمُ - عَنِ
الصَّلاة فِي ثَوْبِ دِيبَاجِ فَقَالَ «مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ اَلتَّمَاثِيلُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ».
فاول ما في هذا الخبر انا قد روينا عن الرضا عليه السلام ما ينافي هذا الخبر، ولا يجوز ان تختلف اقواله عليه السلام، ثم
ليس في ظاهر هذا الخبر انه لا بأس بالصلاة فيه في أي حال ، وإذا لم يكن هذا في ظاهره خصصناه بحال الحرب دون
حال الاختيار والذي يدل على ذلك ما رواه:
english_text:
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
As for what was narrated by Sa‘d, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘, who
said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him ,about prayer in a garment of brocade
(dibaj), and he said: "As long as it does not have images (tamathil), then there is no
problem."
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
commentary:
The first issue with this report is that we have already narrated from (Imam) Al-Ridha
{a.s}, peace be upon him, that which contradicts this narration, and it is not permissible
for His {a.s}, peace be upon him, statements to be in contradiction. Moreover, the
apparent wording of this narration does not indicate that there is no problem praying
in it under all circumstances. And since this is not apparent in its wording, we restrict
its meaning to the condition of war, not to a situation of choice. What indicates this is
what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.208 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.386 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.425 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.370

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
سَعَدْ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - عَنْ لِبَاسِ الْحَرِيرِ وَ الدِّيبَاجِ
فَقَالَ «أمًا فِي الْحَرْبِ فَلاَ بَأْسَ وَ إِنْ كَانَ فِيهِ تَمَاثِيلُ».
ويحتمل ايضا أن يكون أراد عليه السلام إذا كان الديباج سداه ولحمته غزلا أو كتانا دون أن يكون مبهما لانه متى كان الامر
على ذلك جازت الصلاة فيه وليس في الخبر انه ديباج ليس فيه شئ من الغزل ولا من الكتان بل هو يحتمل لما ذكرناه،
والذي يدل على ما قلناه ما رواه:
english_text:
Sa‘d, from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from Sama‘ah ibn Mihran, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about wearing silk and brocade.
Imam {a.s} said: "As for during war, there is no problem, even if it contains images
(tamathil)."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
And it is also possible that what He, peace be upon him, intended was that if the
brocade (dibaj) had its warp and weft made of spun thread or linen, rather than being
entirely pure silk, then, in that case, prayer in it would be permissible. The narration
does not state that the brocade mentioned contained nothing of spun thread or linen,
so it remains open to the interpretation we have mentioned. What supports what we
have said is what was narrated:
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.6 p.453 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.208 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.386 • Al-Wafi, Vol.2 0 p.727 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.372

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنْ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يُوسُفَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لا بَأْسَ
بِالثَّوْبِ أَنْ يَكُونَ سَدَاهُ وَ زِرُّهُ وَ عَلَمُهُ حَرِيراً وَ إِنَّمَا كُرِهَ الْحَدِيرُ الْبُهْمُ لِلرِّجَالِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : (ولا يصلى في الفنك والسمور ولا تجوز الصلاة في أوبار ما لا يؤكل لحمه).
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yusuf ibn Ibrahim:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: "There is no problem with a garment whose
warp, buttons, and embroidery are of silk. What is disliked for men is pure silk (al-harir
al-buhm)."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} support him, said: "And one does not pray in
garments made of fennec or sable, and it is not permissible to pray in the furs of
animals whose meat is not lawful to eat."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.264 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.208 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.386 • Al-Wafi, Vol.2 0 p.726 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.375 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.80 p.240

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَ زُرَارَةُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَاَمُ - عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي التَّعَالِبِ وَ الْفَنَكِ وَ السِّنْجَابِ وَ غَيْرِهِ مِنَ الْوَبَرِ فَأْخِرَجَ كِتَاباً زَعَمَ أَنَّهُ إِمْلاءُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ
صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ «أنَّ الصَّلاةَ فِي وَبَرِ كُلّ شَيْءٍ حَرَامٍ أكْلُهُ فَالصَّلاَةُ فِي وَبَرِهِ وَ شَعْرِهِ وَ جِلْدِهِ وَ بَوْلِهِ وَ رَوْتِهِ
وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ فَاسِدَةٌ لا تُقْبَلُ تِلْكَ الصَّلاةُ حَتّى يُصَلِّيَ فِي غَيْرِهِ مِمَّا أَحَلَ اللَّهُ أَكْلَهُ» ثُمَّ قَالَ «يَا زُرَارَةُ هَذَا عَنْ
رَسُولِ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ اللّهِ فَاحْفَظُ ذَلِكَ يَا زُرَارَةُ فَإِنْ كَانَ مِمَّا يُوكَلُ لَحْمُهُ فَالصَّلاَةُ فِي وَبَرِهِ وَ بَوْلِهِ
وَشَعْرِهِ وَ رَوْتِهِ وَ أَلْبَانِهِ وَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ جَائِزَةٌ إِذَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّهُ ذَكِيْ قَدْ ذَكَاهُ الذَّبْحُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ مِمّا قَدْ
نَهِيتَ عَنْ أَكْلِهِ أَوْ حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكَ أَكْلُهُ فَالصَّلاَةُ فِي كُلَ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ فَاسِدَةٌ ذَكَاهُ الذِّبْحُ أَوْ لَمْ يُذَكَهِ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:
Zurarah asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about prayer in the skins of foxes,
fennec, squirrels, and other types of fur.
So He {a.s} took out a book, which He {a.s} claimed was dictated by the Messenger of Allah
{SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, (and it said):
"Indeed, prayer in the fur of every animal whose meat is forbidden to eat, then prayer
in its fur, hair, skin, urine, feces, and everything from it, is invalid. That prayer is not
accepted until one prays in something other than it, from that which Allah {SWT} has
permitted its meat to be eaten."
Then Imam {a.s} said: "O Zurarah, this is from the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon
him and his family, by Allah {SWT}.
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
So preserve it, O Zurarah. For if it is from that whose meat is permissible to eat, then
prayer in its fur, urine, hair, feces, milk, and everything from it is permissible, if you
know that it is from a properly slaughtered animal (dhakiyy), slaughtered by the proper
method. But if it is other than that, from what you have been prohibited from eating or
what is forbidden for you to eat, then prayer in anything from it is invalid, whether it
was ritually slaughtered or not."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.397 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.209 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.383 • Awali Al- La’ali, Vol.3 p.74 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.401 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.345

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ إبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ الْهَمَذَانِيِّ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ
يَسْقُطُ عَلَى تَوْبِيَ الْوَبَرُ وَ الشَّعْرُ مِمَّا لا يُوْكَلُ لَحَمُهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ تَقِيَّةٍ وَ لا ضَرُورَةِ فَكَتَبَ «لا تَجُوزُ الصَّلاَةُ فِيهِ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-
Hamadhani, who said:
I wrote to Him {a.s}: "Fur and hair from animals whose meat is not lawful to eat fall onto
my garment, without any taqiyyah or necessity, what is the ruling?"
He {a.s} wrote in reply: "Prayer in it is not permissible."
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.209 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.384 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.403 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.346 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.381 • Awalim Al-Uloom, Vol.2 3 p.315 • Awalim Al-Uloom, Vol.2 3 p.384

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَيُوبَ بْنِ نُوحِ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ ٱلْوَشَاءِ قَالَ: كَانَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱَلسَّلامُ يَكْرَهُ الصْلاَةَ
فِي وَبَرٍ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ لاَ يُوْكَلُ لَحَمُهُ.
english_text:
And from him, from a man, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha’, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, used to dislike prayer in the fur of anything whose
meat is not lawful to eat.
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: ‘Ilal Al-Shara’i’, Vol.2 p.342 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.209 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.403 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.346 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.381 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.80 p.221

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ إسْحَاقَ عَمَّنْ ذَكَرَهُ عَنْ مُقَاتِلِ بْنِ مُقَاتِلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ
اللّه عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فِي السَّمُورِ وَ السِّنْجَابِ وَ التَّعَالِبِ فَقَالَ «لا خَيْرَ فِي ذَا كُلَّهِ مَا خَلاَ السِّنْجَابَ فَإِنَّهُ
دَابَّةٌ لا تَأْكُلُ اللَّحْمَ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq, from someone who mentioned
it, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about prayer in garments made from
sable, squirrel, and fox.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no good in any of that, except for the squirrel, for it is a creature
that does not eat meat."
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.210

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
عَلِيْ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيَّ بْنِ رَاشِدِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي الْفِرَاءِ أَيّ شَيْءٍ يُصَلّى
فِيهِ قَالَ «أيُّ ٱلْفِرَاءِ» قُلْتُ الْفَنَكَ وَ السِّنْجَابَ وَ السَّمُورَ قَالَ «فَصَلٌ فِي الْفَنَكِ وَ ٱلسِّنْجَابِ فَأمَا السَّمُورُ فَلاَ تُصَلَّ
فيهِ» قُلْتُ فَالتَعَالِبُ يُصَلّى فِيهَا قَالَ «لا وَ لَكِنْ تُلْبَسُ بَعْدَ الصَّلاَةِ» قُلْتُ أُصَلِّي فِي الثَّوْبِ الَّذِي يَلِيهِ قَالَ «لا)».
english_text:
Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, who said:
I said to Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, peace be upon him: "What do you say about fur garments, can
one pray in them?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Which fur garments?"
I said: "The fennec, the squirrel, and the sable."
Imam {a.s} said: "Then pray in the fennec and the squirrel. As for the sable, do not pray
in it."
I said: "Can one pray in fox furs?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No, but they may be worn after the prayer."
I said: "Can I pray in the garment that touches it (worn underneath it)?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
PRAY IN, FROM THAT
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Jawad {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.400 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.210 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.384 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.403 • Awalim Al-Uloom, Vol.2 3 p.386

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ الصِّرْمِيّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي بَشِيرُ بْنُ بَشَارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ
الصَّلاَةِ فِي الْفَنَكِ وَ ٱلْفِرَاءِ وَ السَّنْجَابِ وَ السَّمُورِ وَ الْحَوَاصِلِ الَتِي تُصَادُ بِبِلاَدِ الشَّرْكِ أَوْ بِلادِ ٱلْإِسْلامِ أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ
فِيهِ لِغَيْرِ تَقِيَّةٍ قَالَ فَقَالَ «صَلِّ فِي السِّنْجَابِ وَ ٱلْحَوَاصِلِ الْخُوارَزْمِيَّةِ وَ لاَ تُصَلَّ فِي التَعَالِبِ وَ لا السِّمُّورِ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said Bashir ibn
Bashshar narrated to me, saying:
I asked Him {a.s} about prayer in garments made from fennec, fur, squirrel, sable, and
decorative collars (hawasil) that are hunted in the lands of polytheism or the lands of
Islam, whether I may pray in them when not under taqiyyah.
Imam {a.s} said: "Pray in the squirrel and the Khwarazmian collars, and do not pray in
foxes or sable."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Muhammad al-Hadi {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.210 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.384 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.406 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.348

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
أحمد بن محمد عن جعفر بن محمد بن أبي زيد قال : سئل الرضا عليه السلام عن جلود الثعالب الذكية قال : لا
تصل فيها،
english_text:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Zayd, who said:
(Imam) Al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, was asked about the tanned skins of foxes.
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in them."
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2

Chapter Title: WHAT IS PERMISSIBLE TO PRAY IN, FROM CLOTHING AND PLACE, AND WHAT IS NOT PERMISSIBLE TO
arabic_text:
فَأَمّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ ٱلْعَبَّاسِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيَّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَألْتُهُ عَنِ الْفِرَاءِ وَ السَّمُورِ وَ السِّنْجَابِ وَ التَعَالِبِ وَ أَشبَاهِهِ قَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِيهِ».
english_text:
